amd-92605.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: AMD is looking for AI Networking Systems Software Engineer to drive the design, development and bring-up of networking software for GPU scale-up interconnects and Ethernet-based AI fabrics. You will be a senior technical contributor in a core team of industry specialists, working with the latest GPU, NIC, switch and rack-scale technology. In this role, you will lead the design, development, optimization and bring-up of networking software across the driver, firmware and systems software layers for AMD Helios rack-scale deployments, with a primary focus on Ethernet-based scale-up GPU interconnect and scale-out networking. You will work across silicon, hardware, firmware, driver, switch software and architecture teams to deliver high-performance, low-latency and resilient networking for next-generation AI infrastructure. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a senior software engineer with deep experience across networking, switches and GPU interconnects, who can own complex technical areas end to end and drive difficult cross-team issues to resolution. You communicate clearly with architecture, hardware, firmware and software teams, and provide technical direction and mentorship to other engineers. You have hands-on experience spanning device drivers, embedded firmware and systems software, and are comfortable debugging problems that cross silicon, firmware, driver, switch and workload boundaries. You work well in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and are motivated by end-to-end system challenges in rack-scale AI platforms. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: • Lead the design and development of networking software for GPU scale-up interconnect and Ethernet-based AI fabrics on AMD Helios rack-scale systems • Develop and optimize Linux kernel drivers, embedded firmware and user-space software for GPU interconnect, NIC and switch subsystems • Drive hardware and software bring-up of new ASICs and platforms, including SerDes and link initialization, Ethernet MAC/PCS/FEC configuration, topology discovery and validation • Work with switch software teams on switch configuration, forwarding, QoS, telemetry and fabric management for scale-up and scale-out topologies • Define firmware, driver and management interfaces and control-plane protocols between GPUs, switches and fabric management software • Analyze end-to-end network performance, latency, bandwidth utilization, congestion behavior and communication efficiency across multi-node and rack-scale deployments • Develop tools, diagnostics and telemetry frameworks to monitor link and fabric health, identify bottlenecks and accelerate root cause analysis • Investigate and resolve issues across the stack, including GPU interconnect, NICs, switches, transport layers, firmware, drivers, collective communication libraries and distributed runtimes • Contribute to resiliency, RAS, serviceability and deployment readiness features for large-scale clusters • Support performance characterization of collective operations and distributed training and inference workloads over scale-up and scale-out fabrics • Partner with internal and external teams, including switch and platform vendors, to validate interoperability and optimize AI workload performance on AMD platforms • Help define software requirements and influence future GPU, interconnect, switch and system architecture • Provide technical leadership through design and code reviews, and mentor engineers across the team PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: • Years of experience in networking, systems software, driver or firmware development • Strong C/C++ programming skills with a keen attention to code quality; Python or Go for tooling is a plus • Linux kernel driver development experience, including PCIe devices, DMA, interrupts and memory management • Embedded firmware development experience on microcontrollers or SoC management processors, including RTOS or bare-metal environments • Strong knowledge of Ethernet (MAC, PCS, FEC, SerDes, link training and auto-negotiation) and high-speed link bring-up • Experience with GPU interconnect or scale-up fabric technologies such as UALink, Infinity Fabric/xGMI, NVLink or Ethernet-based scale-up • Strong Ethernet networking experience, including L2 switching and bridging, VLANs, MAC learning, LLDP, link aggregation, L3 forwarding, and QoS (PFC, ETS, ECN, buffer and queue management) • Experience with datacenter switch software such as SONiC, SAI or switch ASIC SDKs • Experience with network protocols and transports such as RDMA, RoCE, InfiniBand, TCP/IP or related high-performance transport technologies • Familiarity with scale-up and scale-out architectures in AI or large distributed computing environments • Experience debugging complex multi-node system issues involving hardware, firmware, drivers, switches and application workloads • Experience with performance analysis, profiling, tracing and observability tools used for system and network performance tuning • Experience with ASIC, GPU, NIC or switch bring-up is highly desirable • Knowledge of reliability, availability and serviceability considerations in rack-scale or datacenter deployments is a plus • Experience with software development processes and tools such as debuggers and source code control • Effective communication and problem-solving skills, with a proven ability to lead technical work across architecture, hardware, firmware, software and validation teams ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent LOCATION: Santa Clara, CA This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. #LI-NP1 Benefits offered are described: AMD benefits at a glance. AMD does not accept unsolicited resumes from headhunters, recruitment agencies, or fee-based recruitment services. amd-89589.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology can change lives for the better. It can heal us, entertain us, and make us more connected, productive, and understanding of the world around us. And we’re looking for talent who feel the same: people who want to leave the planet better than they found it, those who don’t shy away from humanity’s challenges but are determined to help solve them. AMD is powering the next generation of supercomputing, high-performance computing, cloud, and AI. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or creating go-to-market plans, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. THE ROLE: We are seeking a highly motivated and technically exceptional PMTS AI/ML Compiler Engineer to join AMD's AI Software organization. In this role, you will drive compiler and performance optimizations that enable state-of-the-art AI training and inference workloads on AMD GPU platforms. You will work at the intersection of compiler technology, machine learning frameworks, GPU architecture, and performance engineering, contributing to the ROCm software ecosystem and ONNX Runtime execution stack. The ideal candidate combines deep compiler expertise with hands-on experience optimizing AI workloads, and thrives in a fast-paced environment collaborating across architecture, kernel, runtime, and framework teams. THE PERSON: You are passionate about building high-performance AI software and solving complex optimization challenges. You possess strong compiler fundamentals, GPU programming expertise, and a proven ability to improve performance for large-scale AI models. You enjoy collaborating with architecture, compiler, runtime, and machine learning teams to deliver innovative solutions that scale across current and future AMD GPU platforms. You have a strong sense of ownership, excellent problem-solving skills, and a track record of driving meaningful performance improvements across software stacks. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Work with AMD’s architecture specialists to improve future products Design, develop, and optimize compiler transformations and operator lowerings within MLIR, LLVM, and the ROCm software stack. Develop scalable solutions that improve portability and performance across AMD GPU architectures. Collaborate with compiler and runtime teams to develop advanced optimization strategies for AI workloads. Implement, validate, and maintain ONNX operators and microbenchmark test suites. Lead performance optimization efforts for AI training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning (RL), and inference workloads on AMD GPUs. Design and implement graph-level, kernel-level, and runtime-level optimizations that deliver measurable performance gains. Analyze workload execution characteristics and identify opportunities for improvements in compute efficiency, memory utilization, and communication overhead. Drive performance characterization and benchmarking across pre-silicon and post-silicon environments. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Strong proficiency in C++ and object-oriented software development. Hands-on experience with GPU programming technologies such as HIP, CUDA, Triton, or equivalent parallel programming frameworks. Experience with compiler technologies including MLIR, LLVM, or related compiler infrastructures. Strong understanding of machine learning frameworks, model execution pipelines, and AI workload optimization. Experience profiling and optimizing performance-critical software systems. Proficiency with Linux development environments, source control systems (Git), debugging tools, and performance profilers. Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent LOCATION: San Jose, California #LI-JG1 Benefits offered are described: AMD benefits at a glance. amd-81089.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE You will join the system software architecture team behind AMD Instinct™ accelerators, the GPUs powering some of the world's largest AI and HPC deployments. This role is focused on next-generation, rack-scale AI platforms in the MI400 class spanning the GPU, the node, and the scale-up/scale-out fabric that binds thousands of accelerators into a single training and inference system. THE PERSON As a Systems Software Architect, you sit at the intersection of silicon, firmware, driver, runtime, and framework. You define how the software stack exposes and orchestrates the hardware so that AMD's largest customers can extract maximum performance, reliability, and utilization from their infrastructure. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Own the end-to-end system software architecture for one or more MI400-class subsystems for example GPU memory management, scheduling and queuing, RAS and serviceability, virtualization/partitioning (SR-IOV), or the scale-up/scale-out interconnect software model. Drive architecture across the stack: kernel-mode driver (amdgpu/KFD), user-mode runtime (ROCr/HSA), firmware interfaces, and the ROCm software platform, ensuring the layers compose cleanly and perform. Partner with silicon and SoC architects during pre-silicon definition to shape hardware/software interfaces, programming models, and register/firmware contracts before tape-out. Define the software strategy for multi-GPU and rack-scale topologies, including Infinity Fabric / UALink-style interconnect, collective communication (RCCL), memory coherence, and address translation across the platform. Establish architecture for reliability, availability, and serviceability at scale, error detection, containment, telemetry, recovery, and graceful degradation across large clusters. Set direction on performance: identify bottlenecks in the launch path, memory subsystem, and communication path, and define the software mechanisms to close them. Produce architecture specifications, reference designs, and design reviews that align firmware, driver, runtime, and framework teams onto a shared plan. Act as a technical anchor across AMD and with strategic hyperscale and AI customers — translating their workload requirements into architectural direction and representing AMD in deep technical engagements. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE Linux Memory Management and Heterogeneous Memory Management (HMM). GPU / DRM driver development. Cache coherence and memory consistency protocols. GPU Networking technologies including including scale up transport, NVLink, UALink, RDMA, and peer-direct. Scale-up and scale-out networking, and communication collectives (e.g., RCCL/NCCL), MPI, or SHMEM. Data-center fabrics such as Infinity Fabric, UALink, Ultra Ethernet, InfiniBand, and RoCE, with topology-aware software. DESIRABLE EXPERIENCE Direct experience with the ROCm stack, AMD Instinct, CUDA, or comparable GPU compute ecosystems. Hands-on experience developing or optimizing GPU compute kernels (HIP, CUDA, Triton, or assembly-level tuning). Experience with deep learning frameworks like PyTorch and TensorFlow in particular including framework integration, custom operators, and performance tuning on GPU backends. Familiarity with the broader ML framework and compiler ecosystem (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, ONNX, MLIR/compiler stacks). Hands-on experience with GPU compute technologies such as OpenCL and Vulkan. Familiarity with AI/ML training and inference workloads (transformers, large-scale distributed training, KV-cache and memory pressure, inference serving). Background in virtualization, multi-tenancy, confidential computing, or cloud GPU provisioning. Contributions to open-source kernel, driver, or runtime projects. amd-92004.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE AMD's Datacenter Performance Group is seeking a GPU Performance Software Engineer to drive performance analysis, SW/HW co-design, and architecture evaluation for next-generation GPU-based AI systems. In this role, you will work at the intersection of software, architecture, and performance engineering, analyzing AI workloads and system behavior to identify performance opportunities and influence future GPU designs. Working closely with architecture, runtime, driver, firmware, and AI software teams, you will evaluate new architectural concepts, prototype emerging hardware features, and guide optimization efforts across the GPU software stack. The position is primarily focused on pre-silicon architecture evaluation and SW/HW co-design for next-generation AI inference systems, with opportunities to validate performance and investigate bottlenecks on emerging hardware platforms. THE PERSON The ideal candidate combines strong software engineering skills with a solid understanding of computer architecture and performance analysis. You enjoy investigating complex performance problems, understanding interactions across large software stacks, and using data to influence future hardware and software designs. You are comfortable working across multiple layers of the GPU software stack and can effectively communicate technical findings to both software and hardware teams. Experience with AMD, NVIDIA, or other GPU architectures is strongly preferred. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Analyze AI workloads on current and future GPU-based systems to identify performance bottlenecks and optimization opportunities across the software stack. Collaborate with architecture teams to evaluate, prototype, and influence next-generation GPU features through data-driven performance analysis and SW/HW co-design. Develop performance studies, benchmarks, and software prototypes to assess architectural tradeoffs and estimate the impact of future hardware capabilities. Investigate system-level performance across single-GPU, multi-GPU, and rack-scale environments, including communication, synchronization, memory, and workload distribution effects. Participate in pre-silicon architecture evaluation and post-silicon performance validation, driving improvements across hardware and software teams. The ideal candidate completes well-defined tasks with guidance, learns quickly, and collaborates effectively within a high-performing team. Run Benchmarks & Experiments: Run performance experiments across AMD GPU generations and network configurations, and summarize results for the team. GPU Programming & Architecture: Foundational knowledge of GPU architecture; experience with HIP, CUDA or similar GPU programming is a plus. Deep Learning Frameworks: Familiarity with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, vLLM or SGLang and with distributed training or inference concepts. Software Engineering Fundamentals: Proficiency in C++ and Python, with experience in debugging, profiling and writing tests. Problem Solving & Communication: Strong problem-solving skills, eagerness to learn, and good written and verbal communication skills. Industry Experience: professional experience in software development, with exposure to performance engineering, systems software, networking, or GPU programming. amd-86384.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: AMD is seeking a Principal AI Software & Systems Architect to help drive adoption of AMD AI solutions in the on premise, enterprise environment. This role requires deep expertise in AI software stacks, inference runtimes, heterogeneous computing, and hardware-aware software architecture. You will analyze real-world AI deployments, determine how workloads should be mapped across CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, and distributed infrastructure, identify platform and ecosystem gaps, and drive the technical work required to enable successful enterprise deployments on AMD platforms. The ideal candidate can reason about AI workloads from framework to hardware and translate customer requirements into software, platform, and product direction. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a systems-oriented software architect with deep understanding of AI frameworks, accelerators, and performance engineering. You are comfortable taking a customer deployment built for another platform, determine what parts run unchanged, what parts must be modified, what parts are missing from the ecosystem, and what engineering investments are required to make the workload successful on AMD. You bring: Deep understanding of AI workload architecture and hardware-aware software design Experience analyzing complex software stacks spanning frameworks, runtimes, drivers, operating systems, and hardware The ability to move seamlessly between architecture, performance analysis, and technical execution Strong customer and ISV engagement skills with engineering-level credibility The ability to influence software, hardware, and product roadmaps using real-world workload requirements KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AI Workload Analysis & Architecture Analyze customer and ISV AI deployments, including models, frameworks, runtimes, serving infrastructure, and dependencies. Decompose workloads to identify portability, performance, scalability, and operational requirements. Determine the optimal deployment architecture across client, edge, workstation, and datacenter environments. Evaluate how workloads should be partitioned across CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, and distributed compute resources for optimal performance and overall TCO, including modeling of the TCO for customers. Define reference architectures for enterprise AI deployments and emerging AI workload patterns. Platform Enablement & Optimization Identify software, runtime, framework, compiler, driver, and hardware dependencies that impact deployment on AMD platforms. Define and drive the technical work required to enable workloads on AMD hardware and software stacks. Partner with engineering teams to close ecosystem gaps, improve platform readiness, and accelerate customer adoption. Analyze workload performance and identify bottlenecks related to compute, memory, communication, storage, power, and utilization. Establish performance targets, validation criteria, and benchmarking methodologies to support TCO discussions. Customer & ISV Technical Leadership Serve as the technical lead for strategic customer and ISV engagements. Conduct architecture reviews and technical assessments of AI deployments. Guide customers and partners through workload migration, platform selection, enablement, and optimization activities. Develop reusable deployment patterns, best practices, and technical guidance that can be applied across multiple engagements. Product & Platform Strategy Translate real-world workload requirements into software, platform, and hardware requirements. Influence AMD roadmap priorities through direct engagement with customers, ISVs, and ecosystem partners. Identify emerging AI deployment trends and opportunities across client, edge, workstation, and datacenter markets. Help shape AMD's long-term AI platform strategy through workload-driven insights and technical leadership. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Deep understanding of AI inference systems, model serving architectures, AI infrastructure, and performance optimization in production environments. Strong understanding of AI software stacks, including frameworks, runtimes, compilers, drivers, and accelerator libraries. Experience analyzing and optimizing software across multiple layers of the stack, from application and framework behavior through runtime, operating system, driver, and hardware interactions. Strong understanding of heterogeneous computing architectures and workload partitioning across CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, and distributed compute resources. Experience evaluating workload characteristics such as latency, throughput, memory footprint, communication patterns, scalability, power efficiency, and total cost of ownership (TCO). Experience enabling, optimizing, porting, or debugging software on GPU or other accelerator platforms. Ability to decompose complex customer deployments, identify software and platform dependencies, and define the technical work required to achieve successful deployment on a new platform. Experience leading technical discussions with customers, ISVs, and internal engineering teams. amd-80588.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. The Role: AMD’s Embedded Business unit is looking for a Senior PM - Automotive IVI SW and Solutions for the exciting role of owning and driving the execution of business-critical SW programs. The Person: As a Senior Software Program Manager, you will own the planning and execution of complex software programs that deliver SDKs, software suites, and integrated software solutions enabling new SoC product launches for key customers in the Automotive Infotainment (IVI) segment. You will drive end‑to‑end software release execution by partnering closely with silicon design, platform product management, software development, performance benchmarking, validation/QA, and applications engineering teams. You will build and leverage strong relationships with senior engineering and management stakeholders, to report progress, align on critical topics, influence priorities, and drive software‑related action items to closure. Key Responsibilities: Own and drive software program execution for strategic IVI platforms, ensuring SDKs, software suites, and integrated SW solutions meet scope, quality, and schedule commitments aligned with hardware milestones. Lead cross‑functional release planning for SDKs and integrated software stacks (features, target platforms, OS support, toolchains, reference applications) with software architects, product management, and OEM/Tier‑1 customers. Define, maintain, and own software program plans and release roadmaps, including dependencies on silicon, boards, firmware, BSPs, middleware, applications, safety/security components, and ecosystem partners. Drive coordinated release readiness for Automotive IVI software through core team meetings Report overall software execution and release status at senior leadership level and clearly communicate schedule changes, critical issues, and risks, along with mitigation and recovery plans. Design, implement, and continuously improve lightweight, standardized SW execution and release processes (e.g., integration gates, release criteria, defect triage, branching/labeling, release documentation) that scale across IVI programs. Lead the prioritization and resolution of critical defects and integration issues, coordinating across BSP, drivers, middleware, applications, silicon/platform teams, and customer engineering organizations. Manage and own software‑related escalations, setting up and running tiger teams, driving root‑cause and corrective actions, and ensuring timely, transparent communication to all stakeholders. Facilitate closure of complex, cross‑company issues and dependencies involving AMD teams, Automotive OEMs/Tier‑1s, and ecosystem partners (OS vendors, middleware providers, tool vendors). Align IVI software roadmaps (SDKs, reference stacks, integrated solutions) with AMD’s technology roadmaps (SoCs, GPUs, AI accelerators, connectivity, and platform features); lead migration strategies for customers on prior generations. Support pre‑design‑win and post‑design‑win activities for strategic Automotive accounts by providing credible software roadmaps, schedules, and feature commitments; coordinate early SDKs, evaluation kits, and reference demos. Preferred Experience: Extensive experience leading large‑scale software programs for SoC‑based systems, ideally in Automotive IVI (e.g., Android Automotive, Linux, Xen, QNX, or adjacent embedded domains). Strong background in the software development lifecycle for SDKs and application frameworks, including integration and release engineering. Proven ability to leverage AI-driven automation tools to optimize program delivery, including the streamlining of requirements management and cross-functional reporting to enhance operational efficiency. Proven ability to drive multiple concurrent strategic programs, managing competing priorities across customers, platforms, and product lines. Solid understanding of SoC architectures and common IP blocks (CPU, GPU, display, audio, connectivity, safety/security IP) and their implications for software enablement and performance. Demonstrated experience with program metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting, and familiarity with budget, headcount, and resource planning. Exceptional communication and influence skills, capable of aligning diverse stakeholders—from engineers to executives—around complex technical and schedule decisions. Comfortably operating in a large, matrixed organization, achieving results through influence, leadership, and escalation management rather than direct authority. Self‑starter with strong ownership and leadership qualities, energized by fast‑paced, ambiguous environments and aggressive Automotive schedules. Track record of delivering end‑to‑end program outcomes from inception through production. Experience defining program scope, success criteria, and KPIs in collaboration with architects, systems engineers, and business leaders, and using data to steer the program. Primary owner for clear, concise messaging of software status, risks, and decisions to internal and external senior stakeholders. Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills, including structured risk management, scenario planning, and data‑driven decision making. Academic Credentials: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, with 12+ years of relevant experience in software program management, software development, or embedded systems. THE ROLE: We are looking for an experienced Program Manager to join a fast-paced software development organization delivering solutions for some of AMD’s key customers. This role sits at the intersection of software engineering, customer engagement, and program execution, partnering across development, firmware, hardware, manufacturing, and business teams to drive successful customer programs from requirements through delivery. The team works in an environment that increasingly leverages AI-assisted code development to accelerate software solutions. In this highly visible role, you will work directly with engineering teams and customers to understand requirements, establish execution plans, manage software deliverables, identify and mitigate risks, and keep complex programs moving forward. This is an opportunity to work across technologies and organizations, build relationships throughout AMD and with customers, and play an important role in delivering the software and technology that enable next-generation computing and AI solutions. THE PERSON: You are a self-directed, highly collaborative program leader who is comfortable operating in a complex and dynamic engineering environment. You can move comfortably between technical discussions, customer conversations, and executive-level communication while keeping teams aligned on priorities and deliverables. You bring strong analytical, problem-solving, presentation, and risk-management skills, along with a high level of ownership and attention to detail. You know how to build relationships across teams, influence without direct authority, navigate differing viewpoints, and drive issues toward resolution. You are also curious about evolving technology and comfortable working with software teams that incorporate AI-assisted development tools into their workflows. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Define, plan, and drive software projects and program plans in partnership with engineering, program leadership, and customers. Partner with customers to understand platform and software requirements and translate those needs into actionable engineering plans, schedules, and deliverables. Drive software releases and customer program deliverables while coordinating dependencies across software, firmware, hardware, manufacturing, and other cross-functional teams. Create and maintain program management artifacts, including schedules, resource forecasts, risk and issue logs, action plans, and program status reporting. Identify technical and program risks early, develop mitigation strategies, and drive cross-functional teams toward resolution. Facilitate communication and alignment across development teams, customers, business units, product management, and other key stakeholders. Collect, analyze, organize, and communicate program performance data through dashboards, status reports, and executive-level updates. Identify opportunities to improve existing processes, team efficiency, communication, and program execution. Build strong working relationships across the organization and create alignment among teams with competing priorities or perspectives. Develop a strong understanding of the team’s software development environment, customers, products, and processes, progressing toward independent ownership of programs and customer deliverables. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Strong understanding of software development, software design principles, and the software development lifecycle. Technical program management experience supporting software development and customer-facing programs. Experience managing software releases, engineering schedules, dependencies, deliverables, risks, and issues. Experience working in cross-functional or matrixed engineering organizations. Strong customer relationship management skills with the ability to translate customer needs into actionable engineering requirements. Experience collaborating with software engineering, firmware, hardware, manufacturing, product management, and business teams. Familiarity with AI-assisted software or code development environments and tools. Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and risk-management skills. Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to communicate effectively across technical teams and executive-level stakeholders. amd-91724.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: We are building next-generation systems software for AMD GPUs with Rust as a core technical direction. The work spans compilers, runtimes, low-level GPU software, firmware, developer tooling, and methods for improving the safety and correctness of complex hardware-software systems. Rust is not incidental to this role. You will help establish how Rust is used in performance-sensitive and high-trust parts of the GPU stack, including the compiler and tooling support, system interfaces, engineering practices, and validation methods required for production deployment. You will have the opportunity to influence both near-term implementations and the longer-term architecture for using Rust across current and future AMD platforms. THE PERSON: This role is for a deeply technical compiler and systems generalist who enjoys working across abstraction layers. You may move between Rust source semantics, rustc internals, intermediate representations, MLIR and LLVM, target-specific code generation, object formats, runtimes, GPU ISA, firmware, and hardware interfaces. You should have strong judgment about correctness boundaries. Memory safety is important, but production correctness also depends on concurrency, ordering, ABI compatibility, device behavior, compiler transformations, and the assumptions between software and hardware. You will help make those assumptions explicit and build evidence that the resulting systems behave as intended. The ideal candidate has deep expertise in at least one part of this stack and the ability to become productive in unfamiliar areas. Experience with every technology listed below is not expected. A research background is not required, although the ability to read technical work, form testable hypotheses, and turn promising ideas into reliable implementations is valuable. The work sits at the intersection of Rust systems programming, production compiler infrastructure, GPU architecture, firmware, program analysis, and formal methods. Hardware-software co-design experience is highly valuable, especially when compiler, runtime, firmware, or ISA choices must evolve together. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead the design and implementation of production-quality Rust components for low-level and performance-sensitive GPU systems. Help make Rust a first-class engineering language across relevant parts of the GPU software stack, including toolchain integration, libraries, coding standards, diagnostics, testing, and deployment practices. Design and implement compiler pipelines involving rustc, MIR, target-neutral intermediate representations, MLIR dialects and transformations, LLVM IR, and AMDGPU code generation. Build analyses, transformations, legalization passes, and target-specific lowering for GPU execution models, memory spaces, synchronization, capabilities, and specialized hardware operations. Define typed and auditable interfaces across compiler, host runtime, device code, firmware, and hardware boundaries. Work on ABI definition and validation, argument layout, calling conventions, linker and loader behavior, ELF and code-object metadata, and source-to-binary identity. Develop or improve bare-metal and no std Rust components where explicit state, bounded behavior, fail-closed handling, and predictable hardware effects are required. Use testing, fuzzing, property-based testing, differential execution, executable models, and hardware validation to find semantic gaps and prevent regressions. Apply program analysis or formal methods where they provide meaningful assurance, including source-level invariants, state-machine properties, refinement obligations, and clearly documented trusted boundaries. Distinguish precisely among type-system guarantees, source-level proofs, compiler evidence, binary validation, simulator results, and behavior observed on hardware. Partner with compiler, runtime, firmware, architecture, validation, security, and performance teams to solve problems that cross organizational and technical boundaries. Write design documents, lead technical reviews, mentor engineers, and explain complex language, compiler, and hardware behavior clearly. Evaluate emerging compiler and verification technologies and integrate them when they improve the safety, performance, maintainability, or development velocity of production systems. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Strong production Rust experience, including ownership and borrowing, lifetimes, traits and generics, error handling, concurrency, FFI, and the careful design of safe abstractions over unsafe operations. Experience with low-level or constrained Rust, including no std, embedded systems, firmware, custom targets, allocators, volatile access, interrupt handling, or architecture-specific code. Strong C or C++ systems programming skills and the ability to work across mixed-language codebases. Experience with rustc internals, MIR, custom codegen backends, procedural macros, compiler plugins, or other Rust toolchain infrastructure. Experience with LLVM, MLIR, GCC, or another production compiler framework. Experience designing intermediate representations, dialects, analyses, optimization passes, legalization, instruction selection, scheduling, or target-specific code generation. Understanding of compiler correctness issues such as undefined behavior, aliasing, provenance, layout, calling conventions, memory models, and source-to-target semantic preservation. Ability to read and reason about low-level assembly, ISA encodings, compiler output, and machine-level execution. Experience with linkers, loaders, ELF or other object formats, code-object metadata, DWARF, LLVM MC, disassembly, post-link analysis, or binary rewriting. Understanding of GPU execution models, including waves or warps, SIMD/SIMT execution, address spaces, registers, local or shared memory, caches, synchronization, atomics, barriers, and asynchronous operations. AMDGPU, GCN, RDNA, CDNA, ROCm, HIP, HSA, or AMDGPU LLVM backend experience. Experience with GPU runtimes, drivers, firmware, embedded processors, device initialization, command processing, queueing, or hardware control paths. Experience building secure or high-assurance systems that process untrusted inputs or operate across privilege, memory-isolation, or hardware trust boundaries. Experience with program analysis, abstract interpretation, symbolic execution, model checking, SMT solvers, or formal verification tools such as Verus, Lean, Coq, Isabelle, Dafny, or TLA+. Experience writing executable specifications, proving state-machine invariants, or validating refinement between source, IR, binaries, simulators, RTL, and hardware. Strong validation instincts, including adversarial testing, differential testing, property-based testing, fuzzing, reproducible evidence, and careful treatment of assumptions and counterexamples. Hardware-software co-design experience for ISA features, compiler-visible architecture, memory systems, synchronization, security mechanisms, or specialized compute pipelines. Technical leadership experience: setting direction, resolving ambiguous cross-layer problems, influencing partner teams, mentoring engineers, and communicating tradeoffs clearly. PREFERRED ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience. Research publications and advanced degrees are welcome but are not required. LOCATION: San Jose, CA #LI-DNI This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. AMD and its subsidiaries are equal opportunity, inclusive employers and will consider all applicants without regard to age, ancestry, color, marital status, medical condition, mental or physical disability, national origin, race, religion, political and/or third-party affiliation, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: We are seeking a Senior Triton Compiler and Kernel Engineer to advance Triton performance and capabilities on AMD GPUs. Triton is an open-source language and compiler for developing high-performance GPU kernels in Python. It is a critical layer in the AI software stack, connecting frameworks and workloads to GPU hardware. Triton is strategic to AMD’s AI roadmap, and AMD is investing fully in making it a first-class platform for current and future AMD GPUs. You will work across GPU architecture, compilers, kernels, multi-GPU communication, and AI frameworks while contributing to upstream Triton and AMD’s ROCm software stack. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate has strong experience in several of the following areas: GPU architecture and programming Compiler development and optimization High-performance GPU kernels Multi-GPU communication and collective operations Distributed AI training and inference AI workload and framework performance Low-level performance analysis You can reason across the stack—from distributed AI algorithms and Triton programs to compiler transformations, communication libraries, generated instructions, and GPU hardware. Create high-performance kernels for attention, GEMM, MoE, and other AI workloads. Develop and optimize multi-GPU kernels and communication primitives. Enable new AMD GPU and interconnect capabilities through effective Triton abstractions. Analyze compute, memory, communication, occupancy, register usage, and generated code. Resolve complex correctness and performance issues across single- and multi-GPU workloads. Collaborate with GPU architecture, ROCm, PyTorch, and AI framework teams. Contribute designs and implementations to upstream Triton and LLVM/MLIR. Provide technical leadership, code reviews, and mentoring. Experience with collective communication, distributed programming, and libraries such as RCCL or NCCL. Understanding of communication topologies, interconnects, synchronization, and communication–computation overlap. Familiarity with distributed training, inference, tensor parallelism, expert parallelism, or pipeline parallelism. Experience using AI coding tools and autonomous agents to accelerate software development, debugging, benchmarking, and kernel performance tuning. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: At AMD, we build products that accelerate next-generation computing—from AI and data centers to PCs, gaming, and embedded systems. Progress here comes from bold ideas, strong execution, and people who care about hard problems. This role sits at the center of that mission: making AMD the platform of choice for the most demanding AI workloads by improving how models train, align, and run on our GPUs. THE PERSON: We're looking for a senior software engineer who combines deep systems performance work with modern AI—someone who can shape software from GPU kernels through distributed training and inference. You'll join a core team of specialists working on the latest AMD hardware and software. Your work will directly influence the ROCm ecosystem and how foundation models and agentic systems perform on AMD GPUs. The challenge: Help train and run AI systems that make AI itself more efficient on GPUs—tuning stacks, kernels, and workflows in ways that can materially shift what's possible on our hardware. This is a high-impact, hands-on role. You'll own hard technical problems, influence direction across teams, and mentor others as we scale AMD's AI software strategy. WHAT YOU'LL DO Own the AI software stack: Establish best practices and drive performance from low-level GPU kernels to large-scale distributed systems. Use modern LLMs and agent-based tooling where it accelerates development and tuning of the ROCm ecosystem. Accelerate foundation models and agents: Improve training, post-training, and inference for LLMs and autonomous AI workloads so AMD is the default platform for the most demanding use cases. Co-design hardware and software: Partner on the full lifecycle—from GPU architecture input to software for new accelerators—and engage with the broader AI community to keep AMD at the forefront. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR We need someone who can go deep in the areas below and collaborate effectively. SYSTEMS & GPU PERFORMANCE (KERNEL ENGINEERING) Expert-level modern C++ and design of large, performance-critical systems. Strong grasp of GPU architecture, memory hierarchy, and kernel optimization (HIP/CUDA). Hands-on delivery on large-scale C++/HIP/CUDA codebases, such as ROCm (rocBLAS, hipDNN, Composable Kernel, AITemplate), the CUDA ecosystem (cuBLAS, cuDNN, CUTLASS, Thrust, CUB, NCCL), and ML framework cores such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX (C++/HIP/CUDA paths). Comfort diagnosing bottlenecks with profilers (for example, ROCm Profiler and Nsight) in multi-GPU, distributed settings. AI POST-TRAINING & LLM SYSTEMS Deep understanding of transformers, attention, and the full model lifecycle. Hands-on work in alignment and post-training—for example, SFT, RLHF, and GRPO. Awareness of current LLM trends, including MoE, quantization, speculative decoding, and agentic systems. Experience optimizing post-training and inference pipelines at scale. PREFERRED BACKGROUND Substantial professional experience in software development within performance-critical environments. Extensive HIP/CUDA experience optimizing deep learning and OSS LLM inference/training kernels and operators. Strong technical ownership and a track record of shipping complex systems. Clear communication and influence across teams. Plus: Deep familiarity with the AMD ROCm/HIP ecosystem. Plus: Working knowledge of RTL design and Verilog/SystemVerilog for hardware–software co-design. We are seeking a visionary Lead/Principal Diagnostics Engineer to drive our shift from proven post-silicon software validation frameworks and System-Level Tests (SLT) directly into all manufacturing flows for our latest products.. THE PERSON: In this role, you will bridge the gap between platform-level software execution and traditional hardware-driven manufacturing test patterns. You will design the architecture, tooling, and translation methodologies required to pack, convert, and stream complex software-driven GFX and compute test cases into robust, production-grade patterns used across all manufacturing insertions. This is a high-impact role requiring deep knowledge of system software/hardware interactions, graphics IP mechanics, and high-volume structural/functional manufacturing test domains. KEY RESPONSIBILTIIES Strategic Technical Leadership: Define the technical roadmap, architecture, and deployment strategy for migrating post-silicon SLT and functional GFX IP feature diagnostics onto various testing and validation platforms Pattern Generation & Conversion: Architect and develop software utilities/pipelines to convert functional diagnostic sequences, register configurations, and compute workloads into cycle-accurate vector formats (e.g., STIL, WGL, or proprietary tester formats) compatible with modern testers. Cross-Domain Collaboration: Serve as the primary technical liaison between the GFX/Compute Diagnostics team, Product/Test Engineering, and Design-for-Test (DFT) teams, analyzing and root causing RTL bugs and improving pre-silicon coverage Platform Integration & Emulation: Analyze existing platform-level hardware/software dependencies (such as sideband management interfaces, firmware, and power management behaviors) to build deterministic, tester-friendly models that emulate host behaviors on multiple hardware platforms Test Coverage & Cost Optimization: Optimize tester execution times (test cost reduction) while maximizing structural and functional test coverage for data center GPU IPs, focusing on massively parallel compute pipelines, high-bandwidth memory (HBM) controllers, and matrix math engines. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience: Proven industry experience in silicon engineering spanning post-silicon validation, product engineering, diagnostics development, or structural/functional test generation. Platform HW/SW Proficiency: Strong programming background in C/C++ and Python, with a concrete understanding of bare-metal or driver-level programming, registers, firmware interactions, and system memory maps Pattern Flow Knowledge: Expert understanding of structural pattern generation, vector timing, clock domains, and diagnostic patterns (such as functional vectors, BIST/MBIST, or scan compression output). Familiarity with high-volume manufacturing challenges unique to data center architectures, including high-power profiles, HBM integration, and multi-die chiplet interconnect protocols (e.g., UCIe, proprietary fabrics). Deep understanding of GFX and compute architectures, with proven ability to design and implement diagnostic and test cases that maximize coverage and proactively identify silicon issues early Understanding of AI/ML principles and some experience in applying LLM & ML models in applications Experience with working in DevOps environment like GitHub, CI/CD pipelines Excellent problem-solving abilities with a keen eye for detail are highly valued ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Education: Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field. This role focuses on maximizing performance and efficiency of large-scale AI training/RL/inference workloads on AMD GPU platforms. You will drive innovations across the full software-hardware stack, optimizing at scale and pushing the limits of system throughput, scalability, and utilization for generative AI workloads. This position requires deep expertise in GPU performance analysis, distributed systems, and ML workloads, along with the ability to influence architecture, software ecosystems, and best practices across the organization. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a recognized technical leader with deep expertise in GPU performance optimization, large-scale distributed system, and system-level bottleneck analysis. You have a strong understanding of GPU architecture, interconnects, memory hierarchies, and communication patterns, and can translate this knowledge into measurable improvements in training efficiency at scale. You are comfortable operating across layers—from kernels and runtimes to frameworks and distributed strategies—and have a track record of driving impactful optimizations and influencing technical direction. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead performance optimization of large-scale AI training/RL/inference workloads on AMD GPU platforms across single-node and multi-node environments. Identify and eliminate system bottlenecks across compute, memory, and communication (e.g., kernel efficiency, memory bandwidth, network utilization). Drive cross-stack optimizations spanning kernels, compilers, runtimes, communication libraries, and ML frameworks. Develop and apply advanced profiling, benchmarking, and performance modeling methodologies. Collaborate with hardware, compiler, and framework teams to influence next-generation GPU architecture and software stack design. Contribute to and lead open-source efforts to improve ecosystem performance on AMD platforms. Stay at the forefront of advancements in large-scale systems and performance optimization techniques. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Deep expertise in GPU architecture and performance characteristics (compute units, memory hierarchy, interconnects such as PCIe/Infinity Fabric/RDMA). Strong experience with performance profiling tools (e.g., ROCm tools, Nsight-like systems, custom profilers) and bottleneck analysis. Proven experience optimizing large-scale distributed training workloads across thousands of GPUs. Experience with frameworks such as Megatron-LM, Torchtitan, vLLM, Sglang, or equivalent. Strong understanding of communication libraries and patterns (e.g., NCCL/RCCL, collective ops, overlap of compute and communication). Proficiency in Python and at least one systems language (C++/CUDA/HIP), including debugging and low-level optimization. Experience with compiler stacks, kernel optimization, or graph-level optimization is a strong plus. THE ROLE: At AMD, we push the boundaries of what is possible. We believe in changing the world for the better by driving innovation in high-performance computing, graphics, and visualization technologies – building blocks for gaming, immersive platforms, and the data center. THE PERSON: Developing great technology takes more than talent: it takes amazing people who understand collaboration, respect, and who will go the “extra mile” to achieve unthinkable results. If you have this type of passion, we invite you to look at the opportunities available to come join our team. Study new features and new IPs in next gen SoC product and train software engineers for designing and developing new diagnostic cases Driving the technical requirements to achieve the feature coverage and hardware bug capture targets through the diag cases. Forward thinker to improve feature coverage model, test time reduction, development process and drive innovation. Lead the resolution of critical technical challenges, including complex issue debugging and triage. Guide Diags IP and release engineers in root-cause analysis and test coverage enhancements PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Significant firmware or software development experience, with close interaction with hardware or product engineering team. Excellent understanding of processors based on SoC architecture, including processor, system IO, memory, engine IP (e.g. graphics, display, video codec etc.), security block, to identify the critical areas for focus of SoC & IP verification. Strong system level debugging and testing skills, and capability to quickly identify problems and provide robust solutions. Strong Linux environment programming knowledge, including device driver, user space programming, shell scripts, GCC/Clang toolchains, etc. Rich knowledge with x86 CPU architecture and programming skills. Or strong discreate graphics software development. Strong mix of large-scale firmware or software development ability and hardware understanding. Experience with BIOS, GPU, PCIe, DDR, PMU, RAS firmware development is a plus. Hands-on experience with SoC emulation and bring up is preferred. Experience being technical leader or architect for software programs is a definite asset. amd-79010.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: We are looking for a visionary technical leader to join the AI Software group. As a Fellow, you will be accountable for defining and driving the end-to-end software optimization strategy to achieve industry-leading performance for our top-tier customers. You will sit at the intersection of architecture, customer engagement, and software engineering, ensuring that AMD’s software stack—from ROCm and compilers to high-level AI frameworks—is tuned to extract maximum performance for the world's most demanding AI workloads. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a technical powerhouse with a proven track record of solving complex performance bottlenecks at scale. You possess deep knowledge of AI hardware architecture and software optimization, with the ability to map emerging model architectures to low-level software. You are an exceptional communicator who can translate complex technical challenges into strategic roadmaps and influence senior leadership, while also engaging deeply with key customers to solve their most critical performance needs. Workload Performance Engineering: Lead the profiling, analysis, and tuning of large-scale models (LLMs, Diffusion, Multimodal, and MoE) to ensure "out-of-the-box" performance excellence on AMD hardware. Customer Engagement: Partner with top customers and hyperscalers to understand their unique workload requirements and deliver tailored architectural wins and software optimizations. Hardware-Software Co-design: Collaborate across hardware architecture, compiler, and framework teams to influence future silicon features based on evolving AI workload trends. Ecosystem Innovation: Drive the development of advanced tools and frameworks for performance estimation, modeling, and automated reporting. Community & Mentorship: Act as a technical ambassador in industry forums and open-source communities. Mentor and inspire the next generation of AMD’s technical leaders and engineers. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Deep software development experience with experience in a high-level technical leadership role (Fellow or equivalent). Deep expertise in AI Frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, vLLM, SGLang) and the ROCm software stack. Proven history of optimizing distributed inference and training at scale across multi-node/multi-GPU environments. Mastery of performance profiling tools (e.g., TorchProfiler, ROCm Profiler, Nsight) and hardware-level performance modeling. Strong understanding of modern model architectures (Transformer, Attention, KV Cache) and optimization techniques like quantization, speculative decoding, and FlashAttention. Demonstrated ability to drive cross-functional initiatives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments. Demonstrated research or applied experience in AI/ML, including areas such as deep learning, model training/inference optimization, large language models, or computer vision. Research, design, develop, and improve system level test (SLT) software, test programs, and characterization flows for datacenter server processors across the full product life cycle, including post silicon bring up and volume production. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: Triton is a widely adopted language and compiler for high-performance GPU kernels, powering major AI frameworks such as PyTorch, vLLM, and SGLang. As AI workloads increasingly scale across multiple GPUs and nodes, first-class support for distributed execution and communication in Triton is strategically critical to enabling efficient large-scale training and inference on AMD Instinct Accelerators. AMD GPUs are an official Triton backend, and delivering industry-leading distributed performance and scalability on AMD Instinct accelerators is a key priority. The performance, scalability, and usability of Triton directly impact the competitiveness of AMD hardware in large-scale AI deployments. In this role, you will advance the Triton compiler and runtime stack for AMD CDNA and next-generation GPU architectures by building native distributed execution and communication capabilities. You will develop compiler and runtime infrastructure that enables efficient inter-GPU communication, scalable execution, and optimal hardware utilization. You will work across compiler, runtime, and hardware layers, collaborating closely with GPU architecture and software teams to help establish AMD GPUs as a best-in-class platform for Triton-based distributed AI. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate has deep expertise in GPU architecture, compiler technologies, and distributed GPU systems, with proven experience optimizing workloads at multi-GPU scale. You are comfortable working across the full execution stack — from compiler and runtime to hardware — and understand how GPU execution, memory hierarchy, and inter-GPU communication impact performance. You have experience working close to the GPU runtime, communication stack, or compiler backend, and are motivated to build native distributed execution and communication capabilities tightly integrated with the compiler and runtime to maximize scalability and hardware utilization. You thrive on solving complex system-level performance challenges and delivering scalable, high-performance GPU infrastructure. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Design and develop native distributed communication and execution capabilities within the Triton AMDGPU backend, enabling scalable multi-GPU execution for large-scale AI workloads Design and implement Triton compiler and runtime mechanisms for native GPU-initiated communication, including collective operations, remote memory access, synchronization, and distributed execution primitives Drive performance optimization across compute and communication, including inter-GPU data movement, communication/computation overlap, memory hierarchy utilization, and GPU-driven Job Title: Edge and Enterprise Solution Architect & Systems Engineer General Description of the Role As an Edge & Enterprise Solution Architect, you will be the core technical authority responsible for defining, architecting, and deploying end-to-end GPU-accelerated computing solutions targeted at enterprise data centers, hybrid cloud environments, and edge platforms. In this role, you will bridge the gap between customer workload requirements and complex system architecture—combining cutting-edge GPU hardware platforms with complete software application stacks to solve real-world enterprise and edge challenges. You will partner closely with key enterprise customers, ISVs, systems integrators, and internal engineering teams (hardware, firmware, driver, and software stack teams) to translate business needs into robust, scalable, and secure deployment blueprints. Your scope spans the full technology stack: from evaluating underlying GPU compute hardware, thermals, form factors, high-speed interconnects, and enterprise management interfaces (e.g., Redfish, IPMI, iDRAC/iLO) down to configuring AI/ML frameworks, edge orchestration platforms (Kubernetes/K3s), telemetry, security, and domain-specific edge and enterprise application stacks. Key Responsibilities Hardware, SoC & Platform Architecture Platform & Systems Architecture: Drive end-to-end dGPU platform definition, evaluating trade-offs across SoC design, power delivery, thermal envelopes, board-level signal/power integrity, and form factors for server, edge, and client systems. Memory & Interconnect Trade-Offs: Assess memory architecture requirements (GDDR, LPDDR, HBM) alongside memory controller design and compression techniques; optimize high-speed interconnect topologies to maximize bandwidth and system efficiency. Manageability & Telemetry: Define hardware-level telemetry, power-monitoring, and diagnostics hooks to integrate seamlessly with enterprise manageability platforms (iDRAC, iLO, IPMI) for data center and edge deployments. Software Architecture & Go-to-Market Readiness Full-Stack Software Vision: Translate high-level system architectural concepts into concrete software requirements spanning firmware, drivers, runtimes, ROCm libraries, tools, and application layer stacks, across AI, media, visualization, and simulation workloads. Enterprise & Cloud Enablement: Create long-term software architecture plans of record that ensure seamless integration with Kubernetes orchestration, AI frameworks, and enterprise management tools. Customer Enablement & Deployment: Author reference architectures, sizing guidance, and tuning guides for customers, ISVs, and systems integrators; support application porting and migration onto the platform; act as the escalation point for failures in a live customer software stack. Hardware–Software Co-Design & Pre-Silicon Validation Co-Design Leadership: Lead the hardware/software interface definition, ensuring silicon feature sets directly support software requirements while firmware, driver, and library designs reflect hardware constraints. Early Silicon & Bring-Up: Serve as a primary technical escalation point during pre-silicon modeling and early post-silicon bring-up; debug complex cross-layer issues spanning physical hardware, firmware, drivers, and application software. Diagnostics & Workflows: Guide the development of robust diagnostics, pre-silicon emulators, and silicon validation tools to accelerate bring-up schedules across cross-functional engineering teams. Cross-Functional Leadership & Process Innovation Cross-Functional Alignment: Collaborate closely across SoC architecture, design verification, hardware engineering, driver development, performance libraries, and product management teams. AI-Assisted Development: Champion the use of AI-assisted tools to accelerate system modeling, code development, review, and documentation, establishing standards for traceability and validation. Knowledge Capture: Document reusable architectural patterns, bring-up playbooks, and hardware-software design best practices to scale engineering capability across product generations. Experience & Qualifications Required Experience & Qualifications 3+/ 7+/ 10+ years of engineering experience in dGPU/SoC platform architecture, hardware engineering, systems software, firmware, or low-level driver development used to bring new silicon to market. Proven track record in Hardware/Software Co-Design, including defining hardware-software interfaces, analyzing system performance bottlenecks, and debugging complex multi-layer hardware/firmware/software issues. 0 / 0 /2+ years in technical leadership roles with a demonstrated ability to drive technical alignment and resolve ambiguity across multi-disciplinary teams (SoC, platform, drivers, software). Solid grasp of enterprise manageability standards (IPMI, iDRAC, iLO) and system telemetry frameworks and the software monitoring stacks that operations teams run in production (for example Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry). Hands-on experience with containerized GPU deployment and orchestration on Linux and Windows: Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes (including K3s for edge nodes). Experience with Slurm or another cluster scheduler for batch and HPC environments. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex architectural trade-offs to both hardware and software audiences. Willingness to travel domestically and internationally on an occasional basis. Desired & Optional Qualifications Machine Learning & AI Frameworks: Knowledge of ML/AI workloads and model architectures (Transformers, Stable Diffusion, CNNs, UNet), including optimization for GPU acceleration libraries (e.g., ROCm, CUDA). Graphics Architecture: Hands-on experience with DirectX 12, Vulkan, ray tracing pipelines, neural rendering, or game engine performance profiling. Advanced Systems Engineering: Experience with pre-silicon simulation/emulation environments, server board design, or power integrity analysis. Production AI Deployment: Experience taking AI workloads from prototype into production: installing and integrating the serving stack (for example vLLM, SGLang, or equivalent), scaling it across nodes, tuning throughput and latency, and handing it over for the customer to operate. Education: Advanced degree (M.Sc., M.Eng., or Ph.D.) in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. SMTS SYSTEMS DESIGN ENGINEER Job Title: Edge and Enterprise Solution Architect & Systems Engineer 1. General Description of the Role As an Edge & Enterprise Solution Architect, you will be the core technical authority responsible for defining, architecting, and deploying end-to-end GPU-accelerated computing solutions targeted at enterprise data centers, hybrid cloud environments, and edge platforms. In this role, you will bridge the gap between customer workload requirements and complex system architecture—combining cutting-edge GPU hardware platforms with complete software application stacks to solve real-world enterprise and edge challenges. You will partner closely with key enterprise customers, ISVs, systems integrators, and internal engineering teams (hardware, firmware, driver, and software stack teams) to translate business needs into robust, scalable, and secure deployment blueprints. Your scope spans the full technology stack: from evaluating underlying GPU compute hardware, thermals, form factors, high-speed interconnects, and enterprise management interfaces (e.g., Redfish, IPMI, iDRAC/iLO) down to configuring AI/ML frameworks, edge orchestration platforms (Kubernetes/K3s), telemetry, security, and domain-specific edge and enterprise application stacks. 2. Key Responsibilities Hardware, SoC & Platform Architecture Platform & Systems Architecture: Drive end-to-end dGPU platform definition, evaluating trade-offs across SoC design, power delivery, thermal envelopes, board-level signal/power integrity, and form factors for server, edge, and client systems. Memory & Interconnect Trade-Offs: Assess memory architecture requirements (GDDR, LPDDR, HBM) alongside memory controller design and compression techniques; optimize high-speed interconnect topologies to maximize bandwidth and system efficiency. Manageability & Telemetry: Define hardware-level telemetry, power-monitoring, and diagnostics hooks to integrate seamlessly with enterprise manageability platforms (iDRAC, iLO, IPMI) for data center and edge deployments. Software Architecture & Go-to-Market Readiness Full-Stack Software Vision: Translate high-level system architectural concepts into concrete software requirements spanning firmware, drivers, runtimes, ROCm libraries, tools, and application layer stacks, across AI, media, visualization, and simulation workloads. Enterprise & Cloud Enablement: Create long-term software architecture plans of record that ensure seamless integration with Kubernetes orchestration, AI frameworks, and enterprise management tools. Customer Enablement & Deployment: Author reference architectures, sizing guidance, and tuning guides for customers, ISVs, and systems integrators; support application porting and migration onto the platform; act as the escalation point for failures in a live customer software stack. Hardware–Software Co-Design & Pre-Silicon Validation Co-Design Leadership: Lead the hardware/software interface definition, ensuring silicon feature sets directly support software requirements while firmware, driver, and library designs reflect hardware constraints. Early Silicon & Bring-Up: Serve as a primary technical escalation point during pre-silicon modeling and early post-silicon bring-up; debug complex cross-layer issues spanning physical hardware, firmware, drivers, and application software. Diagnostics & Workflows: Guide the development of robust diagnostics, pre-silicon emulators, and silicon validation tools to accelerate bring-up schedules across cross-functional engineering teams. Cross-Functional Leadership & Process Innovation Cross-Functional Alignment: Collaborate closely across SoC architecture, design verification, hardware engineering, driver development, performance libraries, and product management teams. AI-Assisted Development: Champion the use of AI-assisted tools to accelerate system modeling, code development, review, and documentation, establishing standards for traceability and validation. Knowledge Capture: Document reusable architectural patterns, bring-up playbooks, and hardware-software design best practices to scale engineering capability across product generations. 3. Experience & Qualifications Required Experience & Qualifications 3+/ 7+/ 10+ years of engineering experience in dGPU/SoC platform architecture, hardware engineering, systems software, firmware, or low-level driver development used to bring new silicon to market. Proven track record in Hardware/Software Co-Design, including defining hardware-software interfaces, analyzing system performance bottlenecks, and debugging complex multi-layer hardware/firmware/software issues. 0 / 0 /2+ years in technical leadership roles with a demonstrated ability to drive technical alignment and resolve ambiguity across multi-disciplinary teams (SoC, platform, drivers, software). Solid grasp of enterprise manageability standards (IPMI, iDRAC, iLO) and system telemetry frameworks and the software monitoring stacks that operations teams run in production (for example Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry). Hands-on experience with containerized GPU deployment and orchestration on Linux and Windows: Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes (including K3s for edge nodes). Experience with Slurm or another cluster scheduler for batch and HPC environments. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex architectural trade-offs to both hardware and software audiences. Willingness to travel domestically and internationally on an occasional basis. Desired & Optional Qualifications Machine Learning & AI Frameworks: Knowledge of ML/AI workloads and model architectures (Transformers, Stable Diffusion, CNNs, UNet), including optimization for GPU acceleration libraries (e.g., ROCm, CUDA). Graphics Architecture: Hands-on experience with DirectX 12, Vulkan, ray tracing pipelines, neural rendering, or game engine performance profiling. Advanced Systems Engineering: Experience with pre-silicon simulation/emulation environments, server board design, or power integrity analysis. Production AI Deployment: Experience taking AI workloads from prototype into production: installing and integrating the serving stack (for example vLLM, SGLang, or equivalent), scaling it across nodes, tuning throughput and latency, and handing it over for the customer to operate. Education: Advanced degree (M.Sc., M.Eng., or Ph.D.) in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.
