amd-92891.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: AMD's Software and Solutions Team is seeking a Solution Engineering technical leader to accelerate the integration and adoption of AMD technology across the open software ecosystem. This role will define and deliver production-oriented solutions that connect AMD CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, networking, memory, and software platforms with the operating systems, databases, runtimes, APIs, developer frameworks, and cloud-native services customers use to build and operate modern infrastructure. The role will bridge AMD architecture and the broader open ecosystem by creating reference architectures, upstream integrations, reusable software components, validated deployment patterns, and early customer proof-of-concepts. Primary focus areas include Linux and other operating-system kernels, runtime and system services, database and data-platform enablement, API layers, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, container and orchestration environments, observability, security, and performance engineering. Working across AMD + AMD (A+A) and AMD + NVIDIA (A+N) environments and leveraging ROCm™, AMD Zen Software Studio, AMD Enterprise AI, open-source projects, industry standards, and upstream communities, this leader will make AMD platforms easier to adopt, integrate, operate, and optimize. AI is one supported workload domain—particularly inference, retrieval, developer tooling, and data-intensive services—but the role is fundamentally centered on open systems integration and solution engineering. As a recognized technical authority, this individual will collaborate with silicon architecture, product engineering, software organizations, customers, hyperscalers, ISVs, standards bodies, and open-source communities. The role will influence AMD hardware and software roadmaps through implementation evidence, workload analysis, ecosystem gaps, customer requirements, and measurable improvements in compatibility, performance, scalability, security, manageability, and developer experience. This is a highly technical, hands-on individual contributor role focused on architecture, integration, implementation, performance engineering, and ecosystem leadership. It is not a people management, program management, or alliance management position. THE PERSON: A deeply technical solution engineer and systems architect with broad expertise across operating systems, kernel and driver interfaces, runtime services, databases, distributed systems, APIs, cloud-native infrastructure, heterogeneous computing, networking, storage, virtualization, security, and performance engineering. This individual has a record of turning platform capabilities into integrated, supportable solutions that customers and open-source communities can deploy at scale. The ideal candidate understands how applications move through API, middleware, runtime, kernel, driver, firmware, and hardware layers, and how data moves across transactional databases, analytical platforms, caches, object stores, and retrieval systems. They can diagnose integration barriers, contribute production-quality code, shape stable interfaces, and optimize end-to-end behavior across AMD and third-party components. Familiarity with practical AI infrastructure, model serving, vector search, and MCP-enabled tools is valuable where these technologies intersect with broader platform solutions. This individual thrives in customer-facing and community-facing environments where long-term technical direction must be grounded in working code, benchmarks, upstream collaboration, and repeatable deployment outcomes. They lead through technical excellence and influence while partnering across engineering organizations and engaging directly with strategic customers, cloud providers, OEMs, ISVs, database vendors, operating-system communities, and standards organizations. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Define and execute AMD's solution engineering strategy for integrating AMD hardware and software into open-source, commercial, enterprise, cloud, and edge ecosystems, creating end-to-end reference architectures, reusable components, integration guides, validated configurations, and customer proof-of-concepts spanning AMD CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, networking, memory, storage, and accelerators. Drive enablement and upstream collaboration across Linux kernels, device drivers, firmware interfaces, system libraries, package ecosystems, container runtimes, Kubernetes, schedulers, service meshes, and observability platforms, and optimize runtime services—including language runtimes, compilers, libraries, inference and data-processing frameworks, communication stacks, and background system services—for AMD architectures. Integrate and optimize relational, NoSQL, analytical, vector, graph, and distributed database platforms on AMD systems, addressing query execution, concurrency, memory hierarchy, storage I/O, networking, resiliency, and scale-out performance. Design stable, secure, high-performance APIs and SDK integration patterns that expose AMD platform capabilities while simplifying application portability and developer adoption, and develop MCP servers, connectors, and reference patterns where MCP provides a practical interface between developer tools, enterprise data, platform services, and selected AI-assisted workflows. Support both AMD + AMD (A+A) and AMD + NVIDIA (A+N) deployment models, improving interoperability, workload portability, operational consistency, and customer choice. Apply rigorous profiling, benchmarking, tracing, and systems analysis to improve latency, throughput, scalability, availability, energy efficiency, total cost of ownership, and quality of service. Build security into solution architectures through confidential computing, trusted execution, attestation, identity, secure boot, software supply-chain controls, cryptography, data protection, governance, and auditability. Enable practical AI workloads where relevant, including model serving, retrieval, vector search, data pipelines, and developer productivity, without making AI the sole focus of the platform solution. Partner directly with strategic customers, hyperscalers, OEMs, ISVs, database and platform vendors, and open-source maintainers to resolve integration barriers and validate production readiness, translating implementation findings and ecosystem requirements into actionable feedback for AMD silicon, firmware, compiler, operating-system, runtime, library, and product roadmaps. Represent AMD through technical publications, conferences, standards bodies, upstream contributions, architecture reviews, and executive customer engagements, and mentor senior engineers and architects in systems integration, open-source engagement, performance engineering, and production solution design. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Extensive experience delivering systems software, platform integration, solution architecture, or customer engineering for large-scale enterprise, cloud, data-center, or edge environments, with deep expertise in heterogeneous computing across CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, networking, storage, memory subsystems, virtualization, and cloud infrastructure. Strong knowledge of Linux kernel architecture, drivers, system calls, memory management, I/O, networking stacks, security mechanisms, performance tooling, and upstream development practices, plus hands-on experience with runtime services, compilers, language runtimes, system libraries, containers, Kubernetes, distributed schedulers, observability, CI/CD, and software supply chains. Strong database and data-platform expertise spanning relational, NoSQL, analytical, vector, graph, caching, messaging, and distributed storage technologies, including performance and scale-out optimization. Experience designing and integrating REST, gRPC, event-driven, and systems-level APIs, with attention to compatibility, security, observability, versioning, and developer experience, along with working knowledge of Model Context Protocol (MCP), including server, client, tool, resource, authentication, and enterprise integration patterns. Strong programming skills in C, C++, Python, Go, Rust, or comparable systems languages, with comfort in performance-critical paths, profiling, debugging, and production-quality open-source development. Experience with ROCm™, AMD Zen Software Studio, AMD Enterprise AI, or comparable accelerator, compiler, runtime, and developer-tool ecosystems is desirable; practical familiarity with AI infrastructure, model serving, retrieval-augmented applications, vector databases, and inference performance is beneficial, but broad systems integration depth is more important than specialization in AI. Demonstrated technical leadership with customers, hyperscalers, OEMs, ISVs, standards groups, and open-source communities, supported by shipped solutions, upstream contributions, patents, publications, or conference presentations. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline; equivalent advanced industry experience may be considered. This is a highly technical, hands-on individual contributor role focused on architecture, integration, implementation, performance engineering, and ecosystem leadership. It is not a people management, program management, or alliance management position. THE PERSON: A deeply technical solution engineer and systems architect with broad expertise across operating systems, kernel and driver interfaces, runtime services, databases, distributed systems, APIs, cloud-native infrastructure, heterogeneous computing, networking, storage, virtualization, security, and performance engineering. This individual has a record of turning platform capabilities into integrated, supportable solutions that customers and open-source communities can deploy at scale. The ideal candidate understands how applications move through API, middleware, runtime, kernel, driver, firmware, and hardware layers, and how data moves across transactional databases, analytical platforms, caches, object stores, and retrieval systems. They can diagnose integration barriers, contribute production-quality code, shape stable interfaces, and optimize end-to-end behavior across AMD and third-party components. Familiarity with practical AI infrastructure, model serving, vector search, and MCP-enabled tools is valuable where these technologies intersect with broader platform solutions. This individual thrives in customer-facing and community-facing environments where long-term technical direction must be grounded in working code, benchmarks, upstream collaboration, and repeatable deployment outcomes. They lead through technical excellence and influence while partnering across engineering organizations and engaging directly with strategic customers, cloud providers, OEMs, ISVs, database vendors, operating-system communities, and standards organizations. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Define and execute AMD's solution engineering strategy for integrating AMD hardware and software into open-source, commercial, enterprise, cloud, and edge ecosystems, creating end-to-end reference architectures, reusable components, integration guides, validated configurations, and customer proof-of-concepts spanning AMD CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, networking, memory, storage, and accelerators. Drive enablement and upstream collaboration across Linux kernels, device drivers, firmware interfaces, system libraries, package ecosystems, container runtimes, Kubernetes, schedulers, service meshes, and observability platforms, and optimize runtime services—including language runtimes, compilers, libraries, inference and data-processing frameworks, communication stacks, and background system services—for AMD architectures. Integrate and optimize relational, NoSQL, analytical, vector, graph, and distributed database platforms on AMD systems, addressing query execution, concurrency, memory hierarchy, storage I/O, networking, resiliency, and scale-out performance. Design stable, secure, high-performance APIs and SDK integration patterns that expose AMD platform capabilities while simplifying application portability and developer adoption, and develop MCP servers, connectors, and reference patterns where MCP provides a practical interface between developer tools, enterprise data, platform services, and selected AI-assisted workflows. Support both AMD + AMD (A+A) and AMD + NVIDIA (A+N) deployment models, improving interoperability, workload portability, operational consistency, and customer choice. Apply rigorous profiling, benchmarking, tracing, and systems analysis to improve latency, throughput, scalability, availability, energy efficiency, total cost of ownership, and quality of service. Build security into solution architectures through confidential computing, trusted execution, attestation, identity, secure boot, software supply-chain controls, cryptography, data protection, governance, and auditability. Enable practical AI workloads where relevant, including model serving, retrieval, vector search, data pipelines, and developer productivity, without making AI the sole focus of the platform solution. Partner directly with strategic customers, hyperscalers, OEMs, ISVs, database and platform vendors, and open-source maintainers to resolve integration barriers and validate production readiness, translating implementation findings and ecosystem requirements into actionable feedback for AMD silicon, firmware, compiler, operating-system, runtime, library, and product roadmaps. Represent AMD through technical publications, conferences, standards bodies, upstream contributions, architecture reviews, and executive customer engagements, and mentor senior engineers and architects in systems integration, open-source engagement, performance engineering, and production solution design. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Extensive experience delivering systems software, platform integration, solution architecture, or customer engineering for large-scale enterprise, cloud, data-center, or edge environments, with deep expertise in heterogeneous computing across CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, networking, storage, memory subsystems, virtualization, and cloud infrastructure. Strong knowledge of Linux kernel architecture, drivers, system calls, memory management, I/O, networking stacks, security mechanisms, performance tooling, and upstream development practices, plus hands-on experience with runtime services, compilers, language runtimes, system libraries, containers, Kubernetes, distributed schedulers, observability, CI/CD, and software supply chains. Strong database and data-platform expertise spanning relational, NoSQL, analytical, vector, graph, caching, messaging, and distributed storage technologies, including performance and scale-out optimization. Experience designing and integrating REST, gRPC, event-driven, and systems-level APIs, with attention to compatibility, security, observability, versioning, and developer experience, along with working knowledge of Model Context Protocol (MCP), including server, client, tool, resource, authentication, and enterprise integration patterns. Strong programming skills in C, C++, Python, Go, Rust, or comparable systems languages, with comfort in performance-critical paths, profiling, debugging, and production-quality open-source development. Experience with ROCm™, AMD Zen Software Studio, AMD Enterprise AI, or comparable accelerator, compiler, runtime, and developer-tool ecosystems is desirable; practical familiarity with AI infrastructure, model serving, retrieval-augmented applications, vector databases, and inference performance is beneficial, but broad systems integration depth is more important than specialization in AI. Demonstrated technical leadership with customers, hyperscalers, OEMs, ISVs, standards groups, and open-source communities, supported by shipped solutions, upstream contributions, patents, publications, or conference presentations. THE ROLE AMD is looking for a hands-on research engineer to advance life sciences computing at the intersection of computational biology, AI, and high-performance computing. You will investigate emerging scientific workloads, develop and optimize algorithms, and build software that enables researchers to tackle larger and more complex biological problems on AMD platforms. Areas of interest include genomics, biological foundation models, protein and molecular modeling, and computational drug discovery. Working with AMD researchers, software engineers, and external collaborators, you will take projects from scientific problem definition through implementation and evaluation. Your findings will help identify where AMD can deliver meaningful advances in life sciences computing and guide future research and software investments. THE PERSON You bring deep understanding of a computational life sciences domain and the programming skills to turn scientific ideas into working software. You enjoy writing code, testing hypotheses, and solving difficult technical problems. You can distinguish improvements that matter to a scientific workflow from gains in an isolated benchmark and communicate your findings clearly to both domain scientists and systems engineers. We value depth in one or more relevant areas, curiosity across disciplines, and the ability to take ownership of a technical project from investigation to validated results. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Investigate important and emerging life sciences workloads, understanding their scientific objectives, algorithms, computational requirements, and practical limitations. Develop, implement, and evaluate algorithms and AI methods for applications in genomics, biomolecular modeling, or related areas. Profile and optimize scientific applications and AI workflows on AMD platforms, addressing bottlenecks in computation, memory, data processing, and communication. Explore algorithmic reformulations, parallelization strategies, numerical precision, and GPU acceleration while preserving scientific validity. Build reproducible benchmarks that measure end-to-end performance, scalability, resource use, and relevant scientific outcomes. Work directly with academic and industry collaborators to translate scientific needs into technical requirements and working implementations. Contribute reusable software, optimized operators, and improvements to relevant open-source projects. Translate experimental findings into recommendations for AMD’s research priorities, software capabilities, and hardware requirements. Communicate results through technical reports, demonstrations, publications, and invention disclosures, as appropriate. REQUIRED EXPERIENCE Strong computational expertise in at least one life sciences area, such as computational genomics, bioinformatics, protein modeling, computational chemistry, or molecular simulation. Hands-on experience implementing scientific algorithms or developing machine learning models for biological applications. Strong programming skills in Python and experience with C++ or another language used for high-performance scientific computing. Solid understanding of algorithms, data structures, numerical methods, and experimental evaluation. Experience profiling, debugging, and improving computational software. Ability to work independently on a defined technical problem and collaborate effectively across scientific and engineering disciplines. Clear written and verbal communication skills. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE Biological foundation models, protein structure prediction or design, molecular generative models, or genomic sequence modeling. Scientific AI architectures, including transformers, geometric deep learning, graph neural networks, or diffusion models. GPU programming and optimization using HIP, CUDA, Triton, or comparable technologies. Deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, including custom operators or distributed training and inference. Parallel algorithms, multi-GPU computing, or large-scale scientific workflows. Established life sciences software ecosystems and experience extending or contributing to open-source tools. Research contributions demonstrated through publications, software, patents, or deployed scientific applications. amd-89280.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology can change lives for the better. It can heal us, entertain us, and make us more connected, productive, and understanding of the world around us. And we’re looking for talent who feel the same: people who want to leave the planet better than they found it, those who don’t shy away from humanity’s challenges but are determined to help solve them. AMD is powering the next generation of supercomputing, high-performance computing, cloud, and AI. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or creating go-to-market plans, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. THE ROLE: AMD is seeking a Senior Manager, Graphics Productization to lead a highly talented team responsible for transforming innovative graphics technologies into world-class products that reach millions of users. This leader will play a critical role in bridging advanced graphics research and commercial product delivery, ensuring new technologies are successfully integrated into AMD's graphics software and platform ecosystem. In this role, you will collaborate with researchers, software engineers, architects, technical leaders, and product teams across AMD to drive the successful delivery of next-generation graphics capabilities. You will help shape the future of Radeon graphics technologies, including AI-enhanced graphics, rendering innovations, and graphics software releases, while leading a globally distributed team focused on delivering high-quality experiences to customers worldwide. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a passionate engineering leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys turning innovative ideas into shipping products. You are a strong communicator who can align diverse technical teams, influence stakeholders, and build high-performing organizations focused on execution and delivery. You are equally comfortable discussing graphics technologies, software development processes, release execution, and organizational strategy. You value collaboration, mentorship, accountability, and developing talent while fostering an environment that empowers teams to innovate and deliver. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead AMD's graphics productization efforts, driving the successful transition of graphics innovations, SDKs, and proof-of-concepts into production-ready software and platform features. Build, lead, and develop a high-performing organization responsible for graphics software delivery and release execution. Collaborate closely with graphics researchers, GPU architects, software engineering teams, ISVs, and ecosystem partners to ensure successful feature adoption and deployment. Drive execution of key graphics initiatives, ensuring roadmap commitments are delivered with high quality and on schedule. Establish scalable engineering processes, release practices, and operational excellence across the organization. Mentor technical leaders and managers while fostering a culture focused on innovation, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Within the first 90 days, establish strong partnerships across the graphics organization, gain deep understanding of current productization programs, and assume ownership of key delivery milestones. Drive long-term success by scaling graphics productization capabilities and enabling the successful delivery of future Radeon technologies and software releases. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience leading graphics software, graphics engineering, rendering, gaming, GPU, or related technology organizations. Strong understanding of graphics pipelines, rendering technologies, GPU software, or graphics SDK development. Experience delivering complex software releases and coordinating execution across multiple engineering organizations. Demonstrated success leading large engineering teams and developing technical leaders. Experience working with external ecosystem partners, game studios, ISVs, or industry organizations. Knowledge of AI-assisted graphics technologies, machine learning applications, or advanced rendering techniques. Experience in semiconductor, graphics, gaming, or high-performance computing industries. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor's degree is preferred in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Graphics, or a related technical field. Master's degree or PhD desired. You will be a member of a core team of incredibly talented industry specialists and will work with the very latest hardware and software technology. THE PERSON: We are seeking a Software Optimization Engineer with deep experience improving real‑world browser performance in Chromium‑based browsers. In this role, you will focus on identifying, analyzing, and resolving performance bottlenecks across the Chromium stack, working close to the browser engine, OS, and hardware. This position is ideal for an engineer who enjoys low‑level performance analysis, system‑level optimization, and collaborative work with browser, OS, and silicon teams to deliver measurable user‑visible gains. Key Responsibilities Profile and optimize performance across Chromium subsystems, including Blink, V8, Skia, GPU/ANGLE, and browser multi‑process architecture Identify CPU, memory, GPU, and power bottlenecks using real workloads, benchmarks, and field telemetry Implement performance improvements in areas such as page load, rendering, JavaScript execution, graphics/compositing, and browser responsiveness Drive optimizations across platforms (Windows primary; Linux/macOS experience a plus), including interactions with OS schedulers, graphics stacks, and drivers Analyze performance using industry‑standard and custom tools (e.g., Perfetto, ETW, Chrome Tracing, VTune, PIX, GPUView, perf) Collaborate with browser vendors, OS teams, compiler teams, and hardware partners to co‑optimize software and platforms Contribute clean, well‑reviewed patches upstream to Chromium or downstream forks as appropriate Translate benchmark and microarchitectural findings into practical, scalable browser improvements Document performance investigations, results, and best practices; communicate findings clearly to technical stakeholders software engineering experience, with a strong focus on performance optimization Hands‑on experience working with Chromium or Chromium‑based browsers (e.g., Chrome, Edge, internal forks) Strong proficiency in C++ and modern C++ performance best practices Deep understanding of browser internals, including at least two of the following: Rendering pipeline (Blink lifecycle, style/layout/paint) JavaScript engines (V8 internals, JIT behavior, GC) Graphics and compositing (Skia, GPU rasterization, ANGLE, WebGL) Multiprocess/threading model and IPC in Chromium Proven experience using low‑level profiling and tracing tools to drive optimizations Strong debugging skills across large, complex codebases Ability to reason from microarchitectural behavior (cache, memory, SIMD, branch behavior) up to user‑perceived performance Preferred Qualifications Experience as an active Chromium contributor or committer, with a track record of upstream contributions, code reviews, and accepted patches to Chromium projects such as Blink, V8, Skia, ANGLE, or related components. amd-87873.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: We are hiring AI Engineers to build recursive self-improvement systems for compute. This role sits at the intersection of AI systems, performance engineering, hardware-aware optimization, and agentic software development. You will help build systems where AI proposes improvements, verifies correctness, measures impact, learns from failures, and improves the next generation of compute workloads and platforms. The work requires turning complex engineering tasks into repeatable optimization loops with clear inputs, candidate generation, automated validation, measurable scoring, and reliable iteration. You will work on problems where feedback may be expensive, correctness is non-negotiable, and small improvements can have large impact at scale. THE PERSON: You are a hands-on engineer who can move between modern AI methods, systems performance, and hardware-aware workflows. You are comfortable with fast-moving AI research, but you care most about measurable outcomes: correctness, speed, efficiency, quality, reproducibility, and engineering leverage. You can collaborate with research scientists, hardware engineers, software engineers, and external technical partners while keeping an end-to-end loop working. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Build agentic and learning-driven optimization loops for compute workloads and hardware engineering workflows. Develop systems that generate, compile, test, benchmark, profile, and iterate on candidate improvements with minimal human intervention. Convert high-value engineering workflows into verifiable tasks with clear graders, harnesses, metrics, and failure feedback. Collaborate with AI researchers on reward design, reward shaping, reward hacking analysis, long-horizon optimization, and model improvement loops. Design feedback systems that accumulate useful data from successful attempts, failed attempts, profiler traces, benchmark results, and validation logs. Improve iteration speed through staged validation, caching, parallel execution, proxy metrics, and faster feedback paths. Build reusable tools and patterns that can generalize across multiple compute and hardware optimization domains. Mentor other engineers and help set technical direction for self-improving AI systems for compute. TECHNICAL FOCUS AREAS: AI-assisted program optimization, code generation, debugging, and automated repair. GPU and CPU performance engineering, including kernels, libraries, compilers, profilers, and benchmark-driven optimization. Agentic workflows that use tools, tests, simulators, profilers, and structured feedback to improve over time. Reinforcement learning, post-training, reward modeling, and evaluation methods for engineering tasks. Hardware-aware optimization where correctness, latency, throughput, area, power, timing, or resource usage may all matter. Experiment platforms, leaderboards, dashboards, and data pipelines for reproducible comparison and continuous improvement. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Strong software engineering experience in Python and at least one systems language such as C++, C, HIP, CUDA. Experience building AI, ML, agentic, optimization, or automation systems that are evaluated with objective metrics. Ability to design reliable experiment loops, benchmark harnesses, validation workflows, and correctness/performance evaluation pipelines. Strong technical judgment in debugging, profiling, root-cause analysis, and performance-oriented iteration. Clear communication skills and ability to work across AI research, hardware, software, and partner-facing teams. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience with GPU kernels, ROCm/HIP, CUDA, Triton, PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, or distributed training/inference systems. Experience with reinforcement learning, post-training, reward modeling, automated program optimization, or agentic coding systems. Familiarity with CPU performance engineering, compiler optimization, benchmarking, profiling, or math libraries. Exposure to hardware design, simulation, formal verification, performance/power/area analysis, or hardware/software co-design. Experience building production-quality evaluation platforms, experiment tracking, dashboards, or leaderboards. Publications, open-source contributions, or shipped systems in AI systems, GPU computing, compilers, RL, or hardware/software co-design are a plus. EDUCATION Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or related field, or equivalent practical experience. Master's preferred; PhD is a plus, especially in AI systems, reinforcement learning, compilers, GPU computing, or hardware/software co-design. amd-88589.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology can change lives for the better. It can heal us, entertain us, and make us more connected, productive, and understanding of the world around us. And we’re looking for talent who feel the same: people who want to leave the planet better than they found it, those who don’t shy away from humanity’s challenges but are determined to help solve them. AMD is powering the next generation of supercomputing, high-performance computing, cloud, and AI. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or creating go-to-market plans, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. THE ROLE This role focuses on leading system-level, rack-level, and cluster-scale validation for next-generation AI and machine learning platforms. You will define validation strategies, drive technical direction, and lead complex validation initiatives across hardware, firmware, software, and infrastructure domains. You will work closely with architecture, platform engineering, silicon design, firmware, software, and deployment teams to ensure product quality, reliability, and deployment readiness at scale. The role requires deep technical expertise, strong analytical skills, and the ability to influence technical decisions across multiple engineering organizations. You will be responsible for establishing validation methodologies, driving execution across large-scale validation environments, and identifying quality risks that impact product readiness and customer deployments. THE PERSON You are a technical leader with extensive experience in system-level validation and large-scale server platforms. You thrive on solving complex technical problems, driving cross-functional initiatives, and defining scalable validation approaches for emerging technologies. You are comfortable operating with minimal supervision while providing technical leadership across engineering teams. You possess strong debugging skills, sound technical judgment, and a deep understanding of hardware-software interactions. You proactively identify technical risks, drive resolution of complex platform issues, and influence engineering decisions that improve product quality, validation effectiveness, and deployment readiness. You are passionate about mentoring engineers and elevating engineering excellence across the organization. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Lead system-level, rack-level, and cluster-scale validation strategy for AI and machine learning server platforms. Define and drive comprehensive validation plans covering customer deployment scenarios across scale-up and scale-out environments. Develop validation methodologies and test strategies spanning CPU, GPU, memory, BIOS, BMC, networking, storage, platform firmware, operating systems, and infrastructure components. Collaborate with architecture, hardware, firmware, software, and platform engineering teams to define validation requirements, identify coverage gaps, and improve overall product quality. Lead investigation and root cause analysis of complex hardware, firmware, software, networking, and system integration issues. Drive technical decision-making within the validation organization and influence cross-functional teams to resolve critical product risks and quality concerns. Define and enhance scalable validation frameworks, automation infrastructure, telemetry-driven workflows, and data-driven validation methodologies. Analyze large-scale validation data to identify systemic failures, reliability risks, performance bottlenecks, and product readiness concerns. Establish validation readiness criteria, quality metrics, and coverage strategies that improve execution efficiency and provide early risk identification. Mentor and provide technical leadership to engineers, helping improve validation methodologies, automation capabilities, debugging effectiveness, and system-level engineering practices. Drive execution across multiple validation programs while managing priorities, dependencies, schedules, and technical risks. Communicate validation status, readiness assessments, quality metrics, technical recommendations, and key risks to senior technical leadership and management. Support customer-focused validation efforts by ensuring test environments accurately represent real-world deployment conditions and hyperscale operating environments. Drive continuous improvements in validation processes, tools, and automation to improve organizational efficiency, test coverage, and product quality. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE 8+ years of experience in system-level validation, platform validation, post-silicon validation, large-scale infrastructure validation, or related engineering disciplines. Proven experience validating large-scale server, AI, cloud, HPC, or data center platforms. Demonstrated ability to lead investigation and resolution of complex hardware, firmware, software, networking, and infrastructure issues. Experience validating scale-up and scale-out architectures, including rack-scale and cluster-scale deployments. Deep understanding of computer architecture, server platform design, operating systems, networking, storage, and hardware/software interactions. Experience developing automated validation frameworks, orchestration systems, and large-scale test infrastructure. Strong proficiency in Python and Linux environments, with working knowledge of Bash and/or PowerShell. Experience leveraging telemetry, analytics, and data-driven methodologies to improve validation coverage, efficiency, and root cause analysis. Familiarity with AI, machine learning, GPU computing, or accelerated computing environments deployed in data center infrastructures. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional technical initiatives and influence engineering decisions across organizational boundaries. Experience mentoring engineers and driving technical excellence within validation and product engineering organizations. Experience supporting product readiness, customer deployment validation, and release qualification activities. Strong communication skills with the ability to convey technical risks, recommendations, and status to executive and technical leadership. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent. Write test plans, review them with all stakeholders to cover the scenarios comprehensively, and execute them efficiently. Build maintainable, high-quality and effective automated test scripts. Strong experience in firmware test and automation roles. Solid understanding of AI tools and how to leverage them in a large-scale distributed environment. Proficiency in writing automation scripts in Python, and experience with test and performance-testing tools. Solid understanding of automation frameworks, and fluency in Python. Prior experience with cloud, security and data center technologies is an added advantage. Strong troubleshooting skills. Knowledge of operating systems, kernel-mode programming, device drivers, and related technologies and architectures. Good interpersonal and communication skills. Ability to write high-quality automation code with keen attention to detail. Good understanding of the Linux operating system and hypervisors (VMware ESX, KVM). Experience with software development processes and tools such as debuggers, source code control systems (GitHub) and profilers is a plus. Track record of defining test strategy and release quality gates, and of building automation frameworks used across teams. Experience leading customer escalations and influencing development teams and leadership. Experience testing firmware on CPU, GPU or SoC platforms at scale, including AI workloads on multi-node clusters, is a strong plus. This executive leadership role will build and lead a team of Forward Deployed Engineers who work directly with customer engineering organizations to deploy, integrate, optimize, and scale AMD datacenter GPU platforms and software solutions. The Director will own the technical engagement model across a portfolio of customers, guiding deployments from early architecture and proof-of-concept through cluster bring-up, workload enablement, production readiness, and operational scale. This role will drive alignment across customer engineering teams and AMD Software, Hardware, Product Management, Business Development, Operations, and Support organizations to resolve deployment barriers, accelerate time-to-value, and translate field experience into product and platform improvements. They combine deep technical understanding of GPU-based computing, distributed systems, AI software stacks, and production infrastructure with strong organizational leadership, executive communication, and customer relationship skills. They thrive in ambiguous and fast-moving environments, build credibility with customer executives and hands-on engineering teams alike, and lead through influence across large cross-functional organizations. They can balance immediate customer deployment needs with scalable engineering practices, while using real-world customer experience to improve AMD products, software, support models, and future platform strategies. KEY RESPONSIBILITES: Lead and develop a globally distributed team of Forward Deployed Engineers supporting AMD's strategic customers, cloud service provider, hyperscale, and AI infrastructure customers. Own the technical engagement strategy for assigned Mega Data Center and Cloud Service Provider accounts, aligning engineering resources to customer architecture, deployment priorities, workload requirements, and production milestones. Partner with internal and external stakeholders, drive end-to-end customer deployment execution from discovery, architecture definition, and proof-of-concept through cluster bring-up, software integration, workload enablement, performance optimization, production readiness, and operational scale. Build trusted relationships with customer engineering leaders, architects, platform teams, and executive stakeholders, serving as the senior technical escalation and coordination point for business-critical deployments. Lead resolution of complex, cross-stack issues spanning GPU hardware, firmware, ROCm software, AI frameworks, networking, storage, cluster management, orchestration, reliability, and workload performance. Partner with Product Management, Business Development, Pre-sales, Operations, and Support teams to deliver customer commitments and maintain clear ownership of technical risks, dependencies, and mitigation plans. Serve as the voice of the customer within AMD, converting deployment friction, feature gaps, and emerging workload requirements into actionable product feedback and roadmap priorities. Develop reusable deployment patterns, reference architectures, automation, technical playbooks, readiness criteria, and operating mechanisms that improve execution consistency across accounts. Define and track engineering and customer success metrics, including time-to-deployment, production readiness, workload enablement, performance, utilization, reliability, issue-resolution effectiveness, and expansion readiness. Lead executive deployment reviews and technical health assessments, clearly communicating customer status, engineering risks, decisions, dependencies, and recovery plans. Scale the Cluster FDE operating model through workforce planning, talent development, technical mentorship, account coverage models, and strong collaboration with regional and centralized engineering teams. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Proven track record in customer-facing engineering, forward deployed engineering, solutions architecture, software engineering, systems engineering, or technical leadership roles supporting complex datacenter or cloud environments. Proven success leading and scaling engineering teams responsible for customer deployment, technical integration, production adoption, or operational enablement. Demonstrated experience working directly with MDC providers, cloud service providers, hyperscalers, AI infrastructure companies, OEMs, ODMs, and enterprise customers. Deep understanding of large-scale GPU deployments, AI training and inference environments, distributed systems, datacenter operations, server architecture, networking, storage, Linux, Kubernetes, containers, and performance optimization. Proven ability to lead complex customer deployments from proof-of-concept through production scale while managing technical risk, cross-functional dependencies, and executive expectations. Demonstrated ability to translate customer deployment experience into engineering priorities, product improvements, reusable solutions, and roadmap recommendations. Strong executive presence with experience influencing customer and internal leadership teams across engineering, product, operations, support, and commercial organizations. Exceptional written, verbal, technical, and executive communication skills. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related technical field; advanced degree preferred. Solid years of relevant experience in engineering leadership, software engineering, solutions architecture, customer engineering, forward deployed engineering, technical program management, or related technical leadership roles. THE TEAM: The Competitive Advanced Performance (CAP) team is a new, visible capability focused on predicting, validating and explaining competitive server CPU performance before products reach the market. Joining now means helping define the methods, tools and operating model from the ground up. THE ROLE: AMD is seeking a data scientist and performance engineer to own the quantitative forecasting system behind the CAP team. You will combine architecture assumptions, workload measurements, software trends, platform data and partner validation into forward-looking predictions with explicit confidence ranges. The role is accountable for model error, scenario analysis, forecast-versus-actual learning and a clear competitive narrative: where AMD is likely to lead, where it may face risk, how confident the team is and which variables could change the outcome. THE PERSON: You are neither a pure data scientist who treats performance data as opaque features nor a benchmark engineer who reports only point results. You understand enough CPU and system performance to model causality, and enough statistics to avoid false precision. You care about provenance, versioning and calibration, and you can make uncertainty understandable to engineers and executives. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Design and maintain a forecasting framework that links CPU architecture, memory, I/O, power, operating-system and runtime behavior, and workload kernels. Create performance, performance-per-watt and price-performance forecasts with confidence ranges rather than single-point estimates. Build scenarios for uncertain competitor attributes such as frequency, core count, memory bandwidth, software maturity, launch timing and platform power. Track prediction error by workload, competitor, forecast horizon and model version; decompose errors and tune the model as measured systems become available. Develop normalized competitive scorecards across workload performance, efficiency and TCO, memory and I/O, software ecosystem, deployability and roadmap credibility. Fuse benchmark results, performance counters, partner telemetry, public roadmaps, software changes and platform evidence while preserving source provenance. Identify leading indicators that materially change the forecast and surface early risk or opportunity signals. Partner with architecture and workload leads to design experiments that reduce the most valuable uncertainties. Build executive-grade visualizations of deltas, confidence ranges, scenarios, drivers and forecast-versus-actual history. Write quarterly forecast narratives and support rapid recalibration when new silicon or material evidence appears. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Demonstrated experience building quantitative models used for technical or business decisions under uncertainty. Strong programming and data-analysis skills in Python or an equivalent analytical environment. Expertise in defining meaningful error metrics, calibration methods and sensitivity analyses for sparse or biased data. Working knowledge of server CPU and system performance and a willingness to engage deeply with architectural causality. Experience with reproducible data pipelines, versioning, notebooks or scripts, and source provenance. Strong visualization, writing and presentation skills for technical and executive audiences. Sound judgment about when a model is useful, when it is overfit and when the available evidence does not support a precise conclusion. CPU or GPU performance prediction, pre-silicon modeling, capacity planning, forecasting or benchmark analytics. Bayesian modeling, Monte Carlo simulation, probabilistic programming or uncertainty quantification. Experience combining structured benchmark data with semi-structured roadmap, software-change or market evidence. Cross-ISA or cloud-instance price-performance analysis. Familiarity with platform economics, TCO, rack power or density. WHY THIS OPPORTUNITY STANDS OUT: Build the quantitative engine at the center of a new technical organization. Make uncertainty actionable instead of hiding it behind a single number. Work with architects and workload experts who can test model assumptions against real systems. Create a visible body of work that connects data science directly to product and architecture decisions. Build scenarios for uncertain competitor attributes such as frequency, core count, memory bandwidth, software maturity, launch timing and platform power. Track prediction error by workload, competitor, forecast horizon and model version; decompose errors and tune the model as measured systems become available. Develop normalized competitive scorecards across workload performance, efficiency and TCO, memory and I/O, software ecosystem, deployability and roadmap credibility. Fuse benchmark results, performance counters, partner telemetry, public roadmaps, software changes and platform evidence while preserving source provenance. Identify leading indicators that materially change the forecast and surface early risk or opportunity signals. Partner with architecture and workload leads to design experiments that reduce the most valuable uncertainties. Build executive-grade visualizations of deltas, confidence ranges, scenarios, drivers and forecast-versus-actual history. Write quarterly forecast narratives and support rapid recalibration when new silicon or material evidence appears. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Demonstrated experience building quantitative models used for technical or business decisions under uncertainty. Strong programming and data-analysis skills in Python or an equivalent analytical environment. Expertise in defining meaningful error metrics, calibration methods and sensitivity analyses for sparse or biased data. Working knowledge of server CPU and system performance and a willingness to engage deeply with architectural causality. Experience with reproducible data pipelines, versioning, notebooks or scripts, and source provenance. Strong visualization, writing and presentation skills for technical and executive audiences. Sound judgment about when a model is useful, when it is overfit and when the available evidence does not support a precise conclusion. CPU or GPU performance prediction, pre-silicon modeling, capacity planning, forecasting or benchmark analytics. Bayesian modeling, Monte Carlo simulation, probabilistic programming or uncertainty quantification. Experience combining structured benchmark data with semi-structured roadmap, software-change or market evidence. Cross-ISA or cloud-instance price-performance analysis. Familiarity with platform economics, TCO, rack power or density. WHY THIS OPPORTUNITY STANDS OUT: Build the quantitative engine at the center of a new technical organization. Make uncertainty actionable instead of hiding it behind a single number. Work with architects and workload experts who can test model assumptions against real systems. Create a visible body of work that connects data science directly to product and architecture decisions. THE ROLE: Help bring to life the foundational FPGA and adaptive SoC platforms enabling the next generation of physical AI and advanced embedded applications. Join our team to own embedded designs for post-silicon system-level validation and board bring-up for FPGA and SoC-based platforms. The work spans networking, storage, automotive, aerospace, and emerging AI/ML workloads. You'll be a senior individual contributor writing firmware and software for taking new boards from first power-on to a stable, validated platform. You'll set the technical direction for how we validate, debug, and sign off silicon-to-solution across hardware and software. THE PERSON: You understand how firmware, silicon, and hardware interact, and you can follow a failure across all three. You bring deep hands-on hardware bring-up and validation experience, strong analytical instincts, and the judgment to know what production readiness looks like for a platform. You work well with global teams, communicate clearly, and you go looking for the hard, ambiguous problems rather than around them. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: System-Level Validation: Define and drive the silicon-to-solution validation strategy — plans, coverage, regression, and signoffs. Bring up baremetal and embedded Linux to exercise the full system. Write firmware and low-level system software for on-chip ARM (APU/RPU) or RISC-V cores. Build and customize embedded Linux images using the Yocto-based Embedded Design Flow (BSP configuration, device trees, kernel/rootfs tuning, custom recipes and layers). Board Bring-Up & Validation: Own new board bring-up from first power-on through a stable platform. Build the scripts, baremetal code, and debug flows the boards team needs to complete bring-up and validation. Test Development & Automation: Develop validation tests and applications in baremetal and Linux environments, and automate execution and regression to scale coverage. Debug: Debug complex issues that span silicon, firmware, drivers, and the operating system. Cross-Team Collaboration & Signoff: Partner with architecture, design, verification, software, product engineering, and board teams. Drive production readiness, issue tracking, risk assessment, and validation signoff. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Hands on embedded systems and hardware validation experience. Proven board bring-up and validation experience — taking a new board from power-on through boot and interface bring-up, and debugging clocking, reset, power, and hardware issues on the bench. Strong C/C++ for bare-metal and Linux-based embedded systems on ARM or RISC-V cores; Linux kernel-mode driver knowledge is a strong plus. Hands-on experience with AMD/Xilinx embedded Linux flows: building and customizing images with the Yocto-based Embedded Design Flow (BSPs, device trees, custom recipes/layers). Experience validating interfaces such as Ethernet, USB, plus common peripherals like SPI, I²C, UART, and CAN. Working knowledge of AMD/Xilinx Vitis and EDF environments. Comfortable automating in Python, Tcl, Shell, and Makefiles, with Git and structured CI/regression workflows. Strong ownership and communication, with a track record of technical leadership and mentoring. THE ROLE AMD is seeking an experienced Test Engineer to develop and advance wafer-sort test infrastructure on Advantest V93000 platforms using SmarTest 8. In this highly visible role, you will contribute to AMD’s common Base Test Program and Test Shell. You will have the opportunity to influence test strategy across the full product lifecycle—from first-silicon bring-up and characterization through production release and high-volume manufacturing. Your work will directly improve test quality, yield, test time, scalability, and release readiness for next-generation microprocessor and chiplet products. THE PERSON You are a hands-on ATE Test Engineer with deep experience developing and debugging test programs on Advantest V93000 platforms. You understand how silicon, test software, tester and probe hardware, patterns, timing, and manufacturing processes interact. You bring strong technical judgment, disciplined software-development practices, and the ability to lead complex debug efforts across global teams. You are an effective communicator and mentor who can influence infrastructure strategy across products and organizations. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Develop and integrate reusable wafer-sort Base Test Program and common Test Shell infrastructure, including test flows, services, configurations, diagnostics, data collection, and release controls. Lead SmarTest 8 and Advantest V93000 test program development, debug, validation, release readiness, and production support. Drive wafer-sort strategy, first-silicon bring-up, characterization, margining, screening and diagnostics. Integrate patterns, timing, levels, test methods, device configurations, binning, and debug capabilities into the common test program. Troubleshoot complex interactions across silicon, test software, tester and probe hardware, patterns, timing, and manufacturing processes. Partner with Design, Design for Test, Product Engineering, Yield Engineering, Test Hardware, and Manufacturing teams to improve coverage, testability, yield, test time, and product quality. Define scalable architecture and coding practices that enable reuse across products, silicon revisions, test insertions, and manufacturing sites. Lead technical reviews, document architectural decisions, mentor engineers, and support global engineering teams, manufacturing partners, and equipment vendors. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE Extensive Advantest V93000 test program development and debug experience, including SmarTest 8. Proficiency in Java and at least one additional language, such as C++, Python, Perl, or shell scripting. Experience developing test flows, methods, patterns, timing, levels, diagnostics, characterization plans, and manufacturing screens. Experience leading or making significant architectural contributions to a Base Test Program, common Test Shell, or similar shared ATE infrastructure. Linux or Unix proficiency, including revision control and disciplined software-release practices. Experience with ORE or comparable offline simulation tools. Knowledge of technologies such as PCIe, CXL, UCIe, Ethernet, JESD204, USB, DDR, HBM PHY, xGMI/Infinity Fabric, UPI, or NVLink. Experience with link training, equalization, lane-level diagnostics, bit-error-rate testing, jitter analysis, voltage and timing margining, or ATE-to-bench correlation. Knowledge of chiplet architectures, 2.5D/3D packaging, interposers, bridges, and known-good-die considerations. Experience using AI-enabled or agentic workflows to improve test development, debug, validation, documentation, or engineering productivity. Strong communication skills and demonstrated success leading and collaborating across geographically distributed teams. The candidate must be organized, self-motivated and able to work effectively on teams large and small across multiple sites. Strong verbal and written communication skills are essential for driving technical discussions to successful and actionable outcomes. Own and drive power modeling effort for CG. It can heal us, entertain us, and make us more connected, productive, and understanding of the world around us. And we’re looking for talent who feel the same: people who want to leave the planet better than they found it, those who don’t shy away from humanity’s challenges but are determined to help solve them. AMD is powering the next generation of supercomputing, high-performance computing, cloud, and AI. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or creating go-to-market plans, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. THE ROLE: Our Data Center GPU Validation and Engineering team ensures the quality, reliability, security, and performance of AMD's industry-leading AI, ML, and HPC products. Working closely with architecture, design, product engineering, software, and hardware teams, we develop the validation methodologies, automation frameworks, emulation strategies, and debug capabilities that enable successful silicon bring-up, product readiness, and deliver exceptional customer quality. Validation Architects play a key role in shaping future products by driving design-for-validation requirements and advancing scalable validation solutions for increasingly complex AI and data center platforms. THE PERSON: We are seeking an experienced Validation Architect with deep expertise in GPU, SoC, and data center platform validation to help define the validation strategy for AMD's next-generation AI and HPC products. The ideal candidate combines strong architectural thinking with hands-on validation and debug experience, and has a proven ability to influence and technical direction across engineering organizations. Success in this role requires exceptional problem-solving, communication, and leadership skills, along with a passion for innovation, continuous improvement, and delivering world-class product quality. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Define and evolve AMD's validation strategy for next-generation AI, ML, and HPC accelerators, establishing scalable methodologies, coverage models, and validation frameworks that improve product quality and reduce time-to-market. Drive validation innovation across the product lifecycle, influencing observability, controllability, debuggability, emulation, and automation capabilities to enable more efficient validation and faster root-cause analysis. Provide architectural leadership for complex silicon and platform challenges, guiding resolution of issues involving coherency, memory subsystems, power management, security, PCIe, and HW/SW interactions while advancing debug methodologies and infrastructure. Partner with silicon architects and technical leaders across engineering organizations to develop validation approaches for emerging technologies, including advanced GPU architectures, HBM memory systems, coherent interconnects, and large-scale AI infrastructure. Champion the adoption of modern technologies and best practices, including AI-assisted validation workflows, at-scale validation environments, and data-driven quality methodologies that improve execution efficiency and product readiness. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE Deep understanding of modern GPU, SoC, and server platform architectures, including experience with post-silicon bring-up, validation, system-level debug, and AI/ML accelerator or large-scale data center platform validation. Proven experience developing validation architectures, methodologies, test strategies, automation frameworks, and infrastructure for complex semiconductor products. Strong expertise in silicon and system-level debug across hardware and software domains, with the ability to drive resolution of technically challenging issues. Proficiency in programming and scripting languages such as C/C++ and Python, along with working knowledge of Linux and Windows server environments. Demonstrated ability to influence technical direction, build cross-functional partnerships, and communicate effectively with stakeholders ranging from engineers and architects to senior executives. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills with a passion for innovation, technical excellence, and continuous improvement. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT: Central DFX (CDFX) is a centralized ASIC design organization within AMD Technology and Engineering, with teams across North America and Asia. CDFX develops and standardizes Design-for-Test (DFT) and Design-for-Debug (DFD) architectures, methodologies, implementation flows and CAD automation for high-performance and adaptive-compute products serving data center, embedded, gaming and PC markets. THE ROLE: We are seeking an AI/ML Project Lead who combines deep DFT design and methodology expertise with hands-on experience developing production-quality AI solutions and agentic engineering workflows. This technical leadership role will define and drive a portfolio of AI-enabled capabilities that improve the productivity, quality, scalability and predictability of DFX design and verification flows. THE PERSON: You will partner with DFT, DFD, CAD, design, verification and software engineering teams to identify high-value use cases, translate engineering knowledge into deployable solutions, and lead projects from concept and prototype through production deployment, adoption and sustained operation. The role requires strong technical judgment across semiconductor design, AI/ML, software architecture and program execution. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead the strategy, roadmap and execution of AI/ML and agentic AI initiatives for DFT and DFD design, methodology, verification and debug workflows. Integrate AI agents and services with DFX design flows, EDA tools, repositories, specifications, regression systems and engineering data sources through secure, maintainable interfaces. Develop AI-enabled expert systems, predictive models and intelligent automation to address DFT challenges across IP, subsystem and SoC design environments. Maintain awareness of advancements in AI/ML, agentic systems and semiconductor design automation, and evaluate their relevance to AMD DFX needs. Identify and prioritize use cases based on measurable engineering value, technical feasibility, data readiness, deployment risk and opportunities for reuse across teams. Architect agentic workflows that combine large language models, domain knowledge, retrieval, tools, automation and human-in-the-loop controls to support complex engineering tasks. Establish evaluation methods, quality gates, guardrails, traceability and fallback mechanisms appropriate for production engineering workflows. Lead model and application deployment, monitoring, incident response, maintenance and continuous improvement using sound MLOps, DevOps and software lifecycle practices. Drive scalable DFT implementation and verification automation using Python, Perl, Tcl and shell scripting within complex ASIC design environments. THE ROLE: We are looking for an experienced RAS Architect (Reliability, Availability, and Serviceability) to help shape robust, resilient architectures for AMD products. In this role, you will define and develop system-level RAS capabilities that improve reliability, availability, and serviceability across complex computing systems and scale-out environments. You will collaborate with hardware engineers, system architects, software developers, vendors, and suppliers to identify potential failure modes and develop effective architectural solutions. Your work will span RAS requirements, reliability analysis, fault detection and recovery, redundancy, diagnostics, system-level validation, and product development from architecture through early customer support. THE PERSON: You approach complex system-level reliability challenges with strong analytical and problem-solving skills. You communicate technical concepts clearly and collaborate effectively across hardware and software disciplines. You are comfortable evaluating technical trade-offs, identifying potential points of failure, and working across teams to develop solutions that improve system resilience and availability KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Design and develop server and embedded RAS architectures for AMD products, including solutions deployed in scale-out environments. Define and analyze reliability, availability, and serviceability requirements aligned with industry standards and customer expectations. Collaborate with hardware and software teams to identify potential points of failure, conduct failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and develop mitigation strategies. Develop fault detection, isolation, recovery, redundancy, and error-correction mechanisms to improve system resilience and availability. Define and implement advanced diagnostics and monitoring capabilities to enable proactive system health management and predictive maintenance. Collaborate with vendors and suppliers to assess and integrate RAS-related solutions into the overall system architecture. Conduct system-level simulations, analysis, and testing to validate and verify the effectiveness of RAS architectures and components. Evaluate advancements in RAS techniques, fault-tolerance mechanisms, and industry trends to inform future system designs. Contribute throughout product development, from product definition, architecture, and design through implementation, debugging, testing, and early customer support. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience with system-level architecture design, reliability engineering, and fault-tolerance mechanisms for complex computing systems, data centers, or mission-critical applications. Experience developing and optimizing RAS architectures. Experience with fault-tolerant design principles and techniques, including redundancy, error correction codes (ECC), and error-recovery mechanisms. Experience with system-level simulation tools and methodologies, including fault injection, reliability block diagrams, and failure-rate analysis. Experience programming in C/C++ in Linux environments. Familiarity with Linux kernel internals and code review. Experience analyzing and resolving complex system-level technical issues. amd-87745.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: We're looking for a Forward Deployed Research Engineer to build, evaluate, and deploy cutting-edge AI systems that solve complex engineering challenges for enterprise customers. This is not a traditional Solutions Engineer or prompt engineering role. You'll combine deep software engineering, applied AI research, and customer engagement to develop production-ready AI systems using modern LLMs, reinforcement learning, agentic workflows, and post-training techniques. THE PERSON: You'll work directly with customers, researchers, and product teams to transform ambiguous engineering problems into scalable AI solutions. From rapid prototyping to production deployment, you'll help shape both customer success and the evolution of our AI platform. What Makes This Role Unique Build AI systems that solve real-world engineering problems—not proof-of-concepts. Work across applied AI research, software engineering, and customer deployment. Partner directly with enterprise engineering teams to define, build, and validate AI solutions. Influence future AI products by translating customer challenges into reusable platform capabilities. Own projects end-to-end—from technical discovery and experimentation through deployment and measurable impact. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Partner with customer engineering teams to understand workflows, technical challenges, and opportunities for AI-driven automation. Design, build, and deploy production-grade AI applications, LLM agents, and engineering automation solutions. Develop evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, testing environments, and data pipelines to measure model quality and business impact. Build and evaluate LLM post-training solutions, including supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, preference optimization, and reward modeling. Diagnose and optimize AI system performance across models, data, infrastructure, orchestration, and tooling. Collaborate with AI researchers to validate new models and techniques in production environments. Present technical solutions, architecture, and implementation strategies to engineering leaders, customers, and executive stakeholders. Transform recurring customer use cases into reusable AI infrastructure, frameworks, and platform capabilities. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Strong software engineering experience in Python and at least one systems language such as C++, Rust, C, TypeScript, CUDA, or HIP. Proven experience building production AI or machine learning systems beyond prompt engineering or API integrations. Hands-on experience with one or more of the following: LLM post-training Reinforcement Learning (RLHF, PPO, DPO, GRPO, or similar) Preference Optimization Reward Modeling Model or Agent Evaluation AI Training or Inference Infrastructure Deep understanding of transformer-based LLMs, inference, fine-tuning, retrieval, evaluation, and agent architectures. Experience designing reproducible evaluation frameworks using benchmarks, testing, and measurable performance metrics. Strong systems thinking, debugging, and problem-solving skills. Experience translating ambiguous technical requirements into scalable production solutions. Ability to work directly with customers and technical stakeholders to drive solution design, implementation, and adoption. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with engineers, researchers, customers, and executive leadership. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Experience training, fine-tuning, or post-training foundation models or open-source LLMs. Experience with PyTorch, Hugging Face, JAX, TensorFlow, Ray, vLLM, or distributed AI infrastructure. Experience building AI agents, retrieval systems, tool calling, workflow orchestration, or automated code generation. Experience with GPU optimization, CUDA, distributed systems, or high-performance computing. Background in forward-deployed engineering, applied AI research, customer engineering, or solutions architecture. Demonstrated success delivering AI solutions from customer discovery through deployment with measurable business impact.
