THE ROLE: AMD is seeking a Staff Data Engineer within the Marketing Analytics team to build and operationalize the data foundation that supports advanced analytics, data science, and machine learning across Marketing. This person will lead the hands-on development of scalable data pipelines, canonical data models, and trusted, reusable datasets that enable analytical use cases—from lead and account scoring to attribution, segmentation, forecasting, and campaign optimization. The role will work closely with data scientists, analytics professionals, Marketing stakeholders, and enterprise technology teams to translate analytical requirements into reliable data solutions. Responsibilities include integrating internal and external data through APIs and other ingestion methods, engineering datasets within environments such as Snowflake or Databricks, and establishing the data workflows, quality controls, and documentation needed to support repeatable model development and ongoing machine learning operations. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a hands-on data engineering leader who combines strong technical execution with an understanding of how data supports analytics and machine learning. They think beyond individual pipelines to build reusable data assets with consistent definitions, clear relationships, and reliable historical context. They must be comfortable working with complex, fragmented data, translating analytical needs into practical engineering requirements, and balancing immediate delivery needs with long-term maintainability and scale. They must also be a collaborative problem-solver who builds trusted relationships across business and technical teams, communicates trade-offs clearly, and brings discipline to data quality, documentation, and delivery. The ability to guide and mentor engineers while remaining closely involved in solution design and development is important to success in this role. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Build and operate scalable marketing data pipelines, transforming data from internal platforms and external sources into reliable, analysis-ready and machine-learning-ready datasets within Snowflake, Databricks, or comparable cloud data environments. Develop reusable API integrations and ingestion frameworks to bring together CRM, marketing automation, digital analytics, media, event, partner, and other relevant data, with appropriate controls for incremental updates, schema changes, failures, and reprocessing. Design and maintain canonical datasets and shared data models, establishing consistent definitions, identifiers, relationships, and historical views across core marketing entities such as accounts, contacts, leads, campaigns, engagement, spend, and opportunities. Engineer datasets for machine learning and data science, partnering with data scientists to develop features, labels, and training, validation, testing, and inference datasets. Apply appropriate historical snapshots and point-in-time logic to support reproducibility and prevent data leakage. Lead hands-on engineering delivery and continuous improvement, managing priorities and dependencies, reviewing technical designs and code, mentoring engineers, and improving development practices through reusable components, automated testing, and disciplined release management. Establish data quality, observability, and operational reliability, implementing automated validation, pipeline monitoring, freshness checks, and controls for schema and data distribution changes. Troubleshoot issues and improve pipeline performance, recovery processes, and compute efficiency. Partner with Marketing, Analytics, Data Science, Sales Operations, and IT to understand business priorities, translate use cases into data requirements, and align on dataset definitions, delivery expectations, and ownership. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, data platform development, or a related discipline, including experience leading technical projects or small engineering teams. Strong hands-on proficiency in SQL and Python, with experience developing production-grade data pipelines, transformations, and reusable engineering components. Experience with Spark or PySpark is a plus. Hands-on experience with Snowflake, Databricks, or comparable cloud data platforms, including data modeling, workload optimization, orchestration, and management of scalable analytical datasets. Demonstrated experience building API-based data integrations, including authentication, pagination, rate limits, incremental extraction, retry logic, and schema evolution, along with familiarity with file-based and other ingestion approaches. Experience preparing data for machine learning and data science workflows, including feature engineering pipelines, label generation, point-in-time-correct datasets, training and inference consistency, and reproducible dataset creation. Familiarity with feature stores and dataset versioning is preferred. Familiarity with MLOps and modern data engineering practices, including workflow orchestration, Git-based version control, automated testing, CI/CD, environment management, and the data requirements of model deployment and retraining. Experience with tools such as dbt or Airflow is a plus. Experience designing canonical data models and reusable data products, including entity resolution, deduplication, consistent data grain, historical tracking, and integration of structured and semi-structured data across multiple systems. Understanding of marketing and sales data ecosystems, including CRM, marketing automation, digital analytics, paid media, account-based marketing, events, and opportunity data, and how these sources support analytical and predictive use cases. Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to translate business and analytical needs into engineering requirements, explain technical trade-offs, coordinate cross-functional delivery, and mentor technical colleagues. You will explore how models acquire domain knowledge, reason, use tools, and learn from interaction with real development environments The role spans model training, agent design, and rigorous evaluation, with applications in software development, hardware design and verification, performance optimization, and automated technical discovery. Research may include pre-training, domain-adaptive continued pre-training, post-training, and reinforcement learning, alongside inference-time reasoning and search. You will own projects from initial research questions through working systems and demonstrated impact, delivering advances in models and agents that solve increasingly complex technical problems, generalize across projects and domains, and measurably improve the quality and productivity of software and hardware development. THE PERSON: You combine research depth with strong engineering skills. You enjoy turning ambiguous problems into experiments that improve model and agent capabilities. You can identify whether limitations stem from model knowledge, reasoning, context, or tools, and develop approaches that address them. You value both original research and measurable results in practical settings. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Research methods for reasoning, planning, tool use, memory, and reliable execution of multistep tasks. Develop pre-training and post-training approaches that strengthen models’ technical knowledge, coding abilities, and problem-solving capabilities. Build learning pipelines using curated corpora, demonstrations, synthetic data, agent trajectories, and execution feedback. Apply reinforcement learning and other adaptation methods to improve agent performance in executable environments. Investigate inference-time reasoning and search to improve solution quality and computational efficiency. Develop agents for software and hardware workflows, including code generation, RTL optimization, debugging, verification, and performance analysis. Create benchmarks that measure correctness, generalization, and sustained performance across unfamiliar projects. Collaborate with software and hardware teams to translate research into useful capabilities. Publish research and share findings through technical reports, reusable systems, and working demonstrations. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: A strong publication record in language models, AI agents, reinforcement learning, code intelligence, automated reasoning, or related areas, including venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, and EMNLP. Hands-on experience with LLM pre-training, continued pre-training, or post-training, including supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Experience building agents that interact with tools and executable environments. Experience developing training datasets, generating synthetic data, or learning from agent trajectories and verifiable feedback. Strong Python and deep learning framework skills, with experience running reproducible experiments. Familiarity with distributed training, large-scale evaluation, or efficient inference. Experience applying AI to software development, hardware design, scientific computing, or optimization. Familiarity with RTL, simulation, formal verification, compilers, or GPU kernels is a plus. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering, or a related field preferred. amd-87746.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: We are hiring AI / ML Platform Engineers to build the platform layer that makes AI-for-engineering workflows scalable, reliable, and reproducible. This role focuses on the infrastructure and platform systems that support large-scale agent execution, distributed training and inference, experiment tracking, benchmark automation, artifact management, and GPU cluster utilization. You will work closely with ML Systems Research Engineers, AI Research Scientists, Applied AI Engineers, and hardware domain experts to operationalize the Blueprint framework across kernel optimization, RTL/PPA optimization, ECO fixing, verification, simulation, and debugging workflows. This is a platform engineering role, not a pure research role. The focus is to build robust shared systems that allow researchers and engineers to run more experiments, compare results reliably, reduce manual orchestration, and move successful workflows into production engineering use. THE PERSON: You are a strong systems engineer who enjoys building reliable platforms for AI researchers and applied engineers. You understand distributed systems, ML workloads, GPU infrastructure, experiment management, and production reliability. You can turn messy research workflows into reusable services, APIs, dashboards, job systems, and automation. You care about reproducibility, observability, performance, and developer experience. You are comfortable working across ML, infrastructure, and hardware/software tooling, and you can partner with research teams without requiring every requirement to be fully specified upfront. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Build and operate the shared AI platform for agentic engineering workflows, including job submission, scheduling, orchestration, retries, logging, artifact storage, and experiment tracking. Develop reliable infrastructure for distributed training, distributed inference, batch evaluation, and large-scale agent rollout across GPU clusters. Build platform services for benchmark execution, correctness checking, profiling, regression tracking, and reproducible evaluation. Maintain artifact systems for generated kernels, RTL edits, traces, logs, profiler outputs, benchmark results, simulator outputs, and formal verification artifacts. Support scalable integrations with compilers, ROCm/HIP tooling, profilers, simulators, EDA tools, vLLM, SGLang, and internal engineering systems. Improve GPU cluster utilization, scheduling efficiency, reliability, quota management, and workload isolation. Build dashboards and observability systems for experiment status, resource usage, failure modes, benchmark trends, regression detection, and team productivity. Partner with ML Systems Research Engineers to productionize research workflows for RL systems, inference systems, quantification systems, and evaluation pipelines. Partner with Applied AI Engineers to make Blueprint harnesses reusable across kernel optimization, RTL optimization, verification, firmware, and CPU/GPU performance workflows. Establish platform standards for reproducibility, data retention, run metadata, artifact lineage, access control, and operational reliability. TECHNICAL FOCUS AREAS: Distributed ML platform infrastructure for training, inference, evaluation, and agent execution. GPU cluster scheduling, utilization, reliability, quota management, and multi-user workload isolation. Experiment tracking, artifact management, run lineage, dashboards, and reproducible workflow management. Benchmark and evaluation automation for correctness, performance, regression detection, and reproducibility. Integration with ROCm/HIP, Triton, compilers, profilers, vLLM, SGLang, simulators, formal tools, and EDA flows. Caching and parallelization for expensive feedback loops, including simulator, compiler, verifier, and benchmark workloads. Production-quality APIs, services, workflow engines, and developer tooling for research and engineering teams. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Strong programming skills in Python and one or more systems languages such as C++, Go, or Rust. Experience building ML platforms, AI infrastructure, distributed systems, workflow orchestration, experiment platforms, GPU cluster infrastructure, or developer platforms. Strong understanding of job scheduling, distributed workloads, logging, monitoring, reliability, storage systems, and production operations. Experience with Kubernetes, Ray, Slurm, workflow engines, containerization, CI/CD, data pipelines, or large-scale compute orchestration. Ability to build reliable services, APIs, dashboards, and developer tools used by researchers and engineers. Strong debugging skills across distributed systems, GPU workloads, storage systems, networking, containers, and production infrastructure. Good collaboration skills with AI researchers, ML systems researchers, applied engineers and hardware domain experts. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience with GPU platforms, ROCm/HIP, CUDA, profiling, kernel benchmarking, model serving, or distributed training/inference. Experience with vLLM, SGLang, Triton, PyTorch, JAX, Ray, Kubernetes, Slurm, MLflow, Weights & Biases, or similar systems. Experience building experiment tracking systems, artifact stores, workflow engines, benchmark automation platforms, or developer productivity tools. Experience supporting LLM agents, tool-use systems, large-scale sampling, or automated program optimization workflows. Familiarity with compiler, profiler, simulator, formal verification, EDA, firmware, or hardware performance workflows is a strong plus. Experience operating shared GPU clusters or high-performance ML infrastructure in a multi-user research environment. EDUCATION Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or related field, or equivalent practical experience. Master's preferred; PhD is a plus, especially with work in ML systems, reinforcement learning, distributed systems, GPU computing, or AI infrastructure. amd-87872.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: We are hiring Applied AI Engineers to work directly with hardware and software engineering teams on high-priority AI-for-engineering efforts. This role turns difficult engineering workflows into AI-assisted systems that generate candidates, validate correctness, measure quality, and help engineers move faster on real product problems. You will work across hardware-adjacent domains such as design optimization, verification, simulation, firmware, performance debugging, routing, issue triage, and compute library optimization. The work is practical, measured, and deeply collaborative with domain experts. THE PERSON: You are a builder who likes ambiguous, high-impact engineering problems. You can sit with domain experts, understand the real workflow, identify what can be measured, build the tool or agent loop, and iterate until it saves engineering time or improves a concrete metric. You value correctness, validation, and workflow fit as much as model capability. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Build applied AI workflows for top hardware and software engineering priorities, including optimization, verification, debugging, simulation, and automation workflows. Convert manual engineering processes into structured tasks with inputs, candidate generation, validation, scoring, logging, and reproducible comparisons. Partner with domain owners to define success metrics such as correctness, performance, resource usage, quality, latency, coverage, engineer time saved, or issue classification accuracy. Develop tools that let AI agents use compilers, simulators, formal checks, profilers, benchmark harnesses, ticket systems, and engineering knowledge sources. Build human-in-the-loop workflows for tasks where annotated data, expert judgment, or subjective triage is required. Improve model and agent performance through better prompts, tool interfaces, retrieval, evaluation datasets, graders, and structured feedback. Work with research and infrastructure teams to generalize repeated patterns into reusable platforms, harnesses, dashboards, and data assets. Communicate progress through measurable outcomes, demos, concise technical writeups, and clear stakeholder updates. TECHNICAL FOCUS AREAS: AI-assisted hardware design and software optimization workflows. Automated validation using tests, benchmarks, formal checks, simulators, and domain-specific graders. Agentic systems for code generation, debugging, root-cause analysis, issue triage, and engineering workflow automation. Evaluation design for tasks where ground truth may be sparse, expensive, or partially subjective. Tooling that connects LLMs and agents to real engineering systems while preserving reliability and auditability. Collaboration with domain experts to turn expert workflows into repeatable AI-assisted processes. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Strong software engineering experience in Python and at least one systems language such as C++, C, HIP, CUDA, or Rust. Experience building applied AI, ML, agentic, automation, or developer tooling systems for technical users. Ability to work with complex engineering tools, logs, tests, benchmark harnesses, and validation workflows. Strong debugging and root-cause analysis skills across software systems, AI workflows, or hardware-adjacent tooling. Excellent collaboration and communication skills with domain experts, engineering leads, research teams, and program stakeholders. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experience with hardware design or verification workflows, including RTL, Verilog/SystemVerilog, simulation, formal verification, EDA tools, timing analysis, or power/performance/area tradeoffs. Experience with GPU/CPU performance engineering, compiler tooling, profilers, kernel optimization, ROCm/HIP, CUDA, or benchmarking. Experience designing evaluation datasets, graders, dashboards, leaderboards, or experiment tracking systems. Familiarity with LLM agents, tool use, retrieval, LLM-as-judge workflows, RL, or post-training methods. Experience working with internal engineering customers, forward-deployed teams, or cross-functional product engineering programs. EDUCATION Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or related field, or equivalent practical experience. Master's preferred; PhD is a plus for candidates with relevant AI, systems, EDA, or hardware/software co-design experience. THE ROLE: We are looking for a highly skilled Developer / Data Scientist to join our product development organization focused on power and performance optimization for client PC platforms. This role sits at the intersection of data science, low-level systems engineering, and algorithm development. You will work closely with engineering and architecture teams to analyze telemetry at scale, tune dynamic optimization algorithms, and help shape how modern PCs adapt to diverse hardware configurations and real-world usage scenarios. This is an ideal position for someone who is equally passionate about deep data analysis and hands‑on software engineering, and who enjoys translating complex findings into actionable insights for stakeholders across engineering, leadership, and partner organizations. THE PERSON: This role matches well for someone who: Loves switching between data science and systems-level development. Enjoys both experimental analysis and product-scale engineering. Perform investigations ranging from deep‑dive single‑system analyses to broad statistical studies across hundreds of thousands of devices in the field. Build, refine, and maintain tooling, dashboards, visualizations, and interactive analysis pipelines to help engineering teams understand trends and anomalies. Collaborate with cross‑functional teams to integrate these algorithms into production environments and partner-facing SDKs. Implement robust, scalable data pipelines, ML workflows, or validation frameworks (experience with Dataiku is a strong plus). Contribute to automation, performance measurement workflows, and algorithm validation frameworks. Participate in performance tuning, quality validation, and continuous improvement of system optimization logic. THE ROLE: AMD is searching for a Director of Silicon Design to lead the organization-wide adoption of AI-driven methodologies across our x86 Core Development Organization. This role owns the technical vision and execution strategy for embedding AI/ML into engineering workflows spanning functional verification, RTL design, and physical design. You will build and lead a team of engineers and technical leaders, set the multi-year vision for AI adoption in core development, and be accountable for measurable improvements in engineering efficiency and design quality. You will engage directly with Cores engineering leadership to align investments, technical priorities, and organizational adoption, and will represent AI strategy and technical direction to executive stakeholders. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate combines proven engineering leadership with credible depth in AI/ML and a working understanding of CPU core development across verification, RTL design, and/or physical design. You can set and defend a multi-year AI adoption strategy, translate it into technical execution and measurable outcomes, and build organizational buy-in from engineers and executives alike. Broad knowledge of AI/ML technology, algorithms, and tooling, and how they map to EDA and silicon development workflows, is essential for this position. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Own the strategy, roadmap, and organizational adoption of AI-driven methodologies across verification, RTL design, and physical design within x86 core development. Build, lead, and grow a team of engineers and technical leaders driving AI adoption initiatives (e.g., predictive coverage modeling, intelligent test generation and triage, RTL code assistance, timing/congestion prediction, floorplan and place-and-route optimization). Partner with Cores engineering leadership, architecture, design, verification, physical design, and internal tooling/data engineering teams to prioritize investments and align AI initiatives to business and engineering priorities. Define and own organizational success metrics, including verification velocity, coverage closure, PPA (power, performance, area) targets, design-cycle schedule adherence, and defect escape rate, and communicate progress to executive stakeholders. Drive evaluation and adoption decisions on emerging AI tools and platforms (open-source, EDA-vendor, and internally built), including build-versus-buy and infrastructure investment recommendations. Lead organizational adoption of AI-augmented workflows, including technical enablement, training, and best-practice development. Identify, escalate, and resolve cross-organizational technical challenges and barriers to successful AI adoption. Manage organizational headcount planning and resource allocation for the AI engineering team. Serve as the primary executive point of contact for AI adoption initiatives within core development, presenting strategy, progress, and business impact to senior and executive leadership. Mentor engineers and technical leaders on applying AI/ML methods to solve complex design and development challenges. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Significant experience leading engineering organizations, with a track record of driving large-scale, cross-functional technical initiatives; prior people-management experience leading engineers and technical leaders. Direct experience in CPU or SoC development, including verification, RTL design, and/or physical design, sufficient to credibly set priorities and evaluate tradeoffs across these domains. Demonstrated experience applying AI/ML or data science approaches (or leading teams that do) to engineering, hardware design, or EDA problems, with measurable business or engineering outcomes. Ability to set and defend a multi-year technical strategy, translate it into execution plans, and adjust direction based on a changing technical and business landscape. A mindset that accepts accountability for organizational outcomes, ensuring technical decisions align with business and engineering goals. Superb communication skills at the executive level; experience managing organizational investments, external vendors (including EDA vendors), and complex technical initiatives. Experience spanning more than one of verification, RTL design, and physical design. Hands-on technical background with AI/ML tooling and frameworks sufficient to engage credibly with engineering teams on model approaches, data pipelines, and tooling architecture. Experience building an organization or practice from the ground up, including hiring, defining operating processes, and establishing new organizational capabilities. Familiarity with EDA tooling and vendors (e.g., Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA) and how AI/ML capabilities are being integrated into commercial and open-source EDA flows. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: BS, MS, or equivalent in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, with direct experience. Assess vendor upgrades for configuration and integration compatibility; investigate performance issues and implement fixes with AMD IT and Orange Logic. amd-93544.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE We are seeking a Lead HPC & AI Infrastructure Architect to lead the architecture and technical direction of large-scale CPU and GPU platforms across on-premises infrastructure, public cloud, and specialized GPU cloud providers. You will translate scientific computing, engineering, and AI requirements into secure, reliable, scalable, and cost-effective platforms for tightly coupled HPC workloads, distributed model training, and inference services. This hands-on leadership role spans design, workload validation, deployment, and lifecycle management. You will provide technical direction to infrastructure engineering and SRE teams and collaborate with researchers, AI engineers, security teams, cloud providers, hardware vendors, and data center teams to deliver production-ready platforms. THE PERSON You combine strong systems expertise with practical architectural judgment. You approach complex technical problems collaboratively, validate decisions with measurable results, and communicate tradeoffs clearly. You work effectively across engineering, operations, security, and research teams; mentor engineers with varied backgrounds and experience levels; and balance performance, reliability, security, delivery timelines, and cost. You can lead initiatives with appropriate autonomy while engaging the partners needed to move from requirements through production acceptance. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Lead the HPC and AI infrastructure roadmap, reference architectures, and standards for CPU/GPU clusters. Define workload placement across bare metal, virtual machines, Slurm, and Kubernetes. Lead designs covering CPU/NUMA and GPU topology, accelerator interconnects, networking, storage, and identity. Establish validated hardware, firmware, driver, and runtime baselines. Architect RDMA-capable fabrics and storage tiers. Validate collective communication, parallel I/O, dataset delivery, and checkpoint performance at target scale. Design resource sharing through Slurm accounting, fair-share, quotas, QoS, preemption, and tenant isolation. Enable reproducible environments, self-service onboarding, and inference capacity planning. Standardize provisioning, configuration, and fleet upgrades through infrastructure as code, automation, and CI/CD; manage images, containers, and configuration drift. Define production acceptance criteria, service-level objectives, and fleet observability. Partner with SRE teams on fault isolation, job recovery, checkpoint/restart, incident analysis, and capacity planning. Benchmark HPC and distributed AI workloads; improve scaling efficiency, throughput, inference latency, GPU utilization, reliability, and cost efficiency through bottleneck analysis. Incorporate federated identity, least-privilege access, tenant and network isolation, secrets management, controlled container privileges, audit logging, and vulnerability management into platform designs. Lead architecture reviews, proofs of concept, provider evaluations, and complex technical problem solving. Document decisions and tradeoffs, mentor engineers, and align delivery with stakeholders and infrastructure partners. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE Significant experience in infrastructure, cloud engineering, or distributed systems, including demonstrated experience designing and delivering production HPC or GPU platforms. Equivalent practical experience is welcome. Experience leading large-scale cluster deployments involving hundreds of nodes, substantial multi-GPU environments, or systems of comparable technical complexity, with measurable improvements in workload performance, reliability, utilization, or cost. Experience with a major cloud platform such as Azure, OCI, or AWS, including integration between cloud and on-premises systems. Familiarity with specialized GPU providers such as Crusoe or TensorWave is beneficial. Strong Linux troubleshooting skills across CPU/NUMA topology, PCIe, GPU connectivity, drivers, virtualization, containers, and distributed runtime environments. Hands-on experience with Slurm scheduling and resource governance, plus Kubernetes or comparable orchestration experience. Understanding of MPI, distributed training, collective communication, and AI inference infrastructure. Experience with GPU computing platforms and distributed AI workloads. Experience with AMD Instinct GPUs, ROCm, RCCL, and multi-node PyTorch workloads, including compatibility validation and performance troubleshooting, is particularly relevant. HPC networking and storage experience, including RDMA, RoCE or InfiniBand, topology and oversubscription tradeoffs, parallel I/O, data placement, checkpointing, and enterprise connectivity. Experience with parallel and shared storage technologies such as Lustre, IBM Storage Scale, BeeGFS, NFS, VAST, or comparable technologies, as well as object storage and cluster acceptance benchmarking. Experience with Terraform or equivalent infrastructure as code, Ansible or comparable configuration management, Python or Bash, and Git-based CI/CD. Familiarity with Azure CycleCloud, AWS ParallelCluster, or comparable cluster provisioning frameworks is beneficial. Experience implementing observability and SRE practices using Prometheus, Grafana, or comparable technologies, including secure access, resource controls, fault recovery, and production readiness. We are passionate about BIOS and platform firmware architecture, boot flow, system level debug, power and performance management, and building the firmware foundation that unlocks the potential of AMD's next-generation data center platforms. We are seeking a seasoned firmware engineering manager to lead and grow the Data Center BIOS team. This is a leadership opportunity: you will be responsible for building and developing the team, recruiting top BIOS and platform firmware talent, establishing engineering culture and processes, and accelerating the ramp-up of engineers at all levels. You will set the technical direction for BIOS features and own execution from concept through production, including boot readiness, release milestones, and customer and partner issue resolution. The right candidate brings deep hands-on expertise in BIOS/UEFI, platform initialization, and x86 architecture and debug, combined with the management maturity to coach engineers, drive cross-functional alignment, and deliver predictably on complex multi-quarter programs. THE PERSON: We are looking for an accomplished engineering leader who leads by example: someone who can roll up their sleeves on a hard debug problem one moment and run a productive one-on-one the next. The ideal candidate has a proven track record of building new teams, developing engineers' technical and professional skills, and fostering a culture of ownership, rigor, and continuous improvement. Critical thinking, clear communication, and the ability to translate complex architectural tradeoffs into actionable engineering priorities are essential. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Team Building & People Development Recruit, hire, and onboard firmware engineers across all experience levels to build a world-class BIOS development and support team. Develop and execute structured onboarding and ramp-up plans that accelerate new engineer productivity, including mentorship programs, AI development, technical deep-dives, and hands-on coaching expectations. Conduct regular one-on-ones, performance reviews, and career development planning; identify high-potential engineers and create growth paths for advancement. Foster a collaborative, inclusive team culture grounded in technical excellence, psychological safety, and accountability. Establish team norms, coding standards, firmware review processes, and documentation practices. Technical Leadership & Architecture Own the Platform BIOS from PreSI to Production until the EOL of the program. Drive system Firmware requirements from definition, development in emulation and pre-silicon simulation through first silicon and production; serve as the escalation point for complex, cross-team debug campaigns. Collaborate closely with Feature Enabling Team, firmware architects, Debug team, IFWI teams, and platform software engineers to co-define firmware/hardware interfaces and feature specifications. Plan product Platform Initialization timeline and work closely with Lead System engineers to meet the program goals in order to deliver FW to external and internal stakeholders. Program Execution & Delivery Define, track, and communicate team goals, milestone plans, and risk areas to senior leadership and partner teams. Own the firmware feature roadmap for the program; balance short-term silicon commitments with long-term architectural investment. Drive continuous improvement in firmware quality, test coverage, bring-up velocity, and release reliability. Manage cross-functional dependencies with hardware, software, platform, and validation teams to ensure smooth program execution. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Experienced in x86 bios, semiconductor firmware, embedded systems, or SOC software engineering, with a focus in an engineering management or tech lead-manager role. Proven record of building new engineering teams: hiring, onboarding, and growing engineers from junior to senior level in a fast-paced semiconductor environment. Solid understanding of x86 architecture: server business environment. Track record of mentoring and developing engineers; experience implementing structured onboarding programs, technical training curricula, or engineering ladders. Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills; ability to represent firmware perspective in architecture reviews and executive program updates. amd-84773.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: This position is responsible for Product Planning of next-generation AMD Adaptive and Embedded Computing products, with a focus on ASIC, SoC, FPGA, Adaptive SoC, and semi-custom product definition. The role drives product strategy, roadmap planning, and product requirements by translating customer needs, market opportunities, business objectives, and engineering capabilities into actionable product definitions. A significant aspect of this role is driving product requirements related to power efficiency, thermal performance, packaging, quality, reliability, manufacturability, and performance per watt. The individual serves as a key technical and business point of contact across product planning, architecture, engineering, product engineering, packaging, quality, validation, manufacturing, marketing, and customer-facing teams. The successful candidate will partner with engineering organizations to identify product-level opportunities and influence technical direction through requirements, customer insight, competitive analysis, and data-driven product planning rather than direct implementation ownership. THE PERSON: A successful candidate can independently drive product planning activities and influence technical decisions across multiple engineering organizations. The ideal candidate combines strong technical understanding of semiconductor products, system architecture, and product development with the ability to translate customer needs, market trends, and technical constraints into structured product requirements. The candidate understands how architecture, implementation, packaging, reliability, quality, manufacturing, validation, and thermal decisions affect overall product competitiveness and can effectively challenge assumptions, identify risks, and drive improved product outcomes through requirements and technical influence. This role requires credibility with engineering organizations and the ability to engage deeply in technical discussions while maintaining a broader product, customer, and business perspective. Comfort with ambiguity is essential. The candidate must be able to create structure, evaluate alternatives, and drive decisions when requirements, constraints, or priorities are not fully defined. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Drive product planning activities for future ASIC, SoC, FPGA, Adaptive SoC, and semi-custom products. Gather and translate customer, market, business, and system requirements into product requirements, product definitions, and roadmap recommendations. Drive product requirements and planning activities across performance, power, thermal, quality, reliability, manufacturability, packaging, and performance-per-watt dimensions. Collaborate with architecture, design, product engineering, quality, validation, packaging, manufacturing, and business teams to ensure product requirements appropriately balance customer needs, product competitiveness, implementation complexity, and business objectives. Identify product-level risks and opportunities associated with power delivery, thermal solutions, packaging technologies, reliability targets, manufacturability, qualification, and quality objectives and ensure they are reflected in planning decisions. Influence technical direction through requirements development, customer and market analysis, competitive analysis, and cross-functional alignment. Work closely with engineering teams to challenge assumptions, evaluate alternatives, and improve overall product competitiveness through structured requirements and data-driven analysis. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: 10+ years of relevant experience in semiconductor product development, system architecture, product planning, product management, technical marketing, applications engineering, product engineering, or related technical roles. Demonstrated experience influencing product, architecture, or engineering decisions through requirements development, technical analysis, customer engagement, or product planning. Strong understanding of semiconductor product tradeoffs involving performance, power, thermal management, packaging technologies, quality, reliability, manufacturability, cost, and time-to-market. Experience defining product requirements, platform requirements, roadmap strategies, product planning inputs, or product investment recommendations. Experience working with FPGA, Adaptive SoC, ASIC, CPU, GPU, AI accelerator, networking, communications, embedded, or semi-custom semiconductor products. Experience working across architecture, engineering, product engineering, validation, manufacturing, packaging, and quality organizations. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related discipline. amd-96398.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: AMD is looking for a Senior Member of Technical Staff (SMTS) to join our growing firmware team. As a key contributor, you will be part of a leading team that drives and enhances AMD's ability to deliver the highest-quality, industry-leading technologies to market. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate has an innovative, problem-solving mindset and a keen eye for software engineering, and is diligent and passionate about technology. A successful candidate will bring strong knowledge of computer technologies, technical leadership skills and software engineering expertise, as well as a strong ability to compete effectively in a fast-paced environment while working with different teams of engineers and collaborators. You will take ownership of features end to end, drive issues to resolution and help junior engineers grow. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Validate new firmware and software features for AMD products at a system level before they are released to customers. Own the validation of major features end to end: test plans, automation, execution and sign-off. Leverage AI tools to accelerate the software validation cycle. Contribute actively to the day-to-day activities of the system test team in an Agile environment. Write test plans, review them with all stakeholders to cover the scenarios comprehensively, and execute them efficiently. Build maintainable, high-quality and effective automated test scripts. Review and triage test failures, and verify fixes. Help address customer-reported issues by reproducing them locally and working with peer teams for faster resolution. Stay informed of software and hardware trends and innovations, especially in firmware, CPUs, GPUs and accelerators. Debug complex technical issues and collaborate with peer teams. Develop technical relationships with peers and partners. Mentor junior engineers and lead test plan reviews. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Established years of experience in system testing, validation or test automation. Strong experience in firmware test and automation roles. Solid understanding of AI tools and how to leverage them in a large-scale distributed environment. Proficiency in writing automation scripts in Python, and experience with test and performance-testing tools. Solid understanding of automation frameworks, and fluency in Python. Prior experience with cloud, security and data center technologies is an added advantage. Strong troubleshooting skills. Knowledge of operating systems, kernel-mode programming, device drivers, and related technologies and architectures. Good interpersonal and communication skills. Ability to write high-quality automation code with keen attention to detail. Good understanding of the Linux operating system and hypervisors (VMware ESX, KVM). Experience with software development processes and tools such as debuggers, source code control systems (GitHub) and profilers is a plus. Experience testing firmware on CPU, GPU or SoC platforms is a plus. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or equivalent. amd-93677.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: AMD is looking for a Principal Member of Technical Staff Infrastructure Lead to help enable and support the infrastructure behind AMD’s flagship data center GPU platforms, including Helios. This is a highly visible, hands-on individual contributor role within a growing platform engineering organization supporting cutting-edge AI and large language model workloads. In this role, you will serve as a technical leader across the three core pillars of data center infrastructure: networking, storage, and compute virtualization. You will work across infrastructure architecture, platform, security, and engineering teams to solve complex issues that span multiple technical domains. You will be at the forefront of bringing new platforms and data center environments online, improving infrastructure reliability, and ensuring that critical issues are resolved quickly and do not recur. This is an opportunity to influence how AMD builds and operates its next generation of data center GPU infrastructure while working on technology at significant scale. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a proactive, hands-on technical leader who enjoys solving complex infrastructure problems and can connect issues across networking, storage, and virtualization environments. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong ownership, sound technical judgment, and the ability to remain effective during high-priority incidents. The candidate should be comfortable leading technical discussions, communicating clearly with engineering teams and leadership, and working independently in a fast-moving environment. This person will thrive on a team that values flexibility, responsiveness, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Because this is an infrastructure reliability leadership role, the candidate should also be comfortable providing support outside standard business hours when critical incidents require additional attention. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Diagnose and resolve complex infrastructure incidents spanning data center networking, storage, and compute virtualization. Lead technical troubleshooting and root cause analysis using monitoring, logs, packet captures, and performance data to identify failure points and prevent repeat incidents. Partner with infrastructure architecture, platform, security, and domain engineering teams to implement reliable, scalable infrastructure solutions. Support the deployment and enablement of new AMD data center GPU platforms, including the surrounding network, storage, compute, and virtualization infrastructure required for operation. Design, review, and implement infrastructure solutions for new data center builds, site expansions, migrations, and hardware refreshes. Recommend architecture and reliability improvements that reduce incidents and improve platform availability, performance, and recovery. Establish effective infrastructure monitoring, alerting, documentation, and operational runbooks. Support capacity planning, high availability, failover, backup, and disaster recovery activities across infrastructure services. Identify opportunities to reduce repetitive operational work through automation, scripting, and infrastructure-as-code practices. Provide technical leadership and mentorship to engineers while helping raise the overall technical capabilities of the team. First 30 days: Learn AMD’s infrastructure environment, platforms, operating processes, and current technical priorities. Within 60 days: Begin contributing hands-on to infrastructure incidents, larger technical issues, and near-term improvement opportunities. Within 90 days: Take a leading role in incident response and architecture discussions and become a key technical resource for networking, storage, virtualization, and platform infrastructure questions. Long term: Serve as a trusted technical authority for platform enablement, infrastructure reliability, incident prevention, and future data center growth. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Principal or staff-level, hands-on experience supporting data center, private cloud, platform engineering, or site reliability engineering environments. Deep technical expertise across the three core infrastructure pillars: data center networking, enterprise storage, and compute virtualization. Experience diagnosing complex, cross-domain infrastructure issues and understanding how failures can propagate across network, storage, compute, and virtualization layers. Data center networking knowledge, including technologies such as VLANs, VXLAN/EVPN, spine-leaf fabrics, BGP, OSPF, LACP/MLAG, load balancers, firewalls, DNS, DHCP, and NTP. Experience troubleshooting network performance using packet captures, flow data, switch/router diagnostics, and telemetry. Enterprise storage experience across SAN, NAS, or software-defined storage platforms, including technologies such as Fibre Channel, iSCSI, NVMe-oF, NFS, SMB, Ceph, or vSAN. Experience identifying and resolving storage latency, throughput, IOPS, queue depth, multipathing, and resource-contention issues. Experience with compute virtualization platforms such as VMware vSphere/ESXi, KVM/QEMU, Proxmox, or Hyper-V. Strong Linux administration and command-line troubleshooting skills. Experience with bare-metal provisioning, firmware and BIOS management, hardware troubleshooting, and infrastructure lifecycle management. Exposure to containers or Kubernetes operating within virtualized or bare-metal infrastructure environments. Experience with infrastructure monitoring and observability platforms such as Zabbix, Prometheus, or Grafana. Automation, scripting, or infrastructure-as-code experience using tools such as Python, Bash, Go, Ansible, or Terraform is preferred. GPU, AI data center, HPC, high-speed Ethernet, RDMA/RoCE, or lossless fabric experience is a plus. Experience documenting technical environments and creating operational runbooks, network diagrams, and system architecture documentation. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations to both engineers and leadership. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: A bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical field is preferred. LOCATION: Austin, Texas preferred. Other U.S. AMD locations may be considered based on business needs. This role is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship #LI-CS1 Benefits offered are described: AMD benefits at a glance. THE ROLE: As an AMD-AECG Design Automation Engineer, you will help build the next generation of AI-powered engineering platforms that enable AMD's chip design teams to find, understand, and interact with complex semiconductor design data. You will develop scalable software systems, data pipelines, knowledge graphs, and AI/LLM-driven capabilities that transform how architects, designers, and verification engineers access and leverage engineering knowledge. Working at the intersection of AI, software infrastructure, and semiconductor design, you will help expand the platform to support new engineering domains, workflows, and agent-based experiences that accelerate chip development. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a strong software engineer with experience building production-quality backend systems and a passion for applying AI to solve complex technical problems. You are comfortable designing data models, building large-scale data pipelines, and developing AI/LLM-based solutions such as retrieval systems, knowledge graphs, and agentic workflows. You thrive in highly technical and ambiguous environments, can collaborate effectively with both software and hardware engineers, and are motivated by the opportunity to build tools that directly impact the design of next-generation CPUs, GPUs, and AI accelerators. amd-88556.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: Join AMD’s Data Center Platform Engineering Group (DPEG), where you will help develop the next generation of liquid-cooled AI and high-performance computing platforms. As a Senior Liquid Cooling Thermal Design & Validation Engineer, you will be part of a highly collaborative thermal engineering team responsible for creating innovative cooling solutions that enable AMD’s industry-leading data center GPU products. In this role, you will work across the entire product development lifecycle, partnering with thermal engineers, mechanical engineers, silicon teams, system architects, manufacturing partners, and external vendors to develop and validate advanced thermal solutions. Your work will span from concept development and simulation to hands-on laboratory testing and prototype validation. You will have the opportunity to influence the design of cutting-edge AI hardware while working in a fast-paced environment that combines technical innovation, experimentation, and real-world product impact. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a self-starter who enjoys solving complex engineering challenges and thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. They are naturally curious, enjoy hands-on technical work, and possess strong problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities.Successful candidates are comfortable working across multiple disciplines, communicating with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and driving projects forward with minimal oversight. They are motivated by learning new technologies, tackling challenging engineering problems, and contributing to innovative products that push the boundaries of AI and data center computing. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Develop and validate liquid cooling solutions for AMD data center GPU and AI computing platforms. Drive thermal-mechanical solution development from concept through prototype validation and production readiness. Collaborate with internal engineering teams and external vendors to develop innovative cold plate, heat sink, and liquid cooling technologies. Perform thermal simulations and laboratory-based validation testing. Conduct flow, pressure drop, temperature mapping, and thermal performance measurements. Analyze test results, identify thermal bottlenecks, and recommend design improvements. Generate technical documentation and communicate findings to engineering stakeholders. Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance product quality, reliability, and time-to-market. Support the development and deployment of next-generation liquid-cooled server and rack-level cooling solutions. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Thermal design and validation of high-power electronics, AI platforms, HPC systems, or data center server products. Development of liquid cooling technologies including cold plates, heat sinks, and rack-level cooling solutions. Experience working with vendors and suppliers on thermal-mechanical solution development. CFD analysis using Icepak, FloTHERM, Ansys Fluent, or similar tools. Strong understanding of heat transfer, fluid mechanics, electronics cooling, and thermal management principles. Flow network modeling, pressure drop analysis, and coolant optimization. Laboratory testing, instrumentation, telemetry systems, data acquisition, and thermal characterization. Mechanical design experience using Creo, SolidWorks, or similar CAD tools. Knowledge of GD&T, manufacturing tolerances, assembly processes, and design-for-manufacturing methodologies. Understanding of cold plate manufacturing technologies including machining, brazing, skiving, friction stir welding, or additive manufacturing. Experience with thermal and mechanical validation of liquid-cooled server platforms. Familiarity with FEA, statistical analysis, design optimization, and experimental methodologies. Experience with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or similar tools for automation and data analysis. Familiarity with Open Compute Project (OCP) standards and modern AI infrastructure architectures. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor's or master’s degree preferred in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline. Doctoral degree desired. Relevant certifications, research experience, or specialized training in thermal engineering, CFD, liquid cooling, or mechanical design are a plus. THE ROLE: AMD is seeking a Senior Product Development Engineer to join a results-oriented Test Engineering team where you’ll have a direct impact on the quality, cost, and time-to-market of AMD microprocessors. You’ll collaborate closely with Design and Platform Engineering teams, with opportunities to influence future test strategies and product improvements. Post-silicon, you’ll tackle complex microprocessor debug and characterization challenges involving silicon performance, yield, manufacturing processes, and device marginalities. THE PERSON: This position requires accountability for the quality and timeliness of outcomes within assigned projects or processes. Key duties include the development and debugging of Automated Test Equipment (ATE) test patterns and flows, ensuring device testability and manufacturability from development through production phases, and implementing product improvement measures to reduce cost, increase yield, and resolve quality issues. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Deliver innovative product test solutions consisting of hardware, software, and test content to achieve cost and quality requirements of the product. In this role, you will work across the entire product development lifecycle, partnering with thermal engineers, mechanical engineers, silicon teams, system architects, manufacturing partners, and external vendors to develop and validate advanced thermal solutions. Your work will span from concept development and simulation to hands-on laboratory testing and prototype validation. You will have the opportunity to influence the design of cutting-edge AI hardware while working in a fast-paced environment that combines technical innovation, experimentation, and real-world product impact. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a self-starter who enjoys solving complex engineering challenges and thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. They are motivated by learning new technologies, tackling challenging engineering problems, and contributing to innovative products that push the boundaries of AI and data center computing. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Develop and validate liquid cooling solutions for AMD data center GPU and AI computing platforms. Drive thermal-mechanical solution development from concept through prototype validation and production readiness. Collaborate with internal engineering teams and external vendors to develop innovative cold plate, heat sink, and liquid cooling technologies. Perform thermal simulations and laboratory-based validation testing. Conduct flow, pressure drop, temperature mapping, and thermal performance measurements. Analyze test results, identify thermal bottlenecks, and recommend design improvements. Generate technical documentation and communicate findings to engineering stakeholders. Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance product quality, reliability, and time-to-market. Support the development and deployment of next-generation liquid-cooled server and rack-level cooling solutions. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Thermal design and validation of high-power electronics, AI platforms, HPC systems, or data center server products. Development of liquid cooling technologies including cold plates, heat sinks, and rack-level cooling solutions. Laboratory testing, instrumentation, telemetry systems, data acquisition, and thermal characterization. Mechanical design experience using Creo, SolidWorks, or similar CAD tools. Knowledge of GD&T, manufacturing tolerances, assembly processes, and design-for-manufacturing methodologies. Understanding of cold plate manufacturing technologies including machining, brazing, skiving, friction stir welding, or additive manufacturing. Experience with thermal and mechanical validation of liquid-cooled server platforms. Familiarity with FEA, statistical analysis, design optimization, and experimental methodologies. Experience with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or similar tools for automation and data analysis. Familiarity with Open Compute Project (OCP) standards and modern AI infrastructure architectures. THE ROLE: As a Senior Mechanical Product Engineer in the Data Center Platform Engineering Group (DPEG) Mechanical Engineering department, you will serve as a key technical interface between design engineering and manufacturing for AMD Data Center GPU products. This is not a primary mechanical design role; instead, the position requires deep understanding of AMD mechanical architectures, assemblies, tolerances, and validation intent to ensure that manufacturing and production partners can correctly build, inspect, and test hardware at scale. You will help drive manufacturing readiness for mechanical aspects of the product, translate design intent into clear production test and debug expectations, and help resolve issues discovered during bring-up, pilot builds, and high-volume manufacturing. To succeed in this role, you will work cross-functionally with mechanical design, board engineering, package engineering, validation, quality, operations, suppliers, and manufacturing partners, while influencing execution across internal and external teams. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate is a strong technical leader with excellent communication, planning, and problem-solving skills, and with the credibility to work effectively across engineering, operations, and external manufacturing teams. They should be comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment, making sound technical judgments with incomplete information, and driving issues to closure across organizational boundaries. This person will combine solid mechanical engineering fundamentals with practical manufacturing knowledge, including how hardware is built, tested, debugged, and ramped into production. Experience working with server, rack, and data center hardware, along with familiarity with global manufacturing environments, is highly desirable. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: The Senior Mechanical Product Engineer in the DPEG Mechanical Engineering team will play a critical role in ensuring successful product industrialization and production execution. The successful candidate will partner closely with design teams in Austin and with manufacturing partners to ensure mechanical design intent is clearly understood and translated into robust manufacturing, inspection, and test processes. This role requires strong technical depth, cross-functional influence, and a systems-level perspective spanning silicon integration, board and system hardware, manufacturing process readiness, and field-relevant failure analysis. The position is ideally based in Austin, Texas to enable close collaboration with the core design team and a local manufacturing site, with periodic travel to Asia—especially Taiwan—including potential multi-week trips during key build and ramp phases. Core responsibilities include understanding mechanical designs well enough to identify critical-to-function features, reviewing manufacturing and test plans for alignment with design intent, and enabling production partners to correctly inspect, assemble, and test AMD hardware. The role will support debug and root-cause analysis of issues found during prototype builds, qualification, and manufacturing, and will help drive corrective actions across design, quality, supplier, and factory teams. This person will also help define readiness criteria, close manufacturability gaps, and improve processes that increase product robustness, test coverage, and speed to production. The role requires initiative, strong independent judgment, and the ability to make technical tradeoffs while balancing schedule, quality, and manufacturability. The selected candidate should have the ability to influence technical direction and execution across internal teams and external partners, communicate clearly with both engineering and manufacturing audiences, and drive closure on complex production issues. They will be expected to identify systemic gaps, champion continuous improvement, and introduce scalable approaches that improve manufacturing readiness, test effectiveness, and overall product quality. The following defines successful performance criteria for the position: Manufacturing Readiness and Commercialization – The Senior Mechanical Product Engineer will bridge design, product development, and manufacturing execution to ensure products are ready for successful ramp and sustained production. The role will help translate design intent into factory-ready processes, test methods, and debug plans that support commercially viable delivery in a timely and cost-effective manner. Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement – The role is expected to drive improvements in manufacturing support processes, issue resolution workflows, and production test effectiveness while helping teams execute with speed, quality, and discipline during product introduction and ramp. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: The Senior Mechanical Product Engineer must have demonstrated technical leadership, sound engineering judgment, and a track record of improving how complex hardware products transition from design into manufacturing. The selected candidate will use proven engineering and productization skills to strengthen manufacturing readiness, improve debug and root-cause effectiveness, and help ensure that internal teams and external partners can execute with clarity and confidence. Critical Experiences & Competencies for Success: Technical Leadership Experience - Extensive experience serving as a technical lead in a large, fast-paced engineering environment, with responsibility for driving cross-functional execution across design, validation, manufacturing, and operations. The candidate should be comfortable leading through influence, managing ambiguity, and resolving complex issues across multiple programs in parallel. Technical Experience - Strong understanding of mechanical design principles, design for manufacturability, tolerance management, and how mechanical features translate into manufacturing and production test requirements. The selected candidate should have experience with complex hardware products and be able to interpret design intent at the component, board, and system levels in order to support factory enablement, product debug, and failure analysis. Mechanical Analysis and Tools - Working knowledge of statistical analysis, structural analysis, finite element analysis, and tolerance analysis is valuable, along with CAD fluency in tools such as SolidWorks or Creo. The ideal candidate does not need to be the primary designer, but must be able to understand, review, and communicate design details effectively in support of manufacturing and debug activities. Manufacturing Test and Debug - Experience supporting hardware builds, manufacturing test readiness, debug, and root-cause investigation is required. The candidate should be comfortable working with factory teams, contract manufacturers, suppliers, and internal labs to resolve issues related to assembly, fit, function, reliability, or production escapes, and to help define effective screening and verification approaches. Strategic Thinking - The candidate must be skilled at identifying systemic manufacturing and productization risks, prioritizing high-impact issues, and implementing practical solutions in a dynamic, high-tech environment with significant uncertainty. Collaboration and Communication - Effective collaboration across design engineering, operations, quality, vendors, and manufacturing partners is critical for success. The role requires clear communication, strong follow-through, and the ability to build alignment across geographically distributed teams and cultures. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: BS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field, with significant industry experience in mechanical engineering, product engineering, manufacturing support, or hardware productization. An advanced engineering degree is a plus. LOCATION: Austin, Texas (preferred). This role requires travel to Taiwan and other manufacturing locations as needed, including potential multi-week trips during key development, build, and production ramp periods. The position is ideally based in Austin, Texas to enable close collaboration with the core design team and a local manufacturing site, with periodic travel to Asia—especially Taiwan—including potential multi-week trips during key build and ramp phases. Core responsibilities include understanding mechanical designs well enough to identify critical-to-function features, reviewing manufacturing and test plans for alignment with design intent, and enabling production partners to correctly inspect, assemble, and test AMD hardware. The role will support debug and root-cause analysis of issues found during prototype builds, qualification, and manufacturing, and will help drive corrective actions across design, quality, supplier, and factory teams. This person will also help define readiness criteria, close manufacturability gaps, and improve processes that increase product robustness, test coverage, and speed to production. The role requires initiative, strong independent judgment, and the ability to make technical tradeoffs while balancing schedule, quality, and manufacturability. The selected candidate should have the ability to influence technical direction and execution across internal teams and external partners, communicate clearly with both engineering and manufacturing audiences, and drive closure on complex production issues. They will be expected to identify systemic gaps, champion continuous improvement, and introduce scalable approaches that improve manufacturing readiness, test effectiveness, and overall product quality. The following defines successful performance criteria for the position: Manufacturing Readiness and Commercialization – The Senior Mechanical Product Engineer will bridge design, product development, and manufacturing execution to ensure products are ready for successful ramp and sustained production. The role will help translate design intent into factory-ready processes, test methods, and debug plans that support commercially viable delivery in a timely and cost-effective manner. Operational Excellence and Continuous Improvement – The role is expected to drive improvements in manufacturing support processes, issue resolution workflows, and production test effectiveness while helping teams execute with speed, quality, and discipline during product introduction and ramp. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: The Senior Mechanical Product Engineer must have demonstrated technical leadership, sound engineering judgment, and a track record of improving how complex hardware products transition from design into manufacturing. The selected candidate will use proven engineering and productization skills to strengthen manufacturing readiness, improve debug and root-cause effectiveness, and help ensure that internal teams and external partners can execute with clarity and confidence. Critical Experiences & Competencies for Success: Technical Leadership Experience - Extensive experience serving as a technical lead in a large, fast-paced engineering environment, with responsibility for driving cross-functional execution across design, validation, manufacturing, and operations. The candidate should be comfortable leading through influence, managing ambiguity, and resolving complex issues across multiple programs in parallel. Technical Experience - Strong understanding of mechanical design principles, design for manufacturability, tolerance management, and how mechanical features translate into manufacturing and production test requirements. The selected candidate should have experience with complex hardware products and be able to interpret design intent at the component, board, and system levels in order to support factory enablement, product debug, and failure analysis. Mechanical Analysis and Tools - Working knowledge of statistical analysis, structural analysis, finite element analysis, and tolerance analysis is valuable, along with CAD fluency in tools such as SolidWorks or Creo. The ideal candidate does not need to be the primary designer, but must be able to understand, review, and communicate design details effectively in support of manufacturing and debug activities. Manufacturing Test and Debug - Experience supporting hardware builds, manufacturing test readiness, debug, and root-cause investigation is required. The candidate should be comfortable working with factory teams, contract manufacturers, suppliers, and internal labs to resolve issues related to assembly, fit, function, reliability, or production escapes, and to help define effective screening and verification approaches. Strategic Thinking - The candidate must be skilled at identifying systemic manufacturing and productization risks, prioritizing high-impact issues, and implementing practical solutions in a dynamic, high-tech environment with significant uncertainty. Collaboration and Communication - Effective collaboration across design engineering, operations, quality, vendors, and manufacturing partners is critical for success. The role requires clear communication, strong follow-through, and the ability to build alignment across geographically distributed teams and cultures. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: BS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field, with significant industry experience in mechanical engineering, product engineering, manufacturing support, or hardware productization. An advanced engineering degree is a plus. LOCATION: Austin, Texas (preferred).
