amd-88457.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: Join AMD’s Data Center Platform Engineering Group (DPEG) Thermal Mechanical Engineering team and help shape the cooling technologies behind next-generation Data Center GPU products. In this highly collaborative, hands-on environment, you will work with silicon, package, board, power, validation, manufacturing, and external partner teams to transform product requirements into high-performance, reliable, and scalable thermal solutions. This role offers the opportunity to work across the full product lifecycle, from early concept and computational modeling through cold-plate development, laboratory validation, and production. You will deepen your expertise in advanced liquid cooling, electronics thermal management, and GPU platform design while contributing to one of AMD’s most strategic growth areas. THE PERSON: You are a technically curious and collaborative engineer who enjoys solving complex thermal challenges and turning analysis into practical product solutions. You communicate clearly across engineering disciplines, balance multiple priorities, and are comfortable working directly with internal teams and external vendors. You bring strong ownership, sound engineering judgment, attention to detail, and a willingness to learn new tools and cooling technologies in a fast-paced product-development environment. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Design and develop thermal solutions for next-generation AMD Data Center GPU products, with an emphasis on liquid cooling and cold-plate technologies. Build and analyze thermal and CFD models using tools such as ANSYS Icepak, AEDT, or equivalent, and translate results into actionable design recommendations. Partner with silicon, package, board, power, mechanical, validation, manufacturing, and vendor teams to deliver chip-, card-, and system-level thermal-mechanical solutions. Support thermal characterization and hands-on laboratory validation, including correlation of simulation results with physical test data and resolution of performance gaps. Drive thermal design activities across the product lifecycle, from initial requirements and concept development through qualification and production readiness. Evaluate emerging cooling technologies, components, and supplier capabilities to support future product roadmaps and scalable data center solutions. Within the first 90 days, learn the team’s tools, products, and development processes and begin contributing to simulation, design, or validation activities. Within the first year, independently own thermal deliverables for an assigned product or project and contribute to team knowledge sharing and mentoring. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Strong foundation in heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and electronics cooling. Experience with computational fluid dynamics and thermal-analysis tools such as ANSYS Icepak, AEDT, Fluent, or equivalent. Candidates with strong fundamentals and experience using comparable tools are encouraged to apply. Knowledge of air- and liquid-cooling technologies, including cold plates and thermal management for high-power electronics. Familiarity with thermal-management components such as thermal interface materials, heat sinks, vapor chambers, heat pipes, fans, and liquid distribution systems. Experience with GPU, server, rack, data center, semiconductor, or other high-performance electronics thermal design is desired. Hands-on thermal laboratory testing, instrumentation, data analysis, and simulation-to-test correlation experience. Familiarity with CAD tools such as Creo or SolidWorks and scripting or analysis tools such as Python, MATLAB, C, or C++ is a plus. Experience collaborating with cross-functional engineering teams and external vendors or suppliers. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: BS, MS, or PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Thermal Engineering, or a related engineering discipline is preferred. LOCATION: Secaucus, New Jersey. amd-89258.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology can change lives for the better. It can heal us, entertain us, and make us more connected, productive, and understanding of the world around us. And we’re looking for talent who feel the same: people who want to leave the planet better than they found it, those who don’t shy away from humanity’s challenges but are determined to help solve them. AMD is powering the next generation of supercomputing, high-performance computing, cloud, and AI. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or creating go-to-market plans, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. THE ROLE: AMD’s Data Center Platform Engineering Group (DPEG) designs, builds, and delivers industry‑leading technology platforms that power the world’s most advanced cloud, AI, and telecom infrastructures. We develop cloud‑enabling server platforms and system solutions that allow the world’s leading companies to transform ideas into reality at global scale. Our customers are forward‑looking, and so are we continuously innovating to stay ahead of the next technological challenge. As part of the Data Center Platform Engineering organization, the Staff Product Development Technical Program Manager will lead the management and execution of AI server and hyperscale server platform programs with significant customer and business impact. This role is responsible for driving system‑level hardware execution across the full product lifecycle, from early product definition and architecture through design, validation, production release, ramp, and end‑of‑life. The ideal candidate will operate as a system‑level leader and integrator, coordinating complex, cross‑functional teams to deliver high‑quality, manufacturable, and scalable server platforms that meet aggressive schedule, cost, and quality targets. THE PERSON: You are a hardware‑focused Technical Program Manager with strong system‑level instincts and the ability to lead highly complex programs that span electrical, mechanical, power, thermal, manufacturing, and supply chain domains. You work closely with System Architecture, Engineering, Reliability, Compliance, and Business and Account Teams to translate platform requirements and product specifications into clear, executable hardware programs with well‑defined milestones, risks, and deliverables. You lead cross‑functional hardware execution teams to plan, develop, validate, and launch server platforms on schedule, ensuring alignment across engineering, firmware/BIOS, manufacturing, quality, operations, and supplier organizations. You excel at driving clarity in ambiguous environments, defining program structure, execution plans, and decision frameworks that enable teams to move quickly while managing technical and operational risk. You are comfortable operating at multiple levels from detailed hardware execution reviews to executive‑level program discussions and can clearly articulate tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations to senior stakeholders. You bring a strong ownership mindset, proactively identifying issues, driving resolution across organizations, and holding teams accountable for delivery without relying on formal authority. You naturally mentor and influence others, helping raise the bar for program rigor, system‑level thinking, and execution excellence across the organization. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Own system‑level technical program strategy and execution across feature delivery, product quality, and continuity of supply, balancing technical trade‑offs, customer requirements, and business priorities across the full product lifecycle. Drive cross‑functional alignment between Engineering, Product Management, Sales, Operations, and Supply Chain, translating platform capabilities, system constraints, and roadmap strategy into executable plans that support customer commitments and business outcomes. Lead execution of highly complex, multi‑disciplinary system solutions, spanning Printed Circuit Board Assemblies (PCBAs), mechanical architecture, power and thermals, operating systems, BMC, BIOS, solution software, diagnostics, validation, and test while coordinating internal teams and external vendors to meet cost, quality, and schedule objectives. Act as a system‑level integrator, ensuring alignment across hardware, firmware, and software architectures, proactively managing inter‑team dependencies and surfacing systemic risks early. Ensure designs meet manufacturability, reliability, serviceability, and scalability requirements, partnering closely with manufacturing, quality, and supplier teams to enable production readiness and long‑term lifecycle sustainability. Establish and lead core execution mechanisms, including weekly program reviews and milestone checkpoints with global, cross‑functional stakeholders, driving accountability, resolving escalations, and ensuring on‑time milestone delivery. Identify, assess, and communicate program risks at the system level, defining mitigation plans and driving cross‑functional hardware and software solutions to minimize impact to schedule, cost, quality, and supply continuity. Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, providing clear, data‑driven program status, decision trade‑offs, and escalation paths for high‑impact system and execution issues. Own program governance, documentation, and communications throughout the development lifecycle, ensuring timely, accurate dissemination of decisions, execution status, and deliverables to internal stakeholders, customers, and partners. Define, track, and publish program metrics and KPIs, using quantitative insights to support execution reviews, continuous improvement, and program health reporting. Lead Bill of Materials (BOM) strategy and execution from early prototype through production, facilitating BOM reviews to ensure technical integrity, cost optimization, supplier readiness, and alignment with manufacturing and sourcing strategies. Partner with engineering and configuration management teams to manage BOM lifecycle transitions, ensuring disciplined change control, traceability, and alignment from preliminary design through high‑volume manufacturing. Mentor and influence other Technical Program Managers and technical leads, elevating execution rigor, system‑level thinking, and operational excellence across the organization. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Proven experience owning system‑level hardware programs across the full development lifecycle, from architecture definition and early prototyping through production ramp and sustaining. Strong technical depth in hardware systems, including experience with one or more of the following: Demonstrated ability to manage cross‑functional execution across hardware engineering, BMC/BIOS, manufacturing, quality, operations, and supply chain teams. Experience driving design for manufacturability, reliability, and serviceability, working closely with manufacturing engineers, suppliers, and contract manufacturers. Hands‑on experience managing Bill of Materials (BOM) lifecycle, including prototype, pre‑production, and production stages, with disciplined change control and configuration management. Strong program leadership and communication skills, with a track record of driving alignment, resolving escalations, and influencing without formal authority across multiple organizations. Data‑driven decision‑making capability, including defining and tracking hardware execution metrics, risk burndown, and program health indicators Customer-facing experience, supporting launch readiness, field quality investigations, or hardware execution discussions with strategic customers or partners. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline. Advanced degree (MS) in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field is preferred. Formal project management education, PMP / Scrum Master LOCATION: Austin, TX or Secaucus, NJ This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. #LI-KW1 Benefits offered are described: AMD benefits at a glance. amd-87311.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: As a CPU Core Performance Engineer, you will have a unique opportunity to architect, design and model performance features in AMD’s next-generation CPU core. You will work in the center of an experienced, skilled, and motivated engineering team with a track record of success. As a member of the CPU Core performance team, you will work on the leading edge of processor technology to define CPU Architecture and collaborate with RTL design, Verification and Post-Silicon teams to make AMD’s ambitious future CPU roadmap a reality. THE PERSON: You approach challenges relentlessly with both critical thinking and creativity. You work as part of a team with strong problem-solving, communication and collaboration skills. You have a solid understanding of modern CPU architecture, a solid track-record delivering complex performance features for modern CPU cores and have ideas and a drive to make it even better. Does this describe you? If so, then join us! KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Drive the architecture, design, modeling, and optimization of CPU core performance features using high-performance simulation environments. Develop and enhance CPU performance models to evaluate new microarchitectural features and guide architecture decisions. Analyze workloads, traces, and performance data to identify opportunities for CPU performance improvements. Build and maintain cycle-accurate CPU performance models and correlate results across architectural models, RTL, emulation, and silicon. Perform pre-silicon and post-silicon performance analysis to validate feature behavior and drive model accuracy. Lead performance correlation, root-cause analysis, and optimization efforts across the CPU development lifecycle. Provide technical leadership, mentor engineers, and drive execution to meet project milestones and customer commitments. Collaborate closely with architecture, design, verification, emulation, and silicon teams to deliver industry-leading CPU products. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Strong background in CPU architecture, microarchitecture, and performance modeling, with a proven track record of delivering innovative performance features. Experience modeling and analyzing modern CPU core performance across one or more pipeline domains. Demonstrated ability to identify performance bottlenecks, design experiments, analyze complex workloads, and drive performance improvements through data-driven insights. Proven success solving challenging architecture and microarchitecture problems from concept and feature definition through modeling, validation, and product delivery. Strong software engineering skills, including the use of modern development practices and AI-assisted tools to develop, validate, and optimize performance models. Experience working effectively across globally distributed teams and collaborating with cross-functional engineering organizations. Strong technical leadership, mentoring, and coaching skills, with the ability to influence technical direction and execution. Excellent communication and presentation skills, including the ability to convey complex technical concepts to engineers, architects, and leadership; publications and industry conference presentations are a plus. THE ROLE Join a System IP team developing critical boot firmware that enables system-on-chip (SoC) initialization across a wide range of products. In this role, you will own low-level boot code that runs at power-on, making it one of the first and most essential components in the system lifecycle. You will work at the intersection of firmware and hardware in a pre-silicon environment, translating architecture requirements into code, supporting simulation and validation efforts, and collaborating closely with design and verification teams. THE ROLE: As a key contributor to AMD's quality and reliability initiatives, you will drive supplier and manufacturing excellence for next-generation switch products supporting AI, cloud, and high-performance computing solutions. You will lead data-driven quality improvements, supplier engagement, advanced analytics initiatives, and customer-focused problem resolution while influencing quality, reliability, and process improvements across global operations. You will also lead quality readiness assessments and manufacturing quality execution during NPI transitions and production ramp. THE PERSON: The successful candidate is a highly motivated quality leader with deep expertise in networking hardware, supplier quality, and manufacturing processes. They possess strong technical knowledge of switch systems, paired with exceptional analytical, communication, and leadership skills. This individual thrives in complex, fast-paced environments, effectively driving cross-functional collaboration, influencing stakeholders at all levels, and partnering closely with suppliers and customers to resolve challenging quality issues. They are passionate about using data-driven insights to improve product quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Drive supplier and internal technical organizations, including design, assembly, manufacturing, and product testing teams, to achieve high-quality product releases through review of test plans, qualification results, failure rates, DFx, xFMEA, NUDD, and supplier-led failure analysis. Coordinate and manage quality activities with a focus on issue resolution, part approval, process control, quality assurance during NPI, advancement of analytics capabilities, risk identification, and mitigation planning. Drive quality improvements related to design, materials, and manufacturing processes throughout the product lifecycle, ensuring critical quality data and test telemetry are sourced from system integrators and customers. Monitor factory and field nonconformance metrics for switch products, including manufacturing yield, first-pass yield excursions, hardware replacement rates, and field quality performance, while driving process improvements and corrective actions. Lead root cause investigations and corrective action implementation utilizing 8D, 5-Why, statistical analysis, and industry-standard quality methodologies. Collect and analyze large amounts of data to identify product and process performance trends, providing actionable recommendations to improve quality, reliability, and operational efficiency. Drive switch debug and issue resolution activities involving both firmware and hardware defects. Define switch supplier build report expectations, including reporting frequency, required quality metrics, expected data, yield monitoring, and escalation requirements. Manage field and customer escalations as the primary quality interface with suppliers, driving containment, root cause identification, corrective actions, and long-term resolution of quality excursions. Serve as an advocate for the customer through deep manufacturing knowledge, timely follow-through, and strong customer focus. Capture supplier and customer feedback, track lessons learned and drive continuous improvement in quality and reliability performance against AMD and customer requirements. Travel to supplier locations as needed to support manufacturing quality initiatives, supplier audits, investigations, and continuous improvement activities. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Strong technical understanding of switch architectures, networking systems, AI fabric interconnects, and system-level quality concepts. Experience applying DFx, xFMEA, NUDD, root cause analysis methodologies, statistical process control principles, reliability testing, failure analysis, and corrective action processes. Experience supporting cloud service providers, hyperscale customers, networking OEMs, AI infrastructure deployments, or data center networking environments. Proven experience developing process quality plans and driving effective 8D corrective and preventive actions in complex hardware manufacturing environments. Proven experience leading quality excursions and resolving complex manufacturing, supplier, field, customer, and product quality issues, including executive-level quality reviews and management of critical customer escalations. Strong analytical skills with the ability to derive data-driven insights from large datasets, switch telemetry, manufacturing yield metrics, field quality data, and automated test infrastructure, and influence technical decision-making. Experience working with Original Design Manufacturers (ODMs), Contract Manufacturers (CMs), and suppliers to establish manufacturing quality requirements, drive accountability, and improve operational quality performance. Experience supporting New Product Introduction (NPI), manufacturing ramp, and production readiness activities, including design validation testing (DVT), qualification reviews, process validation, risk assessments, yield improvement initiatives, and deployment of quality control plans. Ability to effectively interface with all levels of an organization, including executive leadership, customers, suppliers, and cross-functional technical teams. Demonstrated leadership skills with the ability to organize, prioritize, and drive complex issues to closure in fast-paced matrix environments. Experience with data center switch platforms, merchant silicon switch architectures (Broadcom, NVIDIA, Marvell, or equivalent), high-speed optical interconnects, rack-scale networking solutions, AI networking infrastructure, or hyperscale networking environments is highly desirable. Familiarity with hardware and firmware interaction within complex networking platforms, including troubleshooting system-level integration, interoperability, platform reliability issues, and reliability qualification methodologies such as HALT, HASS, environmental stress testing, and accelerated life testing. Experience defining supplier quality scorecards, manufacturing KPI dashboards, escalation frameworks, and quality management processes to drive measurable quality improvements. Experience with Microsoft Power BI, Tableau, JIRA, or similar analytics and reporting tools. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a strong sense of urgency, self-motivation, and customer focus. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Engineering, or a related technical discipline. SENIOR PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT ENGINEER , PRODUCT OPERATIONS THE ROLE: AMD Design is seeking a Product Development Engineer, Product Operations, to join our Datacenter Platform Engineering Group. In this role, you will drive the development and manufacturing launch of cutting-edge datacenter hardware (server and rack systems). You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to ensure new products meet design standards, quality targets, and production timelines. This is a high-impact role offering the opportunity to be at the forefront of datacenter hardware innovation. If you are detail-oriented, quality-focused, and excited about coordinating complex technical projects from design through production, we encourage you to apply and join our team at AMD’s Datacenter Platform Engineering Group! THE PERSON: This position is ideal for an engineer with a strong background in product development, manufacturing processes, and cross-team project coordination, who is eager to take a visible role in launching high-quality datacenter products. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, quality-focused, and excited about coordinating complex technical projects from design through production. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with diverse teams (Engineering Design, Materials, Rack/Server Systems Program Management, etc.) to align design, materials planning, manufacturing, and quality efforts throughout the product development lifecycle. Design & DFM Reviews: Review design specifications, CAD drawings, and documentation to ensure compliance with design criteria, industry standards, and manufacturing capabilities. Lead Design for Manufacturability (DFM) reviews to ensure products are optimized for efficient, high-quality production. Project Scheduling & Readiness: Develop and maintain project schedules and implementation of readiness timelines to support on-time new product introductions. Communicate project status and readiness milestones to customer program management teams and internal stakeholders. New Product Introduction (NPI) Leadership: Drive NPI processes by facilitating and leading cross-functional problem-solving meetings with Design, Manufacturing, Test, and Quality Engineering teams. Proactively identify and resolve any design or production issues, ensuring smooth product launch and ramp-up. Technical Design Reviews: Establish and lead regular development review meetings to deepen technical understanding and coordinate design changes. Provide guidance and feedback during design reviews, ensuring feasibility and alignment with manufacturing processes and capabilities. Prototype & First Article Oversight: Oversee first article builds and First Article Inspections (FAI) for new products. Document FAI requirements, analyze initial build results, and implement improvements to validate product design and manufacturing readiness. Production Support & Change Management: Coordinate engineering rework and change orders during the transition to volume production. Manage Engineering Change Order (ECO) processes effectively to incorporate design updates or fixes, minimizing impact on production schedules. Assembly Process Validation: Validate and approve production assembly instructions (including labeling and work instructions) to ensure clarity and accuracy for manufacturing teams. Make sure assembly processes are properly documented and optimized for quality and efficiency. Quality & Delivery Assurance: Ensure that final products meet all customer specifications and quality standards. Work closely with quality and production teams to confirm products are built correctly and delivered on schedule, fostering smooth ramp-up of new server and rack systems into high-volume production. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Hands-on experience guiding products from concept through development and production. Knowledge of physical design (PD) methodologies for hardware or systems. Familiarity with server architectures or rack-level hardware systems and their components. Ability to conduct Design for Manufacturability (DFM) reviews and optimize designs for efficient manufacturing. Experience managing Engineering Change Order (ECO) processes and implementing design updates in a production environment. Understanding of printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) manufacturing processes and best practices. Strong documentation skills, including experience creating and maintaining comprehensive engineering documentation and Bill of Materials (BOM). Proven ability to interpret and review engineering drawings, schematics, and specifications to ensure design accuracy and manufacturability. Hands-on experience working in a manufacturing or factory environment, especially in a fast-paced, dynamic NPI setting, with a history of successfully launching new hardware products. Excellent communication and collaboration skills. Demonstrated ability to lead meetings, coordinate across multiple teams, and drive projects to completion in a timely manner. Minimum of 1 year of relevant industry experience in product development engineering or a closely related hardware engineering role, including work with design and manufacturing processes for complex hardware products (datacenter, servers, or similar). amd-86744.text: WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career. THE ROLE: Triton is a widely adopted language and compiler for high-performance GPU kernels, powering major AI frameworks such as PyTorch, vLLM, and SGLang. As AI workloads increasingly rely on Triton-based kernels, first-class Triton support is strategically critical to AMD’s AI software roadmap. AMD GPUs are an official Triton backend; delivering industry-leading Triton performance on AMD Instinct accelerators is a top priority for AMD. The performance and usability of Triton directly impact the competitiveness of AMD hardware in large-scale AI training and inference. In this role you will author state-of-the-art performant Triton/Gluon kernels for ML kernels powering the latest and greatest AI models. You will collaborate with research, compiler, and hardware architecture teams to co-design high-performance solutions, analyze bottlenecks to make AMD GPUs the best-in-class platform for Triton-powered AI workloads. THE PERSON: The ideal candidate has deep expertise in SIMT programming, parallel algorithms, GPU architecture, and performance engineering. You are comfortable working across the full stack to drive e2e model performance — from vLLM/SGL down to ISA-level performance tuning — and can perform rigorous quantitative analysis to drive measurable improvements. You thrive in highly technical environments, enjoy solving complex performance problems, and are excited to collaborate across model deployment, compiler, runtime, and hardware teams. Most importantly, you are curious, hands-on, and willing to learn and work across boundaries. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Design, research, implement, and rigorously optimize high-performance matmul, attention (flash, paged, grouped-query), MoE, and fully fused transformer kernels using Triton, targeting large-scale LLM and multimodal workloads Own and productionize critical Triton/Gluon kernels within vLLM and SGL (e.g., paged attention, extend attention, MoE, quantized kernels, etc), ensuring correctness, scalability, and peak throughput Partner closely with compiler engineers to develop and maintain the Triton AMD backend across ROCm and the LLVM AMDGPU stack, targeting CDNA and next-generation architectures Drive deep kernel-level optimizations across the AMD memory hierarchy (LDS, L2, HBM), wavefront execution (wave32/wave64), vectorization, MFMA utilization, occupancy tuning, and instruction scheduling to maximize hardware efficiency Perform rigorous profiling and microbenchmarking led optimization on AMD Instinct GPUs using hardware counters and tracing tools; root-cause bottlenecks in memory bandwidth, latency hiding, synchronization, and register pressure Debug and resolve performance and correctness issues end-to-end across PyTorch, vLLM/SGL runtimes, Triton IR/MLIR, ROCm runtime, and the LLVM AMDGPU backend Contribute to open-source Triton, LLVM, and ROCm ecosystems PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Deep experience in GPU kernel development, compiler backends, or performance engineering focused on AI/ML workloads Strong hands-on expertise with Triton, including writing custom matmul, attention, and fused transformer kernels and understanding Triton IR lowering to GPU backends Deep understanding of modern GPU architectures (wavefront execution, memory hierarchy, scheduling, occupancy) Meaningful contributions to open-source projects such as Triton, Torch, vLLM, SGLang, IREE, MLIR, LLVM, or ROCm, with a strong collaborative and upstream-first engineering mindset PREFERRED ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. amd-92482.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. We are seeking a highly experienced Principal Engineer for Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) and Near-Packaged Optics (NPO) to lead the architecture, design, implementation, integration, and validation of next-generation optical interconnect solutions for AI scale-up and scale-out platforms. This role will provide end-to-end technical leadership across optical engines, high-speed electrical interfaces, ASIC integration, package and board design, signal integrity, power integrity, thermal and mechanical design, firmware, diagnostics, and system-level validation. The successful candidate will translate platform requirements into robust CPO and NPO architectures and drive those architectures from early concept and specification development through design implementation, platform bring-up, qualification, and production readiness. The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in CPO and NPO system architecture, silicon photonics, optical-engine integration, 100G and 200G per-lane PAM4 interfaces, 400G, 800G, and 1.6T optical technologies, high-speed SerDes, channel design, FEC, link performance, and system-level debug. You will collaborate closely with architecture, ASIC, package, board, signal integrity, power integrity, thermal, mechanical, firmware, diagnostics, platform engineering, manufacturing, reliability, and external technology partners. You will establish technical requirements, resolve complex cross-domain issues, and influence AMD’s long-term optical interconnect architecture and technology roadmap. Lead the architecture, design, implementation, integration, and validation of CPO and NPO solutions for next-generation AI scale-up and scale-out platforms. Define end-to-end system requirements for CPO and NPO implementations, including optical, electrical, mechanical, thermal, power, firmware, reliability, serviceability, and manufacturing requirements. Own the technical development of CPO and NPO solutions from early feasibility studies and architecture definition through detailed design, prototype bring-up, qualification, and production readiness. Develop and maintain CPO and NPO interface specifications, including optical-engine interfaces, high-speed electrical interfaces, management interfaces, control sequencing, reference clocks, reset behavior, fault handling, telemetry, and diagnostics. Lead the integration of optical engines, electrical integrated circuits, ASICs, packages, substrates, sockets, host boards, interposers, connectors, fibers, external laser sources, cooling solutions, and mechanical retention structures. Define and optimize 100G and 200G per-lane PAM4 electrical and optical link architectures supporting 400G, 800G, 1.6T, and future interconnect solutions. Establish electrical channel budgets and performance requirements for package, socket, connector, board, cable, and optical-engine interfaces. Drive SerDes and link optimization, including TX and RX equalization, link training, eye analysis, jitter analysis, BER characterization, FEC performance, latency, margining, and long-term link stability. Define optical link budgets and performance requirements, including transmitter power, extinction ratio, optical modulation amplitude, receiver sensitivity, stressed receiver performance, return loss, reflectance, insertion loss, crosstalk, and fiber connectivity. Evaluate architectural tradeoffs among CPO, NPO, onboard optics, pluggable optics, linear pluggable optics, retimed optics, co-packaged copper, and other emerging interconnect technologies. Lead system-level feasibility and tradeoff studies covering bandwidth density, reach, latency, power efficiency, thermal performance, reliability, manufacturability, serviceability, cost, and time to market. Partner with ASIC and SerDes teams to define electrical interface requirements, channel assumptions, equalization capabilities, link-training behavior, FEC architecture, clocking strategy, and diagnostic features. Collaborate with package, board, SI, and PI teams to optimize high-speed channel performance, power delivery, reference-clock quality, crosstalk, jitter tolerance, and overall link margin. Work with thermal and mechanical engineering teams to define cooling, heat-spreading, fiber-routing, connectorization, mechanical-tolerance, assembly, and serviceability requirements. Define external laser source architectures and requirements, including optical power delivery, laser safety, redundancy, control, monitoring, connectorization, fiber management, and fault handling. Develop comprehensive design verification and validation plans for component, subsystem, and full-platform testing. Drive electrical and optical characterization using advanced laboratory equipment, including DCA-X systems, BERTs, real-time oscilloscopes, optical spectrum analyzers, optical power meters, VNA and TDR systems, and compliance test platforms. Define validation methodologies for BER, FEC performance, eye margin, jitter, channel margin, link stability, traffic stress, thermal corners, voltage corners, process variation, fault recovery, and long-duration operation. Lead interoperability, compliance, and ecosystem validation activities with optical-engine suppliers, silicon photonics providers, connector and fiber vendors, laser suppliers, manufacturing partners, and system customers. Ensure alignment with applicable IEEE, OIF, CMIS, MSA, and industry standards while identifying areas where CPO and NPO implementations require platform-specific requirements or extensions. Develop reference architectures, design guidelines, interface-control documents, validation specifications, compliance methodologies, and integration best practices. Drive implementation readiness through architecture reviews, design reviews, schematic and layout reviews, SI and PI reviews, thermal reviews, FMEA activities, validation reviews, and production-readiness assessments. Identify critical technical risks and develop mitigation plans related to link margin, thermal performance, power delivery, optical coupling, fiber attach, external laser operation, component variation, aging, reliability, manufacturing yield, and field serviceability. Partner with manufacturing, quality, and reliability teams to define qualification requirements, test coverage, screening strategies, failure-analysis processes, and production monitoring. Develop Python-based automation for test execution, equipment control, data collection, statistical analysis, characterization, visualization, and reporting. Drive issue resolution and technical closure with external suppliers and ecosystem partners, including clear ownership, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and validation of implemented fixes. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Extensive experience in optical networking, silicon photonics, high-speed hardware design, SerDes architecture, optical-system integration, package or board design, or system-level interconnect development. Significant experience leading complex hardware technologies from architecture and specification through implementation, validation, qualification, and production deployment. Deep understanding of CPO, NPO, onboard optics, optical-engine architectures, silicon photonics, external laser sources, and high-density fiber connectivity. Hands-on experience with 100G and 200G per-lane PAM4 electrical and optical interfaces. Strong knowledge of 400G, 800G, 1.6T, and emerging next-generation optical interconnect technologies. Expertise in high-speed SerDes operation, including TX and RX equalization, link training, eye diagrams, jitter analysis, BER testing, FEC, error monitoring, and margin characterization. Strong understanding of electrical channel design, including insertion loss, return loss, crosstalk, impedance discontinuities, package loss, socket loss, PCB loss, connector performance, and channel operating margin. Strong understanding of optical-link engineering, including optical power budgets, transmitter and receiver performance, optical modulation, receiver sensitivity, stressed-eye performance, fiber loss, connector loss, reflectance, crosstalk, and wavelength-dependent behavior. Experience defining high-speed electrical and optical interface specifications, compliance points, test methodologies, and validation limits. Knowledge of FEC architectures, pre-FEC BER, post-FEC BER, error distributions, burst-error behavior, FEC latency, link-layer retry, and system-level reliability tradeoffs. Experience integrating optical engines or high-speed electrical devices near or within ASIC packages, including package, substrate, socket, board, connector, power, thermal, and mechanical considerations. Familiarity with external laser source architectures, laser safety, redundancy, control, power monitoring, fiber routing, and optical fault handling. Working knowledge of IEEE Ethernet standards, OIF implementation agreements, CMIS, relevant MSAs, and high-speed electrical and optical compliance methodologies. Hands-on experience with high-speed laboratory equipment, including DCA-X systems, BERTs, real-time oscilloscopes, optical spectrum analyzers, optical power meters, VNA and TDR systems, and thermal characterization tools. Strong understanding of signal integrity and power integrity fundamentals, including jitter, noise, crosstalk, power-rail variation, reference-clock quality, channel margin, and their impact on high-speed link performance. Experience with thermal and mechanical design considerations for high-density optical integration, including cooling, heat spreading, fiber routing, connector access, assembly tolerances, and serviceability. Experience with component and system-level reliability analysis, including design margins, environmental stress, aging, failure mechanisms, FMEA, qualification planning, and production monitoring. Proven ability to lead complex system bring-up and debug activities across ASIC, package, board, optical, firmware, software, mechanical, thermal, and platform teams. Experience collaborating with optical-engine suppliers, silicon photonics providers, laser suppliers, connector and fiber vendors, manufacturing partners, standards organizations, customers, and ecosystem partners. Proficiency in Python or similar programming languages for laboratory automation, data analysis, visualization, and reporting. Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to resolve complex multidisciplinary issues. Strong technical leadership and mentoring skills, with demonstrated success influencing teams beyond direct organizational boundaries. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical information to engineering teams, senior leadership, customers, and external partners. ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Photonics, Applied Physics, or a related technical discipline. THE ROLE: As a Lead IP Verification Engineer in the AECG Group, you will help bring to life cutting-edge FPGA and ASIC solutions for a broad range of customers. As a member of the front-end design verification team, you will collaborate closely with architecture, IP design, physical design, firmware, and product engineering teams to deliver first-pass silicon success for next-generation PCIe and CXL-based IP solutions. THE PERSON: You are passionate about complex IP architectures, digital design, and advanced verification methodologies. You thrive in a collaborative environment, enjoy solving challenging technical problems, and have a proven ability to work effectively across global teams. You bring strong analytical skills, technical leadership, and a continuous learning mindset. The candidate will be highly accurate and detail-oriented, possessing good communication and problem-solving skills. KEY RESPONSIBLITIES: Architect and implement IP or subsystem-level UVM verification environments, including monitors, scoreboards, checkers, and reusable verification components. Collaborate with architects, hardware designers, and firmware teams to define and verify new PCIe, CXL, and high-speed connectivity features. Develop comprehensive verification plans that address feature interactions, hardware/software integration, performance requirements, and system-level use cases. Develop directed and constrained-random tests, execute regressions, and debug failures to ensure high functional coverage and design quality. Drive verification automation, methodology improvements, and adoption of AI-assisted tools to improve development efficiency and productivity. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: ASIC/IP verification experience using UVM methodology. Strong expertise in SystemVerilog, Verilog, object-oriented programming, and UVM-based verification environments. Experience working across the ASIC/FPGA development lifecycle from planning through tape-out. Exposure to performance verification, simulation optimization, acceleration technologies, HLS tools, or verification efficiency improvements. Technical leadership, mentoring experience, and strong communication skills within geographically distributed teams. Knowledge of computer architecture, system-level design concepts, and emerging AI-driven verification methodologies is a plus. You will collaborate closely with design, verification, physical design, CAD, product engineering, and test engineering teams to deliver robust, high-coverage, production-ready IP. Be part of a collaborative team delivering advanced IP used across SoCs. THE PERSON: The successful candidate brings analytical and problem-solving skills, attention to technical quality, and the ability to lead complex technical work with appropriate autonomy and cross-functional collaboration. The candidate should be able to contribute directly to technical implementation while providing technical leadership across architecture, methodology, RTL implementation, verification, and silicon debug. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Define and lead PHY-specific DFT/DFx architecture and methodology for high-speed SerDes, Memory PHY, and die-to-die interconnect IPs. Implement DFT/DFx features in RTL using Verilog/SystemVerilog. Develop and support DFT micro-architecture, including scan architecture, test modes, clocking, reset, isolation, bypass, and observability features. Support JTAG/IJTAG, ICL/PDL, scan compression, at-speed scan, and hierarchical DFT implementation. Support Siemens Tessent-based or equivalent industry-standard DFT flows for ATPG, pattern generation, pattern validation, and debug. Support scan stitching, scan-readiness checks, test coverage analysis, and DFT rule/debug closure. Develop and maintain DFT timing constraints, test-mode constraints, and integration guidelines compatible with front-end and physical design flows. Perform gate-level simulation and debug using tools such as Synopsys VCS and Verdi or comparable tools. Drive SpyGlass or equivalent lint/DFT-readiness analysis to identify scan, controllability, observability, and test coverage gaps. Plan, implement, and verify MBIST-related features for embedded memories. Support ATPG pattern generation, simulation, debug, and delivery to test engineering. Partner with Test Engineering and Product Engineering on silicon bring-up, tester pattern debug, diagnosis, and yield-learning activities. Develop efficient and reusable DFx flows, scripts, checkers, and methodologies for IP-level and SoC-level integration. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Relevant industry experience in DFT, DFx, RTL design, semiconductor IP development, or SoC test methodology. Level will be determined based on demonstrated technical scope, relevant experience, and role-related interview criteria. Understanding of DFT architecture and micro-architectures, including scan, compression, test clocks, test resets, lock-up latches, clock gates, scan anchors, and test access mechanisms. Hands-on experience with Siemens Tessent DFT flows, such as Tessent Shell, Tessent Scan, Tessent ATPG, Tessent TestKompress, Tessent MemoryBIST, IJTAG, ICL/PDL, and/or Streaming Scan Network/SSN, or experience with comparable industry-standard DFT tools and methodologies. Experience developing or supporting hierarchical DFT flows for complex SoCs or reusable IPs. Hands-on RTL coding experience in Verilog and/or SystemVerilog. Experience with industry-standard ATPG, scan insertion, and DFT implementation tools. Familiarity with JTAG, IJTAG, ICL/PDL, scan compression, at-speed scan, and hierarchical DFT concepts. Experience with gate-level simulation, debug, and waveform analysis using tools such as Synopsys VCS and Verdi or comparable technologies. Experience analyzing DFT readiness, lint, controllability, observability, and test coverage issues. Understanding of MBIST planning, implementation, verification, and debug. Understanding of low-power design concepts such as power gating, multi-voltage domains, multi-Vt usage, isolation, retention, and voltage scaling. Understanding of high-performance and low-power digital design fundamentals. Knowledge of common fault models, including stuck-at, transition, path delay, gate-exhaustive, IDDQ, and cell-aware fault models. Demonstrated ability to investigate and resolve issues across RTL, gate-level netlists, constraints, patterns, and silicon behavior. Ability to communicate technical information effectively and collaborate across design, verification, CAD, physical design, and test engineering teams. Experience with comparable tools, methodologies, and technically relevant environments may also be considered. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career. THE ROLE: AMD is seeking a Fellow Software Development Engineer to architect and develop features in the tensile-lite assembly code generator for General Matrix Multiplication (GEMM) and GEMM + X (including attention). GEMM performance is one of the most critical levers for AI workload efficiency and this role sits at the center of AMD's effort to deliver best-in-class matrix-multiply performance across current and next-generation hardware. You will own the deep, hardware-aware optimization work that turns AMD's GPU architecture into delivered performance: understanding the hardware specification at the instruction and pipeline level, partnering directly with hardware architects to influence future designs, and innovating algorithms to extract maximum throughput. THE PERSON: This role is a strong fit for an engineer who wants to work at the intersection of GPU microarchitecture, low-level code generation, and applied AI performance — someone equally comfortable reading a hardware spec, writing hand-tuned assembly, and explaining a performance tradeoff to a customer or an architect. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Analyze AMD GPU hardware specifications in depth and work closely with hardware architects to align kernel design with current silicon capabilities and to influence requirements for future generations. Develop support for new ISA and HW/SW optimization features in the code-generator Innovate and implement new algorithms for implementing GEMM and GEMM + X Profile and root-cause GEMM performance bottlenecks across the stack Partner with customers and internal stakeholders to understand real-world workload requirements, reproduce performance issues, and deliver targeted performance PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Strong command of GPU computer architecture: compute units, register files, cache/LDS hierarchies, memory bandwidth, matrix cores/WMMA-style instructions, and instruction scheduling/latency hiding. Deep expertise in GEMM algorithms and their mapping onto GPU hardware (tiling, blocking, register/LDS allocation, wave scheduling, memory hierarchy utilization). Strong software engineering fundamentals with a track record of building production-quality, high-performance software. Demonstrated experience optimizing GPU compute kernels, ideally GEMM and attention Proficiency in C++ and assembly-level GPU programming; working knowledge of Python for tooling/automation. Solid understanding of parallel computing, memory hierarchies, and hardware-software performance tradeoffs. Clear written and verbal communication skills; ability to work effectively with hardware architects, customers, and cross-functional engineering teams. Direct experience with any GPU compiler backend Experience with AMD GPU architectures (CDNA/RDNA) or comparable competitive architectures (NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell, etc.) Contributions to industry standards, publications, or patents related to GPU compute or matrix-multiply optimization PREFERRED ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: BS/MS/PHD in CS/CE or related field with deep relevant experience LOCATION: San Jose, CA #LI-G11 Benefits offered are described: AMD benefits at a glance. amd-89874.text: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology can change lives for the better. It can heal us, entertain us, and make us more connected, productive, and understanding of the world around us. And we’re looking for talent who feel the same: people who want to leave the planet better than they found it, those who don’t shy away from humanity’s challenges but are determined to help solve them. AMD is powering the next generation of supercomputing, high-performance computing, cloud, and AI. Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or creating go-to-market plans, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. THE ROLE: We are building next-generation systems software for AMD GPUs with Rust as a core technical direction. The work spans compilers, runtimes, low-level GPU software, firmware, developer tooling, and methods for improving the safety and correctness of complex hardware-software systems. Rust is not incidental to this role. You will help establish how Rust is used in performance-sensitive and high-trust parts of the GPU stack, including the compiler and tooling support, system interfaces, engineering practices, and validation methods required for production deployment. You will have the opportunity to influence both near-term implementations and the longer-term architecture for using Rust across current and future AMD platforms. THE PERSON: This role is for a deeply technical compiler and systems generalist who enjoys working across abstraction layers. You may move between Rust source semantics, rustc internals, intermediate representations, MLIR and LLVM, target-specific code generation, object formats, runtimes, GPU ISA, firmware, and hardware interfaces. You should have strong judgment about correctness boundaries. Memory safety is important, but production correctness also depends on concurrency, ordering, ABI compatibility, device behavior, compiler transformations, and the assumptions between software and hardware. You will help make those assumptions explicit and build evidence that the resulting systems behave as intended. The ideal candidate has deep expertise in at least one part of this stack and the ability to become productive in unfamiliar areas. Experience with every technology listed below is not expected. A research background is not required, although the ability to read technical work, form testable hypotheses, and turn promising ideas into reliable implementations is valuable. The work sits at the intersection of Rust systems programming, production compiler infrastructure, GPU architecture, firmware, program analysis, and formal methods. Hardware-software co-design experience is highly valuable, especially when compiler, runtime, firmware, or ISA choices must evolve together. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead the design and implementation of production-quality Rust components for low-level and performance-sensitive GPU systems. Help make Rust a first-class engineering language across relevant parts of the GPU software stack, including toolchain integration, libraries, coding standards, diagnostics, testing, and deployment practices. Design and implement compiler pipelines involving rustc, MIR, target-neutral intermediate representations, MLIR dialects and transformations, LLVM IR, and AMDGPU code generation. Build analyses, transformations, legalization passes, and target-specific lowering for GPU execution models, memory spaces, synchronization, capabilities, and specialized hardware operations. Define typed and auditable interfaces across compiler, host runtime, device code, firmware, and hardware boundaries. Work on ABI definition and validation, argument layout, calling conventions, linker and loader behavior, ELF and code-object metadata, and source-to-binary identity. Develop or improve bare-metal and no std Rust components where explicit state, bounded behavior, fail-closed handling, and predictable hardware effects are required. Use testing, fuzzing, property-based testing, differential execution, executable models, and hardware validation to find semantic gaps and prevent regressions. Apply program analysis or formal methods where they provide meaningful assurance, including source-level invariants, state-machine properties, refinement obligations, and clearly documented trusted boundaries. Distinguish precisely among type-system guarantees, source-level proofs, compiler evidence, binary validation, simulator results, and behavior observed on hardware. Partner with compiler, runtime, firmware, architecture, validation, security, and performance teams to solve problems that cross organizational and technical boundaries. Write design documents, lead technical reviews, mentor engineers, and explain complex language, compiler, and hardware behavior clearly. Evaluate emerging compiler and verification technologies and integrate them when they improve the safety, performance, maintainability, or development velocity of production systems. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Strong production Rust experience, including ownership and borrowing, lifetimes, traits and generics, error handling, concurrency, FFI, and the careful design of safe abstractions over unsafe operations. Experience with low-level or constrained Rust, including no std, embedded systems, firmware, custom targets, allocators, volatile access, interrupt handling, or architecture-specific code. Strong C or C++ systems programming skills and the ability to work across mixed-language codebases. Experience with rustc internals, MIR, custom codegen backends, procedural macros, compiler plugins, or other Rust toolchain infrastructure. Experience with LLVM, MLIR, GCC, or another production compiler framework. Experience designing intermediate representations, dialects, analyses, optimization passes, legalization, instruction selection, scheduling, or target-specific code generation. Understanding of compiler correctness issues such as undefined behavior, aliasing, provenance, layout, calling conventions, memory models, and source-to-target semantic preservation. Ability to read and reason about low-level assembly, ISA encodings, compiler output, and machine-level execution. Experience with linkers, loaders, ELF or other object formats, code-object metadata, DWARF, LLVM MC, disassembly, post-link analysis, or binary rewriting. Understanding of GPU execution models, including waves or warps, SIMD/SIMT execution, address spaces, registers, local or shared memory, caches, synchronization, atomics, barriers, and asynchronous operations. AMDGPU, GCN, RDNA, CDNA, ROCm, HIP, HSA, or AMDGPU LLVM backend experience. Experience with GPU runtimes, drivers, firmware, embedded processors, device initialization, command processing, queueing, or hardware control paths. Experience building secure or high-assurance systems that process untrusted inputs or operate across privilege, memory-isolation, or hardware trust boundaries. Experience with program analysis, abstract interpretation, symbolic execution, model checking, SMT solvers, or formal verification tools such as Verus, Lean, Coq, Isabelle, Dafny, or TLA+. Experience writing executable specifications, proving state-machine invariants, or validating refinement between source, IR, binaries, simulators, RTL, and hardware. Strong validation instincts, including adversarial testing, differential testing, property-based testing, fuzzing, reproducible evidence, and careful treatment of assumptions and counterexamples. Hardware-software co-design experience for ISA features, compiler-visible architecture, memory systems, synchronization, security mechanisms, or specialized compute pipelines. Technical leadership experience: setting direction, resolving ambiguous cross-layer problems, influencing partner teams, mentoring engineers, and communicating tradeoffs clearly. PREFERRED ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience. Research publications and advanced degrees are welcome but are not required. LOCATION: San Jose, CA #LI-DNI This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. You may move between Rust source semantics, rustc internals, intermediate representations, MLIR and LLVM, target-specific code generation, object formats, runtimes, GPU ISA, firmware, and hardware interfaces. You should have strong judgment about correctness boundaries. Memory safety is important, but production correctness also depends on concurrency, ordering, ABI compatibility, device behavior, compiler transformations, and the assumptions between software and hardware. You will help make those assumptions explicit and build evidence that the resulting systems behave as intended. The ideal candidate has deep expertise in at least one part of this stack and the ability to become productive in unfamiliar areas. Experience with every technology listed below is not expected. A research background is not required, although the ability to read technical work, form testable hypotheses, and turn promising ideas into reliable implementations is valuable. The work sits at the intersection of Rust systems programming, production compiler infrastructure, GPU architecture, firmware, program analysis, and formal methods. Hardware-software co-design experience is highly valuable, especially when compiler, runtime, firmware, or ISA choices must evolve together. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead the design and implementation of production-quality Rust components for low-level and performance-sensitive GPU systems. Help make Rust a first-class engineering language across relevant parts of the GPU software stack, including toolchain integration, libraries, coding standards, diagnostics, testing, and deployment practices. Design and implement compiler pipelines involving rustc, MIR, target-neutral intermediate representations, MLIR dialects and transformations, LLVM IR, and AMDGPU code generation. Build analyses, transformations, legalization passes, and target-specific lowering for GPU execution models, memory spaces, synchronization, capabilities, and specialized hardware operations. Define typed and auditable interfaces across compiler, host runtime, device code, firmware, and hardware boundaries. Work on ABI definition and validation, argument layout, calling conventions, linker and loader behavior, ELF and code-object metadata, and source-to-binary identity. Develop or improve bare-metal and `no_std` Rust components where explicit state, bounded behavior, fail-closed handling, and predictable hardware effects are required. Use testing, fuzzing, property-based testing, differential execution, executable models, and hardware validation to find semantic gaps and prevent regressions. Apply program analysis or formal methods where they provide meaningful assurance, including source-level invariants, state-machine properties, refinement obligations, and clearly documented trusted boundaries. Distinguish precisely among type-system guarantees, source-level proofs, compiler evidence, binary validation, simulator results, and behavior observed on hardware. Partner with compiler, runtime, firmware, architecture, validation, security, and performance teams to solve problems that cross organizational and technical boundaries. Write design documents, lead technical reviews, mentor engineers, and explain complex language, compiler, and hardware behavior clearly. Evaluate emerging compiler and verification technologies and integrate them when they improve the safety, performance, maintainability, or development velocity of production systems. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Strong production Rust experience, including ownership and borrowing, lifetimes, traits and generics, error handling, concurrency, FFI, and the careful design of safe abstractions over unsafe operations. Experience with low-level or constrained Rust, including `no_std`, embedded systems, firmware, custom targets, allocators, volatile access, interrupt handling, or architecture-specific code. Strong C or C++ systems programming skills and the ability to work across mixed-language codebases. Experience with rustc internals, MIR, custom codegen backends, procedural macros, compiler plugins, or other Rust toolchain infrastructure. Experience with LLVM, MLIR, GCC, or another production compiler framework. Experience designing intermediate representations, dialects, analyses, optimization passes, legalization, instruction selection, scheduling, or target-specific code generation. Understanding of compiler correctness issues such as undefined behavior, aliasing, provenance, layout, calling conventions, memory models, and source-to-target semantic preservation. Ability to read and reason about low-level assembly, ISA encodings, compiler output, and machine-level execution. Experience with linkers, loaders, ELF or other object formats, code-object metadata, DWARF, LLVM MC, disassembly, post-link analysis, or binary rewriting. Understanding of GPU execution models, including waves or warps, SIMD/SIMT execution, address spaces, registers, local or shared memory, caches, synchronization, atomics, barriers, and asynchronous operations. AMDGPU, GCN, RDNA, CDNA, ROCm, HIP, HSA, or AMDGPU LLVM backend experience. Experience with GPU runtimes, drivers, firmware, embedded processors, device initialization, command processing, queueing, or hardware control paths. Experience building secure or high-assurance systems that process untrusted inputs or operate across privilege, memory-isolation, or hardware trust boundaries. Experience with program analysis, abstract interpretation, symbolic execution, model checking, SMT solvers, or formal verification tools such as Verus, Lean, Coq, Isabelle, Dafny, or TLA+. Experience writing executable specifications, proving state-machine invariants, or validating refinement between source, IR, binaries, simulators, RTL, and hardware. Strong validation instincts, including adversarial testing, differential testing, property-based testing, fuzzing, reproducible evidence, and careful treatment of assumptions and counterexamples. Hardware-software co-design experience for ISA features, compiler-visible architecture, memory systems, synchronization, security mechanisms, or specialized compute pipelines. Technical leadership experience: setting direction, resolving ambiguous cross-layer problems, influencing partner teams, mentoring engineers, and communicating tradeoffs clearly. PREFERRED ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS: Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience. You will collaborate with architects, operations teams, researchers, network engineers, cloud partners, and technology vendors to bring new capabilities into production. You approach troubleshooting using data and systematic analysis and look for opportunities to simplify operations through automation. You can work effectively both independently and collaboratively, communicate technical information clearly, and partner with colleagues across functions, regions, and time zones. You are comfortable seeking input when decisions affect broader platform architecture or other teams. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Deploy, configure, and maintain Linux-based CPU and GPU clusters following established architecture and security standards. Administer Slurm and Kubernetes environments, including scheduling, resource allocation, access controls, and workload troubleshooting. Support distributed AI training and inference platforms by managing software environments, containers, and workload deployments. Automate infrastructure provisioning, configuration, and lifecycle management using infrastructure as code, configuration management, and scripting. Validate hardware, BIOS, firmware, GPU drivers, and runtime compatibility and support upgrades through testing, rollback planning, and user communication. Configure and troubleshoot host networking for HPC and GPU workloads, including high-speed NICs, RDMA interfaces, IP addressing, VLANs, MTU settings, and routing. Partner with network engineering teams to deploy and validate RoCEv2 or InfiniBand fabrics, including connectivity, congestion management, and end-to-end RDMA performance. Troubleshoot issues across compute, GPU, networking, storage, virtualization, and container environments. Conduct cluster acceptance testing and workload benchmarking to identify bottlenecks and improve performance, utilization, and reliability. Implement monitoring, dashboards, and alerts and contribute to incident resolution, root-cause analysis, and preventive improvements. Apply security updates and support vulnerability remediation in partnership with security and operations teams. Create and maintain technical documentation, operating procedures, and deployment runbooks. Collaborate with infrastructure partners, cloud providers, and hardware vendors to deliver projects and resolve technical issues. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE: Candidates are not expected to have experience with every technology listed below. Relevant skills may be developed through professional experience, education, training, or other technical pathways. Experience supporting Linux systems, HPC infrastructure, cloud platforms, GPU infrastructure, or distributed computing environments. Experience deploying, configuring, supporting, or operating HPC or GPU clusters. Linux administration and troubleshooting experience across operating systems, networking, storage, and system performance. Experience with Slurm, Kubernetes, or comparable workload scheduling and orchestration platforms. Experience supporting GPU drivers, containerized GPU workloads, or accelerator software stacks. Familiarity with AMD Instinct GPUs, ROCm, RCCL, or comparable technologies is beneficial. Familiarity with distributed computing concepts such as MPI, collective communication, and multi-node training. Experience working with high-speed Ethernet, InfiniBand, or comparable cluster networking technologies. Familiarity with RDMA and RoCEv2 concepts, including queue pairs, priority flow control (PFC), explicit congestion notification (ECN), and their relationship to fabric performance. Familiarity with leaf-spine topologies, fabric oversubscription, ECMP, and the impact of network latency, bandwidth, and congestion on distributed workloads. Experience troubleshooting or supporting high-speed cluster interconnects such as RoCEv2 or InfiniBand. Familiarity with Kubernetes networking technologies for GPU workloads, including CNI plugins, SR-IOV, or RDMA device plugins, is beneficial. Experience with shared or parallel storage technologies such as NFS, Lustre, BeeGFS, IBM Storage Scale, Weka, or comparable technologies. Experience using Python, Bash, or comparable scripting languages for infrastructure automation. Familiarity with configuration management and infrastructure-as-code technologies such as Ansible, SaltStack, Terraform, or comparable tools. Experience with Git-based workflows and monitoring or observability technologies such as Prometheus, Grafana, or comparable platforms. Experience with cloud infrastructure such as OCI, Microsoft Azure, AWS, specialized GPU cloud providers, or comparable environments. Familiarity with virtualization technologies such as KVM is beneficial. Familiarity with AI frameworks and inference technologies such as PyTorch, vLLM, SGLang, or comparable technologies is beneficial.
